entries.title: Testosterone Cypionate
entries.subtitle: Test C, TC
entries.text:
Testosterone Cypionate (Test C, TC) — Androgens / TRT

The most prescribed TRT compound in North America. Half-life ~8 days allows once or twice-weekly dosing. As the primary male androgen it supports muscle synthesis, bone density, red blood cell production, libido, and mood. Endocrinology research (2022-2026) confirms physiological TRT at 400-900 ng/dL significantly improves quality of life and body composition with an acceptable safety profile when monitored properly.

Reported benefits:
• Increases lean muscle and strength
• Improves libido and sexual function
• Enhances mood, clarity, and energy
• Improves bone mineral density
• Supports red blood cell production
• Gold standard — extensively studied

Risks and trade-offs:
• Suppresses natural testosterone (HPTA)
• Can elevate E2 — gynecomastia and water retention
• May raise hematocrit — polycythemia risk
• Testicular atrophy with long-term use
• Potential hair loss in susceptible individuals
• Requires bloodwork every 3-6 months

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• TRT / Starting: 100-150mg/week — Once or twice weekly IM/SubQ (Ongoing / indefinite)
• Optimization: 150-200mg/week — Twice weekly preferred (Ongoing with lab monitoring)
• Performance: 300-500mg/week — Twice weekly (12-16 weeks + PCT)

Progression: Start at 100mg/week. Get labs at 6-8 weeks. Titrate based on Total T, Free T, and E2. Optimize for symptoms and labs in range — avoid chasing high numbers.

Common protocols:
• TRT / Optimization: Test Cyp 100-150mg/wk, HCG 250IU 2x/wk (fertility), Anastrozole 0.25mg E3D only if E2 elevated on labs
• Body Recomposition: Test Cyp 200mg/wk, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin 200mcg 2x/day, BPC-157 250mcg/day
• Performance: Test Cyp 400mg/wk, HCG 250IU 2x/wk, Anastrozole per labs

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, E2 (sensitive assay), SHBG, Hematocrit, CBC, PSA, Lipids, CMP. Every 6-8 weeks adjusting; every 3-6 months stable.

Regulatory status: Off-label dosing above TRT levels. TRT itself requires prescription.

entries.title: Testosterone Enanthate
entries.subtitle: Test E, TE
entries.text:
Testosterone Enanthate (Test E, TE) — Androgens / TRT

Nearly identical to Cypionate with a half-life of ~7 days. More common in Europe. Clinically interchangeable with Cypionate in all protocols. Slightly different carrier oil may affect local tolerability.

Reported benefits:
• Equivalent efficacy to Cypionate
• Flexible dosing schedule
• Widely available globally
• Identical evidence base

Risks and trade-offs:
• Same E2/hematocrit risks as Cypionate
• HPTA suppression
• Requires injection technique

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• TRT: 100-150mg/week — Once or twice weekly (Ongoing)
• Performance: 300-500mg/week — Twice weekly (12-16 weeks + PCT)

Progression: Same titration as Cypionate. Clinically interchangeable for all protocols.

Common protocols:
• All goals: Protocols identical to Testosterone Cypionate

Monitoring: Same panel as Testosterone Cypionate.

Regulatory status: Off-label dosing above TRT levels. TRT itself requires prescription.

entries.title: Progesterone
entries.subtitle: Prometrium, Utrogestan
entries.text:
Progesterone (Prometrium, Utrogestan) — Androgens / TRT

Endogenous progestogen critical for female reproductive health, pregnancy, and neuroprotection. Beyond its reproductive role, progesterone acts as a neurosteroid (via allopregnanolone metabolite) improving sleep, reducing anxiety, and protecting brain tissue. Used in BHRT, sleep optimization, and as a DHT modulator in men.

Reported benefits:
• Neuroprotective via allopregnanolone
• Improves sleep quality significantly
• Balances estrogen in female BHRT
• Anti-anxiety via GABA potentiation
• Reduces DHT conversion in men (modest)
• FDA-approved oral and vaginal formulations

Risks and trade-offs:
• Sedating — must be used at night for most
• Can cause bloating and breast tenderness
• Synthetic progestins have different effects — bioidentical preferred
• Weight gain in some users
• Progesterone creams have variable absorption

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Female BHRT: 100–200mg — Oral at bedtime or vaginal (Ongoing, cyclically or continuously)
• Sleep Optimization: 100–200mg — Oral at bedtime (Ongoing)
• Men (adjunct): 10–20mg — Topical cream, nightly (Assess every 3 months)

Progression: Women: 100mg orally at bedtime for sleep and neuroprotection. 200mg cyclically for BHRT. Men: 10–20mg topical only — excess can cause sedation and progesterone accumulation.

Common protocols:
• Female BHRT: Progesterone 100–200mg at bedtime, Estradiol patch or cream, DHEA 10–25mg/day
• Sleep Stack (men/women): Progesterone 100mg at bedtime, Magnesium glycinate 400mg, Glycine 3g

entries.title: BPC-157
entries.subtitle: Body Protection Compound 157
entries.text:
BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound 157) — Peptides

Synthetic pentadecapeptide derived from human gastric juice. Demonstrates remarkable healing across tendons, ligaments, muscle, gut, and brain in animal studies. Mechanisms include GH receptor upregulation, angiogenesis, and dopaminergic modulation. Research through 2026 shows particular efficacy for gut healing and tendon repair. No serious adverse events in current literature.

Reported benefits:
• Accelerates tendon and ligament healing
• Reduces gut inflammation (IBD, leaky gut)
• Systemic anti-inflammatory effects
• Neuroprotective in animal models
• Excellent safety profile to date
• Accelerates wound healing and recovery

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited human RCT data — primarily animal evidence
• Long-term safety not yet established
• Quality control varies by source
• Not FDA approved
• Mechanism not fully characterized in humans

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 200-250mcg/day — Once daily SubQ near injury or orally (4-6 weeks)
• Therapeutic: 250-500mcg/day — Twice daily AM and PM (4-12 weeks)
• Gut Protocol: 250mcg orally — Twice daily fasted (4-8 weeks)

Progression: Start at 200mcg once daily. Assess at 2 weeks. Increase to 250-500mcg twice daily for active injury. Oral for gut; SubQ near injury site for musculoskeletal.

Common protocols:
• Injury Recovery: BPC-157 500mcg/day SubQ, TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week, Testosterone TRT dose
• Gut Health: BPC-157 250mcg orally 2x/day fasted

Monitoring: No specific labs required. Monitor injection site. Liver enzymes if long-term.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label.

entries.title: TB-500
entries.subtitle: Thymosin Beta-4
entries.text:
TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4) — Peptides

Synthetic fragment of Thymosin Beta-4 present in virtually all cells. Critical for cell building and repair via actin upregulation. Research shows efficacy in cardiac repair, wound healing, and musculoskeletal recovery. Systemic acting — complements BPC-157 synergistically.

Reported benefits:
• Systemic healing throughout the body
• Promotes muscle fiber repair
• Reduces scar tissue
• Cardiac protective in animal models
• Strong synergy with BPC-157
• Anti-inflammatory

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited human trial data
• Some cancer concern in animal studies (preliminary)
• Quality sourcing critical
• Not approved for human use
• Relatively expensive

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Loading: 2-2.5mg twice weekly — SubQ or IM (4-6 week loading phase)
• Maintenance: 2-2.5mg once weekly — SubQ (Ongoing as needed)

Progression: Load 2.5mg 2x/week for 4-6 weeks. Transition to 2.5mg/week maintenance. Cycle off for equal time spent on.

Common protocols:
• Injury Recovery: TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week, BPC-157 500mcg/day, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: No specific labs. General health panel annually.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label.

entries.title: CJC-1295
entries.subtitle: Mod GRF 1-29 (without DAC)
entries.text:
CJC-1295 (Mod GRF 1-29 (without DAC)) — Peptides

GHRH analogue stimulating pituitary GH release. Without DAC (preferred): 30-minute half-life for pulsatile dosing. Clinical research shows improvements in IGF-1, body composition, and sleep quality. Gold standard pairing with Ipamorelin.

Reported benefits:
• Increases GH and IGF-1 physiologically
• Improves body composition
• Enhances sleep quality
• More cost-effective than HGH
• Pulsatile release mimics natural pattern
• Synergistic with Ipamorelin

Risks and trade-offs:
• Water retention possible at higher doses
• Temporary bloating
• Carpal tunnel at very high doses (rare)
• Requires refrigeration
• IGF-1 monitoring recommended
• Fasted state required

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 100mcg CJC + 100mcg Ipa — Once daily before bed SubQ fasted (3 months on / 1 month off)
• Optimized: 200mcg CJC + 200mcg Ipa — Twice daily fasted (AM + pre-bed) (3-6 months)

Progression: Always pair with Ipamorelin. Start once-daily bedtime dosing. Advance to twice daily after 4-6 weeks. Fasted state is critical.

Common protocols:
• Anti-aging / Recomp: CJC-1295 200mcg + Ipamorelin 200mcg 2x/day, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, BPC-157 if recovery is concurrent goal

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months. Fasting glucose.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label.

entries.title: Ipamorelin
entries.subtitle: Ipa, Selective GHRP
entries.text:
Ipamorelin (Ipa, Selective GHRP) — Peptides

Most selective GHRP available — stimulates GH release with minimal cortisol or prolactin impact unlike GHRP-2 or Hexarelin. Research shows significant GH pulse amplification, improved sleep architecture, and body composition benefits. The gold standard GHRP pairing with CJC-1295.

Reported benefits:
• Highly selective — minimal cortisol/prolactin impact
• Excellent safety profile
• Improves sleep depth and quality
• Synergistic with CJC-1295 (gold standard)
• No significant desensitization at standard doses
• Well-tolerated long-term

Risks and trade-offs:
• Short half-life requires precise timing
• Mild hunger stimulation
• Requires refrigeration
• Limited long-term human data
• IGF-1 monitoring recommended

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 100-150mcg — Once daily 30 min before bed fasted (3 months on / 1 month off)
• Optimized: 200-300mcg — Twice daily fasted AM and pre-bed (3-6 months)

Progression: Always pair with CJC-1295. Start once-daily at bedtime fasted. Fasted state important — GH release is blunted by insulin.

Common protocols:
• GH Optimization: Ipamorelin 200mcg + CJC-1295 200mcg 2x/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Sermorelin as alternative to CJC-1295

Monitoring: IGF-1 at baseline and every 3 months. Fasting glucose.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label.

entries.title: Pentadeca Arginate
entries.subtitle: PDA, PC-15
entries.text:
Pentadeca Arginate (PDA, PC-15) — Peptides

Pentadeca Arginate (PDA) is a newer synthetic peptide derived from BPC-157 with an arginine substitution that increases stability and bioavailability. Emerging research (2022-2026) suggests superior tissue regeneration and nitric oxide pathway modulation compared to standard BPC-157. It appears to have enhanced activity at the NO synthase pathway, making it particularly promising for vascular healing, wound repair, and inflammation resolution. Considered by some researchers as a next-generation evolution of BPC-157.

Reported benefits:
• Enhanced stability vs standard BPC-157
• Superior nitric oxide pathway modulation
• Promising vascular and wound healing activity
• May have faster onset than BPC-157
• Excellent preliminary safety profile
• Synergistic with TB-500

Risks and trade-offs:
• Even more limited human data than BPC-157
• Very new compound — long-term safety completely unknown
• Difficult to source with verified purity
• Higher cost than BPC-157
• Mechanism not fully characterized
• Research still in early stages

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 250mcg/day — SubQ once daily near target tissue (4-6 weeks)
• Therapeutic: 500mcg/day — SubQ twice daily (6-12 weeks)

Progression: Use identically to BPC-157 protocol. Some researchers alternate weeks between PDA and BPC-157. Can substitute 1:1 for BPC-157 in most protocols.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Injury Recovery: PDA 500mcg/day SubQ, TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week, Testosterone TRT dose, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pre-bed

Monitoring: No specific labs. Monitor injection sites. Liver enzymes if extended use.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label in most jurisdictions.

entries.title: LL-37
entries.subtitle: Cathelicidin, CAMP peptide
entries.text:
LL-37 (Cathelicidin, CAMP peptide) — Peptides

LL-37 is the only human cathelicidin — a naturally occurring antimicrobial peptide produced by immune cells and epithelial cells. It provides broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against bacteria, viruses, and fungi, and is a critical component of innate immunity. Beyond antimicrobial action, research shows significant wound healing, immune modulation, anti-biofilm properties, anti-cancer activity, and gut barrier restoration. Levels decline with chronic illness and Vitamin D deficiency — Vitamin D is required for endogenous LL-37 production.

Reported benefits:
• Broad-spectrum antimicrobial — bacteria, viruses, fungi
• Innate immune system enhancement
• Wound healing and tissue repair
• Anti-biofilm activity (critical for chronic infections)
• Anti-cancer properties in research
• Gut barrier restoration

Risks and trade-offs:
• Can cause injection site inflammation locally
• May exacerbate autoimmune conditions
• Limited human trial data for systemic use
• Topical vs systemic effects differ significantly
• Sourcing and purity critical
• Not FDA approved

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Immune and Antimicrobial: 100-200mcg — SubQ 2-3x weekly (4-6 weeks)
• Wound healing topical: Apply to wound — 1-2x daily (Until healed)

Progression: For systemic immune support use SubQ. For wound healing use topical. Ensure adequate Vitamin D — required for endogenous LL-37 production. Cycle on/off.

Common protocols:
• Immune Optimization: LL-37 100-200mcg 2x/week SubQ, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week, Vitamin D3 5000-10000IU/day, BPC-157 for gut barrier support

Monitoring: CBC (immune cells), Vitamin D levels (essential), CRP. Monitor injection sites for local reactions.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval for systemic peptide therapy use.

entries.title: AOD-9604
entries.subtitle: Anti-Obesity Drug 9604, HGH Frag 177-191, HGH Fragment 176-191
entries.text:
AOD-9604 (Anti-Obesity Drug 9604, HGH Frag 177-191, HGH Fragment 176-191) — Peptides

AOD-9604 is a modified fragment of human growth hormone (amino acids 177-191) developed specifically for fat loss without the insulin-desensitizing or IGF-1-elevating effects of full HGH. Research demonstrates it stimulates lipolysis and inhibits lipogenesis by mimicking the way natural HGH regulates fat metabolism. Completed Phase IIb clinical trials for obesity. Notably it does not bind GH receptors or stimulate IGF-1 — making it safer for long-term metabolic use with none of HGH's anabolic side effects.

Reported benefits:
• Stimulates fat oxidation without affecting IGF-1 or insulin
• No glucose metabolism disruption unlike full HGH
• Completed Phase IIb clinical trials — substantial human data
• May regenerate cartilage and repair bone
• Once daily dosing
• No anabolic effects — purely metabolic
• No effect on blood glucose or IGF-1
• Targeted fat mobilization
• Excellent safety profile
• Compatible with all other peptides
• Cost-effective for fat loss

Risks and trade-offs:
• Less potent for fat loss than full HGH
• Not FDA approved despite advanced trials
• Injection only for systemic effects
• Results modest without diet and exercise
• Sourcing quality critical
• Long-term safety beyond trial periods not established
• Limited human clinical data
• Subcutaneous injection required
• Not FDA approved
• Results modest without diet optimization
• Short half-life requires precise timing

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Fat loss and Metabolic: 300-500mcg — SubQ once daily fasted AM (3-6 months)
• Joint and Cartilage: 500mcg — SubQ daily or near affected joint (8-12 weeks)
• Fat Loss: 250–500mcg/day — SubQ injection, fasted AM (3–6 months)
• Recomposition: 500mcg/day — Split AM/PM, fasted (3–6 months)

Progression: Inject fasted in the morning — food blunts the lipolytic effect. Best combined with caloric deficit and exercise. Results are gradual — allow 2-3 months. No PCT required.

Common protocols:
• Fat Loss Stack: AOD-9604 500mcg fasted AM, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pre-bed, Testosterone TRT dose, Tirzepatide if GLP-1 desired
• Joint Recovery: AOD-9604 500mcg/day, BPC-157 500mcg/day, TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week
• Recomposition Stack: AOD-9604 500mcg AM fasted, CJC-1295 No DAC 100mcg, Ipamorelin 200mcg, Testosterone TRT dose
• Fat Loss: AOD-9604 300mcg 2x/day, Cardarine 10mg/day, Caloric deficit protocol

Monitoring: Body composition tracking, waist circumference. No specific bloodwork required. Fasting glucose baseline recommended.

Regulatory status: Phase IIb clinical trials completed. Not FDA approved. Regulatory gray area in most jurisdictions.

entries.title: HGH Fragment 176-191
entries.subtitle: HGH Frag, Fragment 176-191
entries.text:
HGH Fragment 176-191 (HGH Frag, Fragment 176-191) — Peptides

HGH Fragment 176-191 is the C-terminal fragment of human growth hormone containing the fat-burning region of the molecule. Research demonstrates it is 12.5 times more potent than HGH for fat burning while not affecting blood sugar or IGF-1 levels. It stimulates lipolysis in adipose tissue and inhibits lipogenesis. Particularly effective for stubborn fat regions. Can be injected near target fat areas for localized effect. Popular in cutting protocols alongside testosterone.

Reported benefits:
• 12.5x more potent than HGH for fat burning (research)
• No effect on insulin sensitivity or IGF-1
• Targets stubborn fat deposits
• No HPTA suppression — no PCT needed
• Short half-life allows flexible timing
• Can be used near stubborn fat areas for local effect

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited human clinical data
• Not FDA approved
• Very short half-life — multiple daily injections ideal
• Results modest without diet optimization
• Sourcing and purity verification important
• Does not build muscle — purely fat metabolism

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Fat loss: 500mcg — SubQ 1-2x daily fasted (8-12 weeks)
• Local and Spot: 250-500mcg — SubQ near target fat area (8 weeks)

Progression: Inject fasted — pre-workout and/or before bed. Carbohydrates significantly blunt lipolytic effect. Best in conjunction with caloric deficit. No PCT needed.

Common protocols:
• Cutting and Fat Loss: HGH Frag 176-191 500mcg 2x/day fasted, Testosterone TRT dose, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pre-bed, AOD-9604 can be alternated

Monitoring: Body composition tracking, waist circumference, fasting glucose (should be unaffected). IGF-1 should remain unchanged — if it rises the product may be mislabeled.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Legal gray area in most jurisdictions.

entries.title: Hexarelin
entries.subtitle: Examorelin, HEX
entries.text:
Hexarelin (Examorelin, HEX) — Peptides

Hexarelin is the most potent GHRP — it produces the largest acute GH pulse of any GHRP studied. It also has unique direct cardiac and hepatoprotective properties independent of GH release, via direct receptor binding in cardiac tissue. Research demonstrates cardioprotective effects including improved left ventricular function and protection against ischemia-reperfusion injury. However its potency means faster desensitization and stronger cortisol and prolactin elevation than Ipamorelin — making it unsuitable for daily chronic use.

Reported benefits:
• Most potent GHRP — largest GH pulse
• Direct cardioprotective effects independent of GH
• Hepatoprotective properties in research
• Unique direct cardiac receptor binding
• Useful for pulsatile GH strategies
• Strong synergy with GHRH analogues

Risks and trade-offs:
• Fastest desensitization of all GHRPs — limits chronic use
• Strongest cortisol and prolactin elevation of GHRPs
• Not suitable for daily long-term use
• Requires cycling to maintain effectiveness
• Water retention more pronounced
• Less selective than Ipamorelin

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Pulsatile and Cycling: 100-200mcg — SubQ 2-3x weekly (not daily) (2 weeks on / 1 week off)
• Cardiac protective: 100mcg — SubQ 2-3x weekly (8-12 weeks)

Progression: Do not use daily — rapid desensitization. Best used in 2-week on / 1-week off cycles. Pair with CJC-1295 for amplified GH pulse. Not for daily chronic use — use Ipamorelin instead for daily protocols.

Common protocols:
• GH Pulse and Cardiac: Hexarelin 100-200mcg 3x/week, CJC-1295 200mcg same injection timing, Testosterone TRT dose, Monitor prolactin

Monitoring: IGF-1, Prolactin (elevated with Hexarelin), Cortisol if symptomatic. Cardiac assessment if using for cardiac indications.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Studied in clinical settings for cardiac applications.

entries.title: GHRP-2
entries.subtitle: Pralmorelin, KP-102
entries.text:
GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin, KP-102) — Peptides

GHRP-2 is a synthetic ghrelin mimetic that stimulates GH release from the pituitary. More potent than GHRP-6 with less hunger stimulation, but less selective than Ipamorelin in that it still elevates cortisol and prolactin moderately. Has been studied in clinical trials for GH deficiency diagnosis. Research demonstrates effective GH pulse amplification, improved body composition, and sleep quality enhancement. Often considered a middle ground between Hexarelin potency and Ipamorelin selectivity.

Reported benefits:
• More potent GH release than GHRP-6
• Less hunger stimulation than GHRP-6
• Clinical trial data for GHD diagnosis
• Good body composition effects
• Synergistic with CJC-1295
• Established research profile

Risks and trade-offs:
• Moderate cortisol and prolactin elevation unlike Ipamorelin
• Some hunger stimulation
• Faster desensitization than Ipamorelin
• Requires cycling
• Not FDA approved
• Less selective than Ipamorelin

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard: 100-200mcg — SubQ 2-3x daily fasted (3 months on / 1 month off)
• With CJC-1295: 100mcg GHRP-2 + 100mcg CJC-1295 — SubQ 2x daily fasted (3 months)

Progression: Fasted state critical. Provides stronger GH pulses than Ipamorelin if that is the goal. Monitor prolactin if using long-term. Cycle to prevent desensitization.

Common protocols:
• GH Optimization: GHRP-2 100mcg + CJC-1295 100mcg 2x/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Consider Cabergoline if prolactin rises

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months, Prolactin, Cortisol if symptomatic, Fasting glucose.

Regulatory status: Research compound. Studied in clinical trials for GHD. Not FDA approved for general use.

entries.title: GHRP-6
entries.subtitle: Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-6
entries.text:
GHRP-6 (Growth Hormone Releasing Peptide-6) — Peptides

GHRP-6 was among the first synthetic GHRPs developed and remains well-studied. It produces robust GH pulses and is notable for its strong appetite-stimulating effect via ghrelin receptor activation — making it useful for those seeking to increase caloric intake during bulking or recovery from cachexia, but undesirable for those cutting. It elevates cortisol and prolactin more than Ipamorelin. Still used specifically for its appetite stimulation during mass-building phases.

Reported benefits:
• Strong GH pulse stimulation
• Significant appetite stimulation — useful for bulking and cachexia
• Extensive research history
• Inexpensive relative to newer GHRPs
• Synergistic with CJC-1295
• Best for mass-building phases where appetite is needed

Risks and trade-offs:
• Strong hunger side effect — problematic for cutting
• Most cortisol and prolactin elevation of common GHRPs
• Faster desensitization
• Not FDA approved
• Water retention
• Less selective than Ipamorelin

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Bulking and Mass: 100-200mcg — SubQ 2-3x daily fasted (3 months on / 1 off)
• With CJC-1295: 100mcg GHRP-6 + 100mcg CJC — SubQ 2-3x daily fasted (3 months)

Progression: Best used during caloric surplus where appetite enhancement is welcome. Avoid if cutting. Cycle to prevent desensitization.

Common protocols:
• Mass Building GH Stack: GHRP-6 200mcg + CJC-1295 200mcg 2-3x/day, Testosterone Cypionate 200-300mg/week, High protein diet to capitalize on GH and appetite effect

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months, Prolactin, Cortisol, Fasting glucose, Body weight.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Historical clinical research base.

entries.title: SS-31
entries.subtitle: Elamipretide, MTP-131, Bendavia
entries.text:
SS-31 (Elamipretide, MTP-131, Bendavia) — Peptides

SS-31 (Elamipretide) is a mitochondria-targeted peptide that selectively accumulates in the inner mitochondrial membrane where it binds cardiolipin — a critical phospholipid required for mitochondrial cristae structure and electron transport chain efficiency. Research demonstrates it restores mitochondrial function, reduces oxidative stress, improves ATP production, and protects against ischemia-reperfusion injury. Phase II clinical trials for heart failure and Barth syndrome. In longevity science it is considered one of the most direct interventions for age-related mitochondrial dysfunction.

Reported benefits:
• Direct mitochondrial membrane targeting — unique mechanism
• Restores electron transport chain efficiency
• Reduces mitochondrial oxidative stress
• Clinical trial data for cardiac and mitochondrial diseases
• Potential for age-related energy restoration
• Synergistic with MOTS-c and NMN
• Direct mitochondrial membrane targeting
• Reduces ROS at the source
• Clinical trial data in cardiac conditions
• Improves exercise capacity
• Synergistic with CoQ10 and NMN
• Novel mechanism of action

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very expensive
• Injection only — SubQ or IV
• Limited longevity-specific human dosing data
• Clinical trials ongoing — not FDA approved
• Complex mechanism — effects take weeks
• Sourcing with verified purity extremely important
• Limited availability
• Optimal longevity dosing not established
• Injectable
• Limited long-term human data

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Longevity and Mitochondrial: 5-10mg — SubQ 3-5x weekly (4-8 weeks on / 4 weeks off)
• Clinical trial dose: 4mg/kg IV in trials — Physician administered (Study protocol)
• Research Protocol: 1–3mg/day — SubQ injection (4–12 weeks)
• Performance: 3–5mg pre-training — SubQ injection (As needed)

Progression: For longevity use SubQ 5-10mg several times weekly. Best stacked with other mitochondrial support (NMN, MOTS-c). Expect gradual energy and recovery improvements over 4-8 weeks.

Common protocols:
• Mitochondrial and Longevity Stack: SS-31 5-10mg SubQ 4x/week, MOTS-c 5mg 3x/week, NMN 1000mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Epithalon pulse cycles
• Mitochondrial Support: SS-31 2mg/day SubQ, CoQ10 400mg/day, NMN 1g/day, PQQ 20mg/day
• Cardiac Support: SS-31 3mg/day SubQ, Omega-3 EPA/DHA 4g/day, CoQ10 400mg/day

Monitoring: Energy levels and exercise capacity self-assessment. VO2 max testing if available. No standard blood monitoring protocol established.

Regulatory status: Phase II clinical trials ongoing (Barth syndrome, heart failure). Not FDA approved. Research compound.

entries.title: Humanin
entries.subtitle: HN, Mitochondrial-derived peptide
entries.text:
Humanin (HN, Mitochondrial-derived peptide) — Peptides

Humanin is a 21-amino acid peptide encoded in the mitochondrial genome, discovered in 2001 in an Alzheimer's-resistant brain library. Humanin levels decline with age and correlate with longevity in centenarian studies. It protects across multiple aging pathways: neuroprotection, insulin sensitization, cardiovascular protection, and anti-apoptotic effects. Circulating Humanin predicts metabolic health and longevity outcomes and is one of the most consequential mitochondrial-derived peptides discovered in aging biology.

Reported benefits:
• Potent neuroprotection — Alzheimer's research origin
• Improves insulin sensitivity
• Cardiovascular protection
• Levels correlate with longevity in humans
• Anti-apoptotic effects across multiple tissues
• Mitochondrial health marker and therapeutic

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very early clinical stage
• Limited human dosing data
• Optimal administration route still being determined
• Expensive and difficult to source
• Complex biology — systemic effects vary
• Not FDA approved

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Research protocol: 2-4mg — SubQ 2-3x weekly (4-8 weeks)

Progression: Often used in combination with MOTS-c as a comprehensive mitochondrial peptide protocol. Expect subtle but meaningful effects on energy, cognition, and recovery over weeks of use.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Longevity and Neuro: Humanin 2-4mg SubQ 3x/week, MOTS-c 5mg 3x/week, SS-31 5mg 4x/week, Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, NMN 1000mg/day

Monitoring: Cognitive self-assessment, insulin sensitivity markers (fasting glucose, HbA1c), energy and recovery tracking.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Significant academic research base.

entries.title: Pinealon
entries.subtitle: EDR peptide, Glu-Asp-Arg
entries.text:
Pinealon (EDR peptide, Glu-Asp-Arg) — Peptides

Pinealon is a synthetic tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) developed by Vladimir Khavinson as a pineal gland cytoprotective peptide. Research demonstrates neuroprotective effects, cognitive enhancement, sleep architecture improvement, antioxidant activity, and anti-aging effects via regulation of neuronal gene expression. Studies show improved cognitive performance in aging models and protection of neuronal cells from hypoxia and oxidative stress. Part of Khavinson's validated series of short regulatory peptides alongside Epithalon, Thymalin, and Vilon.

Reported benefits:
• Neuroprotective — protects against hypoxia and oxidative stress
• Improves sleep quality and circadian rhythm regulation
• Cognitive enhancement in aging
• Part of validated Khavinson research series
• Antioxidant activity
• Pineal gland and melatonin system support

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily from Khavinson group — needs wider replication
• Limited Western clinical data
• Long-term human safety not fully established
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing from limited suppliers
• Effects are subtle and cumulative

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cognitive and Sleep: 5-10mg — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2-4x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use the same 10-day pulse cycle approach as Epithalon. Often used together with Epithalon in the Khavinson longevity stack. Best taken in the evening given pineal and sleep relevance.

Common protocols:
• Khavinson Longevity Stack: Epithalon 10mg/day x 10 days, Pinealon 10mg/day x 10 days (concurrent or sequential), Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Sleep quality assessment, cognitive self-evaluation, general health panel.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Approved for clinical use in Russia.

entries.title: Thymalin
entries.subtitle: Thymus peptide complex
entries.text:
Thymalin (Thymus peptide complex) — Peptides

Thymalin is a polypeptide complex from the thymus gland developed by Khavinson to restore thymic function and T-cell activity. The thymus involutes significantly after puberty, leading to declining T-cell production and immune senescence. In one landmark 15-year follow-up study, Thymalin treatment resulted in significantly reduced mortality in older adults compared to controls — among the most compelling long-term longevity data for any peptide intervention.

Reported benefits:
• 15-year mortality reduction data — among strongest longevity evidence
• Restores thymic function and T-cell production
• Reduces infection frequency and severity
• Immune system rejuvenation
• Part of validated Khavinson series
• Annual pulse cycling — convenient

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily from Russia — limited Western replication
• Polypeptide complex — harder to standardize
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing quality critical
• Most dramatic effects in older or immunocompromised individuals
• Subtle effects in young healthy individuals

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Immune and Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 1-2x per year (10-day pulse cycles annually)

Progression: Annual or biannual 10-day cycles. Often administered spring and fall alongside Epithalon and Pinealon as a comprehensive Khavinson protocol. Most relevant for individuals over 40.

Common protocols:
• Immune Longevity Stack: Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Epithalon 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week ongoing, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: CBC with differential (immune cell assessment), infection frequency tracking, inflammatory markers.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used clinically in Russia for decades.

entries.title: Vilon
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu, KE dipeptide
entries.text:
Vilon (Lys-Glu, KE dipeptide) — Peptides

Vilon is a synthetic dipeptide (Lysine-Glutamate) developed by Khavinson as a universal bioregulator. Research demonstrates it activates gene expression related to immune function and protein synthesis, promotes T-lymphocyte differentiation, and has antioxidant properties. Vilon appears to work at the genomic level — regulating chromatin structure and gene transcription in a tissue-nonspecific way, making it one of the most fundamental bioregulatory peptides. Studies show life extension in animal models and immune restoration in aging humans.

Reported benefits:
• Fundamental bioregulator — genomic level action
• Promotes T-lymphocyte differentiation
• Antioxidant properties
• Life extension in animal models
• Universal tissue application
• Part of Khavinson validated series

Risks and trade-offs:
• Extremely limited Western data
• Broad mechanism not fully characterized
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing extremely limited
• Effects subtle without comprehensive biomarker testing
• Research primarily in Russian literature

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Immune and Longevity: 1-2mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use as part of comprehensive Khavinson protocol alongside Epithalon and Thymalin.

Common protocols:
• Khavinson Complete Stack: Epithalon 10mg x 10 days, Thymalin 10mg x 10 days, Pinealon 10mg x 10 days, Vilon 2mg x 10 days, Cortagen 10mg x 10 days

Monitoring: CBC, immune function assessment, inflammatory markers, general health panel.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical research.

entries.title: Cortagen
entries.subtitle: Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, AEDP tetrapeptide
entries.text:
Cortagen (Ala-Glu-Asp-Pro, AEDP tetrapeptide) — Peptides

Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide from Khavinson's peptide series designed as a cardioprotective and vasculoprotective bioregulator. Research demonstrates it protects cardiac muscle, improves coronary circulation, reduces myocardial ischemia damage, and has antioxidant properties in cardiac tissue. Studies show heart rate variability improvement and cardiac function enhancement in aging individuals. As cardiovascular aging is central to overall longevity, Cortagen occupies an important niche in the longevity peptide toolkit.

Reported benefits:
• Cardioprotective — reduces ischemia-reperfusion damage
• Improves coronary circulation
• Heart rate variability improvement
• Antioxidant in cardiac tissue
• Part of Khavinson validated series
• Addresses cardiovascular aging directly

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily from Russian literature
• Limited Western validation
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing very limited
• Best effects in individuals with cardiovascular aging
• Subtle effects in young healthy individuals

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cardioprotective and Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Part of comprehensive Khavinson longevity protocol. Most relevant for individuals over 45. Use alongside Epithalon and SS-31 for comprehensive cardiovascular longevity support.

Common protocols:
• Cardiovascular Longevity: Cortagen 10mg x 10 days, Epithalon 10mg x 10 days, SS-31 5mg 4x/week, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Cardiac biomarkers (BNP if indicated), HRV monitoring, lipid panel, blood pressure.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Russian clinical research validated.

entries.title: Kisspeptin-10
entries.subtitle: Metastin, KP-10
entries.text:
Kisspeptin-10 (Metastin, KP-10) — Peptides

Kisspeptin-10 is the C-terminal 10-amino acid fragment of kisspeptin — the master regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. It acts directly on GnRH neurons, triggering LH and FSH release which then stimulates testosterone production. Research shows pulsatile Kisspeptin-10 administration can restore testosterone in hypogonadal men and may be superior to Clomid for certain secondary hypogonadism types. Additionally demonstrates pro-sexual effects and anti-metastatic properties (hence its original name Metastin). One of the most interesting peptides for natural HPTA restoration.

Reported benefits:
• Master HPG axis regulator — upstream of GnRH
• Restores testosterone via natural axis
• Superior to Clomid for some secondary hypogonadism types
• Pro-sexual and libido enhancing
• Anti-metastatic in certain cancers
• Pulsatile dosing mimics natural physiology

Risks and trade-offs:
• Pulsatile dosing is complex and critical — continuous dosing causes desensitization
• Limited clinical trial data outside fertility research
• Injection only
• Not FDA approved for testosterone restoration
• Mechanism complex — easy to misuse
• Continuous dosing SUPPRESSES the axis — timing is critical

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• HPG Axis Restoration: 1-2mg — SubQ pulsatile — 2-3x daily with 8+ hour gaps (4-8 weeks)
• Libido and Sexual: 1mg — SubQ 30-60 min before activity (As needed)

Progression: Pulsatile dosing is absolutely critical. Continuous infusion desensitizes kisspeptin receptors and suppresses the axis. Administer 2-3x daily with minimum 8-hour gaps between doses.

Common protocols:
• HPG Axis Restoration: Kisspeptin-10 1mg SubQ pulsatile 2-3x/day, HCG 250IU 2x/week (direct testicular support), Enclomiphene 25mg/day (complementary SERM)

Monitoring: Total T, LH, FSH, E2 every 4 weeks. LH surge 30-60 min post-injection confirms receptor response.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval for testosterone restoration. Used in fertility research.

entries.title: ARA-290
entries.subtitle: Cibinetide, Helix B peptide
entries.text:
ARA-290 (Cibinetide, Helix B peptide) — Peptides

ARA-290 (Cibinetide) is a synthetic peptide derived from the helix B surface of erythropoietin (EPO) — engineered to activate the innate repair receptor that drives EPO tissue-protective effects without the red blood cell stimulating effects of full EPO. Research demonstrates remarkable efficacy for neuropathic pain, small fiber neuropathy, and sarcoidosis-related symptoms. Phase II clinical trials show significant pain reduction in small fiber neuropathy. Also shows immune modulation and tissue repair effects.

Reported benefits:
• EPO tissue repair benefits without blood doping effects
• Phase II trial data for neuropathic pain
• Effective for small fiber neuropathy
• Anti-inflammatory via innate repair receptor
• Potential for diabetic neuropathy treatment
• Tissue repair and regeneration properties

Risks and trade-offs:
• Expensive and difficult to source
• Not FDA approved despite advanced trials
• Injection only
• Trials primarily focused on neuropathy — body composition data limited
• Long-term safety not fully established
• Complex receptor pharmacology

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Neuropathy and Pain: 4mg — SubQ daily (4-8 weeks)
• Anti-inflammatory and Repair: 2-4mg — SubQ 3-5x weekly (4-8 weeks)

Progression: For neuropathic pain use daily dosing per clinical trial protocol. For general repair and anti-inflammatory use 3-5x weekly. Allow 4 weeks for meaningful pain relief.

Common protocols:
• Neuropathy and Nerve Repair: ARA-290 4mg/day SubQ, BPC-157 500mcg/day, Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, Alpha-lipoic acid 600mg/day

Monitoring: Pain scales (VAS/NRS), nerve conduction studies if available, inflammatory markers (CRP), CBC.

Regulatory status: Phase II clinical trials completed for small fiber neuropathy. Orphan Drug Designation for sarcoidosis. Not FDA approved.

entries.title: Larazotide
entries.subtitle: AT-1001, INN-202
entries.text:
Larazotide (AT-1001, INN-202) — Peptides

Larazotide acetate is a tight junction regulator — specifically an antagonist of the zonulin pathway, which is the primary regulator of intestinal permeability (leaky gut). By blocking zonulin, Larazotide tightens the junctions between intestinal epithelial cells, reducing gut permeability. Phase IIb clinical trials for celiac disease showed significant symptom reduction even during gluten exposure. Research also ongoing for IBS and NASH. Unlike BPC-157 which heals gut tissue broadly, Larazotide works specifically on the tight junction mechanism — making them highly complementary.

Reported benefits:
• Phase IIb clinical trial data for celiac disease
• Specifically targets tight junctions — precise mechanism
• Reduces gut permeability and leaky gut
• Oral administration — no injection needed
• Complementary to BPC-157 (different mechanism)
• Anti-inflammatory via gut barrier restoration

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not FDA approved despite advanced trials
• Oral bioavailability variable
• Long-term effects beyond trial periods unknown
• Celiac-specific data — other conditions still being studied
• Sourcing limited
• May need dietary changes alongside for full effect

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Gut Permeability and Celiac: 0.5-1mg — Oral 3x daily before meals (12 weeks)

Progression: Take before meals for maximum effectiveness at blocking zonulin response. Combine with BPC-157 for comprehensive gut healing — Larazotide targets tight junctions while BPC-157 addresses broader tissue healing.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Gut Healing: Larazotide 0.5mg orally 3x/day before meals, BPC-157 250mcg orally 2x/day, KPV 500mcg orally 2x/day, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week

Monitoring: GI symptom tracking, zonulin levels if available via specialty labs, inflammatory markers.

Regulatory status: Phase IIb clinical trials completed. Not FDA approved. IND status in US.

entries.title: Semaglutide
entries.subtitle: Ozempic, Wegovy
entries.text:
Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) — GLP-1 / Metabolic

GLP-1 receptor agonist. STEP trials (2021): 15-17% average body weight reduction over 68 weeks. Mechanisms: central appetite suppression, delayed gastric emptying, improved insulin secretion. SELECT trial (2023): significant cardiovascular risk reduction independent of weight loss. One of the most consequential metabolic drugs developed.

Reported benefits:
• 15-17% average body weight reduction
• Cardiovascular risk reduction (SELECT trial 2023)
• Improved insulin sensitivity and glucose control
• Once-weekly dosing
• Reduces food cravings significantly
• Growing evidence for NASH and kidney disease

Risks and trade-offs:
• Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea during titration
• Muscle mass loss without resistance training
• Slow titration required — 4-week increments
• Pancreatitis risk (rare)
• Rebound weight gain upon discontinuation
• Expensive without insurance coverage

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 0.25mg/week — Weekly SubQ (4 weeks then titrate)
• Maintenance: 0.5-1.0mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing)
• Max (Wegovy): 2.4mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing)

Progression: Titrate by 0.25mg every 4 weeks. Pair with resistance training and minimum 1g protein/lb body weight.

Common protocols:
• Fat Loss / Recomp: Semaglutide 1-2mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose (muscle preservation), CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin (GH support), BPC-157 250mcg/day (gut comfort)

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, amylase if abdominal pain, weight monthly.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for T2 diabetes (Ozempic) and obesity (Wegovy). Off-label for general weight loss.

entries.title: Tirzepatide
entries.subtitle: Mounjaro, Zepbound
entries.text:
Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) — GLP-1 / Metabolic

Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist. SURMOUNT trials (2022-2023): 20-22% average body weight reduction — significantly exceeding semaglutide. Dual mechanism provides superior glucose control and appears better tolerated. Currently best-in-class for weight management.

Reported benefits:
• 20-22% body weight loss — best in class
• Dual GIP + GLP-1 mechanism — superior efficacy
• Better GI tolerability than semaglutide in many patients
• Superior metabolic syndrome improvement
• Weekly dosing
• Strong emerging cardiovascular data

Risks and trade-offs:
• All GLP-1 class side effects apply
• Muscle loss without resistance training
• Expensive without coverage
• Newer — less long-term data than semaglutide
• Same thyroid precautions as GLP-1 class

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 2.5mg/week — Weekly SubQ (4 weeks then titrate)
• Maintenance: 5-10mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing)
• Maximum: 15mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing)

Progression: Titrate by 2.5mg every 4 weeks. Most patients find efficacy at 10-15mg. Protein-forward diet and resistance training non-negotiable.

Common protocols:
• Fat Loss / Recomp: Tirzepatide 5-15mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose (critical for muscle), CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin

Monitoring: Same as Semaglutide. HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, weight monthly.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for T2 diabetes (Mounjaro) and obesity (Zepbound). Off-label for general weight loss.

entries.title: Sermorelin
entries.subtitle: GHRH(1-29)
entries.text:
Sermorelin (GHRH(1-29)) — GH Secretagogues

Synthetic analogue of the first 29 amino acids of endogenous GHRH. Stimulates pituitary GH production within natural negative feedback loops — safer than exogenous HGH. Clinical research supports improvements in body composition, sleep quality, and wellbeing. Most conservative and physiological GH-axis intervention available.

Reported benefits:
• Works within natural GH feedback axis
• Safer profile than exogenous HGH
• Significantly improves sleep quality
• Body composition improvements over 3-6 months
• Cost-effective relative to HGH
• No IGF-1 overstimulation risk

Risks and trade-offs:
• Less potent than CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin
• Requires daily dosing
• Short half-life
• Results slower than HGH
• Requires refrigeration and reconstitution

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard: 200-300mcg — Once daily before bed SubQ fasted (3-6 months on / 1 month off)
• With GHRP: Sermorelin 200mcg + Ipamorelin 200mcg — Once or twice daily fasted (3 months on / 1 off)

Progression: Start once-daily bedtime dosing. Add Ipamorelin for enhanced GH pulse. Monitor IGF-1 at 3 months.

Common protocols:
• Anti-aging / Longevity: Sermorelin 300mcg + Ipamorelin 300mcg pre-bed, Testosterone TRT dose, BPC-157 for systemic repair

Monitoring: IGF-1 at baseline and every 3 months. Fasting glucose.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval for general use. Used in anti-aging medicine.

entries.title: Tesamorelin
entries.subtitle: Egrifta, TH9507
entries.text:
Tesamorelin (Egrifta, TH9507) — Peptides

Tesamorelin is an FDA-approved synthetic GHRH analogue — one of the very few peptides with full FDA approval. Approved for HIV-associated lipodystrophy, clinical research shows 15-18% visceral fat reduction in trials, IGF-1 normalization, and metabolic improvement. Research beyond its approved indication shows promise for cognitive decline in older adults, NASH, and general body composition. Its FDA approval provides stronger safety and efficacy data than almost any other peptide in this class.

Reported benefits:
• FDA APPROVED — strongest evidence base among GHRH analogues
• 15-18% visceral fat reduction in clinical trials
• Improves IGF-1 levels and GH pulsatility
• Cognitive benefits in aging adults (emerging research)
• Liver fat reduction NASH research
• Established safety profile from clinical trials
• FDA-approved with human clinical data
• Reduces visceral adiposity significantly
• Improves lipid profiles
• Increases IGF-1 without exogenous HGH
• Once-daily dosing
• Well-studied safety profile

Risks and trade-offs:
• Expensive — approved drug pricing
• Approved only for HIV lipodystrophy — off-label for other uses
• Requires refrigeration
• Daily injection
• May cause fluid retention and joint pain at higher doses
• IGF-1 monitoring required
• Expensive compared to other GH peptides
• Can induce insulin resistance
• Requires physician prescription
• Not widely available
• Injection site reactions common

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• FDA Approved use: 2mg/day — SubQ daily (Ongoing with monitoring)
• Off-label body composition: 1-2mg/day — SubQ daily fasted AM or pre-bed (3-6 months)
• Standard: 1mg/day — SubQ injection, morning (3–6 months)
• Body Composition: 2mg/day — SubQ injection, morning fasted (3–6 months)

Progression: Standard protocol is 2mg/day SubQ. Monitor IGF-1 to maintain upper-normal range. Can be cycled 6 months on / 1-2 months off. One of the most validated GHRH analogues available.

Common protocols:
• GH Axis and Body Composition: Tesamorelin 2mg/day, Ipamorelin 200mcg pre-bed (synergistic), Testosterone TRT dose, Metformin 500mg if insulin sensitivity concern
• GH Optimization: Tesamorelin 1–2mg/day, Ipamorelin 200mcg 3x/day, Testosterone TRT dose
• Longevity Stack: Tesamorelin 1mg/day, GHK-Cu 1mg/day, NMN 500mg/day

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months (critical), fasting glucose, HbA1c, visceral fat assessment, lipid panel.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Off-label use for general body composition and cognitive health.

entries.title: MK-677 / Ibutamoren
entries.subtitle: Nutrobal
entries.text:
MK-677 / Ibutamoren (Nutrobal) — GH Secretagogues

Orally active, non-peptide ghrelin receptor agonist that potently stimulates GH and IGF-1 secretion. Mimics ghrelin to activate the GH secretagogue receptor. Once-daily oral dosing is its primary advantage over injectable GH peptides. Long half-life of 24+ hours provides sustained GH elevation with sleep-related pulse preservation.

Reported benefits:
• Oral administration — no injections
• Once daily dosing
• Increases both GH and IGF-1 significantly
• Improves sleep quality and REM
• Long half-life
• Relatively inexpensive

Risks and trade-offs:
• Significant appetite stimulation
• Water retention and bloating
• Elevated cortisol and prolactin
• Can raise blood glucose — insulin resistance risk
• Numbness and tingling (carpal tunnel like)
• Not FDA approved

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 10mg/day — Oral at bedtime (4–8 weeks)
• Standard: 15–25mg/day — Oral at bedtime (3–6 months, then break)

Progression: Start at 10mg at bedtime. Assess appetite and sleep changes at 2 weeks. Increase to 15–25mg if tolerated. Monitor IGF-1 at 6 weeks — target 200–350 ng/mL. Take 4–6 month breaks.

Common protocols:
• GH Optimization: MK-677 25mg at bedtime, CJC-1295 No DAC 100mcg 3x/day, Testosterone TRT dose
• Lean Muscle: MK-677 15mg at bedtime, Enclomiphene or TRT, High protein diet 2g/kg

entries.title: Anastrozole
entries.subtitle: Arimidex
entries.text:
Anastrozole (Arimidex) — Ancillaries

Third-generation non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor blocking testosterone-to-estradiol conversion. Essential when estrogen rises excessively on TRT. Critical warning: over-suppression of E2 is a major risk — estrogen is vital for bone density, libido, joint health, and cardiovascular protection in men. Use only when bloodwork confirms elevated E2.

Reported benefits:
• Effectively reduces estradiol
• Reduces gynecomastia risk
• Reduces water retention from elevated T
• Well-studied in TRT context
• Available orally

Risks and trade-offs:
• Over-suppression causes joint pain, low libido, depression, bone loss
• Blunts cardiovascular protection from estrogen
• Lab-guided dosing ONLY — not prophylactic
• Negatively affects lipid profile
• Low E2 symptoms mimic high E2 symptoms

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Conservative: 0.25mg E3D — Every 3 days oral (Only while E2 is elevated)
• Standard: 0.5mg E3D — Every 3 days (To maintain E2 20-35 pg/mL)
• Higher dose: 1mg E3D — Bloodwork guidance only (Short-term until E2 in range)

Progression: NEVER dose without labs. Target E2 20-35 pg/mL (sensitive assay). If low E2 symptoms appear, reduce or stop immediately.

Common protocols:
• TRT E2 Management: Use ONLY if E2 >40 pg/mL on sensitive assay AND symptomatic, Anastrozole 0.25-0.5mg E3D, Recheck labs in 6 weeks

Monitoring: E2 sensitive assay, Total T, Free T every 6-8 weeks when adjusting.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for breast cancer. Off-label for estrogen management in TRT.

entries.title: Tamoxifen
entries.subtitle: Nolvadex, Tamox
entries.text:
Tamoxifen (Nolvadex, Tamox) — Ancillaries

SERM blocking estrogen receptors in breast tissue while acting as agonist in others. Unlike AIs, works at receptor level without reducing systemic estrogen. Critical PCT component. Research strongly supports its role alongside Clomid. First-line for gynecomastia treatment and prevention.

Reported benefits:
• Primary PCT agent for restoring natural T
• Treats and prevents gynecomastia
• Does not crash systemic estrogen like AIs
• Bone protective as estrogen agonist
• Extensively studied in PCT context
• Oral

Risks and trade-offs:
• Mood effects reported in some users
• Visual disturbances (rare, reversible)
• Blood clot risk at high doses
• Not for long-term use
• Hot flashes possible

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• PCT Standard: 40mg/day wks 1-2, then 20mg/day wks 3-6 — Daily oral (4-6 weeks total PCT)
• Gyno prevention: 10-20mg/day — Daily during cycle (As needed during cycle)

Progression: Begin PCT 2 weeks after last long-ester injection. Run minimum 6 weeks for full cycles.

Common protocols:
• PCT After Test Cycle: Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg per week, Clomid 50/50/25/25mg concurrent, HCG 500IU 3x/wk during LAST 2 weeks of cycle (stop before PCT)

Monitoring: Total T, LH, FSH, E2 at end of PCT. Goal: LH/FSH recovering, T returning toward baseline.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for breast cancer. Off-label for male gynecomastia and PCT.

entries.title: Clomiphene
entries.subtitle: Clomid, Enclomiphene
entries.text:
Clomiphene (Clomid, Enclomiphene) — Ancillaries

SERM blocking hypothalamic estrogen receptors, increasing LH and FSH, stimulating testicular T production. PCT staple. Contains two isomers: zuclomiphene (side effects) and enclomiphene (active beneficial isomer). Enclomiphene alone is increasingly preferred as a cleaner alternative.

Reported benefits:
• Directly stimulates LH/FSH and endogenous T
• Effective HPTA restart agent
• Fertility preserving
• Oral and convenient
• Enclomiphene isomer has cleaner profile
• Well-studied in PCT literature

Risks and trade-offs:
• Mood side effects from zuclomiphene isomer
• Vision disturbances rare
• Estrogen rebound possible
• Not for use during active suppressive cycle
• Enclomiphene preferred but harder to source

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• PCT: 50mg/day wks 1-2 then 25mg/day wks 3-4 — Daily oral (4-6 weeks PCT)
• Fertility / Low T: 25mg daily or 50mg 3x/week — Oral (3-6 months with monitoring)

Progression: Pair with Nolvadex for PCT. Begin 2 weeks after last long-ester injection simultaneously with Nolvadex.

Common protocols:
• PCT: Clomid 50/50/25/25mg/day, Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg/day, HCG 500IU 3x/wk last 2 wks of cycle (stop before SERMs)

Monitoring: LH, FSH, Total T, E2 throughout PCT and 4 weeks post-completion.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for female infertility. Off-label for male hypogonadism and PCT.

entries.title: HCG
entries.subtitle: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin
entries.text:
HCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin) — Ancillaries

Mimics LH, directly stimulating testicular Leydig cells to produce testosterone and maintain testicular volume. Used during TRT to preserve fertility and testicular size, and as a pre-PCT bridge to prime testes. Research supports 250-500IU 2-3x/week during TRT. Important: HCG is used BEFORE PCT begins, not during PCT.

Reported benefits:
• Preserves testicular size and function on TRT
• Maintains fertility potential during cycle
• Primes testes for PCT restart
• Supports intratesticular testosterone
• Directly mimics natural LH signal

Risks and trade-offs:
• Elevates estrogen (aromatizes significantly in testes)
• Requires refrigeration after reconstitution
• Injection only
• Can cause Leydig cell desensitization at very high doses
• Must stop BEFORE starting SERM PCT

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Fertility on TRT: 250-500IU — 2-3x per week SubQ (Ongoing with TRT)
• Pre-PCT primer: 500IU 3x/week — Last 2-3 weeks of cycle (Stop 2 weeks before starting SERMs)
• Blast restart: 1000-1500IU 3x/week — Short term (2-4 weeks max)

Progression: TRT: low-dose ongoing. Pre-PCT: 500IU 3x/wk for last 2 weeks of cycle, then STOP, wait 2 weeks, start SERMs.

Common protocols:
• TRT + Fertility: Testosterone Cypionate 100-150mg/week, HCG 250IU 2x/week, Anastrozole 0.25mg E3D only if E2 elevated

Monitoring: E2 (HCG aromatizes significantly), Total T. LH/FSH will be suppressed — this is expected.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for female infertility and cryptorchidism. Off-label for male TRT support.

entries.title: Enclomiphene
entries.subtitle: Androxal, Enclomifene, NF-1010
entries.text:
Enclomiphene (Androxal, Enclomifene, NF-1010) — Additional Ancillaries

Enclomiphene is the trans-isomer of clomiphene citrate — the active component responsible for LH/FSH stimulation. Standard Clomid contains both enclomiphene (beneficial) and zuclomiphene (responsible for most side effects including mood disturbances and visual issues). Purified enclomiphene provides the HPTA-stimulating benefits of Clomid with a significantly cleaner side effect profile. Clinical trials demonstrate effective testosterone restoration in hypogonadal men while preserving sperm production — unlike TRT which suppresses it. Increasingly used as an alternative to TRT in younger men who want testosterone restoration while maintaining fertility.

Reported benefits:
• Cleaner than Clomid — no zuclomiphene side effects
• Restores testosterone while preserving fertility
• Effective alternative to TRT for secondary hypogonadism
• Once daily oral
• Maintains LH/FSH activity (unlike TRT)
• Growing clinical evidence base
• Preserves fertility unlike TRT
• Raises endogenous testosterone
• Better tolerated than Clomid
• Once-daily oral dosing
• Useful for younger men not ready for TRT
• Testosterone restoration after cycle

Risks and trade-offs:
• Smaller body of evidence than standard Clomid
• Not FDA approved (Androxal trials completed but approval pending)
• Sourcing may be from compounding pharmacies
• Long-term effects on testicular health not fully studied
• Does not work in primary hypogonadism (testicular failure)
• Still more expensive than standard Clomid
• Cannot achieve testosterone levels as high as TRT
• Daily oral medication
• Less available than Clomid
• Insurance typically does not cover
• Requires intact HPG axis

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Testosterone Restoration: 12.5-25mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing monitoring — reassess every 3 months)
• PCT: 25mg/day — Daily oral (4-6 weeks PCT)
• TRT Alternative: 25mg/day — Oral, morning (Ongoing under physician care)

Progression: Excellent first-line option for men under 40 with secondary hypogonadism who want fertility preservation. Monitor T, LH, FSH, and E2 every 6-8 weeks and titrate dose. Some men remain on long-term with good outcomes.

Common protocols:
• Testosterone Restoration Without TRT: Enclomiphene 25mg/day, HCG 250IU 2x/week (optional, additional LH effect), Anastrozole 0.25mg E3D if E2 elevated
• TRT Alternative: Enclomiphene 25mg/day, HCG 500 IU 2x/week, Anastrozole 0.25mg 2x/week if needed
• PCT Protocol: Enclomiphene 25mg/day for 6–8 weeks, HCG 1000 IU 3x/week for first 2 weeks, Omega-3 for lipid support

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, LH, FSH, E2, Semen analysis (if fertility is goal), every 6-8 weeks when adjusting.

Regulatory status: Not FDA approved (NDA submitted as Androxal — pending). Compounding pharmacy sourced in US.

entries.title: Standard PCT — Testosterone Cycle
entries.subtitle: HPTA Restart Protocol
entries.text:
Standard PCT — Testosterone Cycle (HPTA Restart Protocol) — PCT Protocols

Structured approach to restarting the HPTA after a suppressive cycle. Goal: restore endogenous testosterone, normalize LH/FSH, minimize muscle loss. Research supports SERM-based PCT (Nolvadex plus Clomid) as the evidence-based standard. The pre-PCT HCG phase significantly improves restart outcomes by priming the testes.

Reported benefits:
• Restores natural hormone production
• Reduces long-term suppression risk
• Helps maintain gains post-cycle
• Supports mood and wellbeing during recovery
• Improves fertility markers

Risks and trade-offs:
• Window of vulnerability for muscle loss
• 4-12 weeks for full HPTA recovery
• Side effects from SERMs possible
• Bloodwork essential to confirm recovery
• Heavy or long cycles may cause prolonged suppression

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard (Test-only): Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg + Clomid 50/50/25/25mg — Daily oral concurrent (6 weeks)
• Aggressive (Heavy cycle): Nolvadex 40mg + Clomid 50mg wks 1-2 then taper — Daily (8 weeks)
• TRT discontinuation: HCG 500IU 3x/wk x 3 wks then Nolva + Clomid standard — Sequential (3 weeks HCG + 6 weeks SERMs)

Progression: 1. HCG 500IU 3x/wk during last 2 weeks of cycle. 2. Stop HCG. Wait 2 weeks after last long-ester injection. 3. Start Nolvadex + Clomid together. 4. Run 6 weeks minimum. 5. Bloodwork 4 weeks post-PCT.

Common protocols:
• Complete PCT Stack: Phase 1 (last 2 wks of cycle): HCG 500IU 3x/wk, Phase 2 (2-week washout): No compounds, Phase 3 (6 weeks): Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg + Clomid 50/50/25/25mg, Support: Zinc, Vitamin D, Ashwagandha, Bloodwork 4 weeks after PCT ends

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, LH, FSH, E2 at end of PCT and 4 weeks post. Goal: T toward baseline, LH/FSH rising.

Regulatory status: PCT combines off-label SERM use. SERMs are approved for other indications.

entries.title: Nandrolone Decanoate
entries.subtitle: Deca-Durabolin, Deca, NPP
entries.text:
Nandrolone Decanoate (Deca-Durabolin, Deca, NPP) — Anabolic / AAS

Nandrolone Decanoate is one of the most studied anabolic steroids, with a clinical history spanning 60+ years. It has a lower androgenic ratio than testosterone (anabolic:androgenic = 125:37) making it popular for therapeutic use in muscle-wasting diseases, osteoporosis, and anemia. The decanoate ester provides a half-life of ~15 days. Research (2020-2026) continues to examine its role in HIV wasting syndrome, chronic kidney disease, and cachexia. In performance contexts it is valued for joint lubrication, lean mass gains, and recovery. Notably it converts to DHN rather than DHT, reducing androgenic side effects at tissues.

Reported benefits:
• Exceptional joint lubrication and pain relief
• Lower androgenic activity than testosterone
• Used therapeutically for 60+ years — well studied
• Promotes lean mass gains with less water retention than testosterone
• Beneficial for osteoporosis and bone density
• Approved medical uses in many countries

Risks and trade-offs:
• Highly suppressive to natural testosterone — must run with Test base
• Progesterone-based gynecomastia risk (different mechanism than estrogen)
• Sexual dysfunction (Deca dick) without adequate testosterone base
• Long detection time — months
• Cardiovascular strain on lipids
• Hepatotoxicity low but hematocrit risk present

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• TRT / Therapeutic: 50-100mg/week — Weekly IM (Ongoing with physician oversight)
• Recovery / Joint: 100-200mg/week — Weekly IM (8-12 weeks)
• Performance: 300-400mg/week — Weekly IM (12-16 weeks + PCT)

Progression: Always run with a testosterone base (minimum TRT dose). Start at 200mg/week for performance, assess at 4 weeks. Prolactin management may be needed — consider Cabergoline if prolactin rises.

Common protocols:
• Joint Recovery Stack: Nandrolone 200mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate 200mg/week (base), BPC-157 500mcg/day, Anastrozole per E2 labs
• Performance / Mass: Nandrolone 300-400mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate 400-500mg/week, HCG 250IU 2x/week, Anastrozole per labs

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, E2, Prolactin, LH, FSH, Hematocrit, Lipids, Liver enzymes. Prolactin monitoring is especially important with nandrolone.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for anemia and wasting diseases. Performance use is off-label.

entries.title: Oxandrolone
entries.subtitle: Anavar, Var
entries.text:
Oxandrolone (Anavar, Var) — Anabolic / AAS

Oxandrolone is a mild oral anabolic steroid with a high anabolic:androgenic ratio (322-630:24). Originally developed for muscle-wasting diseases and burn recovery, it remains FDA-approved for these indications. It is uniquely mild — relatively low hepatotoxicity compared to other oral AAS, minimal aromatization, and modest HPTA suppression. Research supports its use in HIV wasting, burn victims, and Turner syndrome. In performance contexts it is valued for lean, dry gains, strength without weight, and fat loss — particularly popular with both male and female athletes due to its mild androgenic profile.

Reported benefits:
• FDA approved — one of the most medically validated AAS
• Mild hepatotoxicity relative to other oral AAS
• Minimal aromatization — no gynecomastia risk
• Significant strength gains without proportional weight gain
• Promotes fat oxidation and favorable body composition
• Women can use at low doses without virilization risk

Risks and trade-offs:
• Oral — 17-alpha alkylated — requires liver monitoring
• Suppressive to HPTA even at low doses
• Expensive — one of the priciest AAS per dose
• Cholesterol impact — HDL reduction
• Hair loss in genetically susceptible individuals
• Fake/underdosed product common on gray market

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Men — Low / Therapeutic: 20-40mg/day — Daily oral split 2x (6-8 weeks)
• Men — Performance: 40-80mg/day — Daily oral split 2x (6-8 weeks)
• Women: 5-10mg/day — Daily oral (4-6 weeks max)

Progression: Start at the lower end and assess liver enzymes and lipids at 4 weeks. Run milk thistle and TUDCA for liver support. Limit to 8 weeks continuous use. PCT required for men.

Common protocols:
• Lean Recomp / Cut: Oxandrolone 50mg/day, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pre-bed, Anastrozole only if E2 elevated
• Strength Cycle: Oxandrolone 60-80mg/day, Testosterone Cypionate 200-300mg/week, HCG 250IU 2x/week during cycle

Monitoring: Liver enzymes (ALT/AST) every 4 weeks, Lipid panel, Total T, Free T, LH/FSH. TUDCA 500mg/day and Milk Thistle throughout.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for wasting diseases and burn recovery. Performance use is off-label.

entries.title: Drostanolone
entries.subtitle: Masteron, Mast E, Mast P
entries.text:
Drostanolone (Masteron, Mast E, Mast P) — Anabolic / AAS

Drostanolone is a DHT-derived anabolic steroid that does not aromatize. Originally developed as a breast cancer treatment, it is now used in performance contexts for its anti-estrogenic properties, hardening effects, and free testosterone elevation. It binds to SHBG, increasing free testosterone availability. Propionate ester (Mast P) has a 2-3 day half-life; Enanthate ester (Mast E) has ~10 days. Particularly valued in cutting phases for muscle hardness, vascularity, and mood elevation. Works best at lower body fat percentages where the hardening effect is visually apparent.

Reported benefits:
• No aromatization — no gynecomastia risk
• Anti-estrogenic properties — may allow reduction of AI use
• Increases free testosterone by displacing SHBG
• Mood elevation and libido enhancement
• Muscle hardness and vascularity at low body fat
• Relatively mild side effect profile

Risks and trade-offs:
• Hair loss — strong DHT derivative (significant risk)
• Lipid impact on HDL
• Requires low body fat to appreciate aesthetic benefits
• HPTA suppression requires PCT
• Propionate ester requires frequent injections (EOD)
• Not effective for mass building

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cutting / Recomp: 300-400mg/week (Enanthate) — 2x weekly IM (10-12 weeks)
• Masteron Propionate: 350-500mg/week — EOD IM (8-10 weeks)

Progression: Best utilized with testosterone at a 1:1 or 1:2 ratio (Mast:Test). Works synergistically at 10-12% body fat or below. May allow AI dose reduction due to anti-estrogenic action.

Common protocols:
• Cutting Stack: Masteron E 400mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate 400mg/week, Tirzepatide or Semaglutide for fat loss, Anastrozole only per E2 labs

Monitoring: Lipid panel, Hair assessment, Total T, Free T, E2, SHBG, Liver enzymes, CBC.

Regulatory status: Originally approved for breast cancer treatment. Performance use is off-label. Schedule III controlled substance.

entries.title: Methenolone
entries.subtitle: Primobolan, Primo, Primo Depot
entries.text:
Methenolone (Primobolan, Primo, Primo Depot) — Anabolic / AAS

Methenolone is a mild DHT-derived anabolic steroid available in oral (acetate) and injectable (enanthate) forms. Famous for its use by Arnold Schwarzenegger, it is considered one of the safest AAS due to low androgenicity, minimal hepatotoxicity (injectable), and modest HPTA suppression. The injectable enanthate form (Primobolan Depot) is significantly preferred over oral. Valued for lean, keepable gains, immune system support (FDA-approved for immune deficiency diseases), and its mild nature suitable for longer cycles. High cost and frequent counterfeiting are notable drawbacks.

Reported benefits:
• One of the safest AAS profiles available
• Minimal aromatization
• Injectable form has very low hepatotoxicity
• Lean, dry, keepable gains
• FDA-approved for immune deficiency conditions
• Suitable for longer cycles than most AAS

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very expensive — most counterfeited AAS on the market
• Oral form has hepatotoxicity and poor bioavailability
• Mild gains relative to more aggressive compounds
• Still suppressive — PCT required
• Hair loss risk (DHT derivative)
• Lipid impact

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Injectable (Depot): 400-600mg/week — 2x weekly IM (12-16 weeks)
• Oral (Acetate) — less preferred: 100-150mg/day — Daily oral (6-8 weeks)

Progression: Injectable strongly preferred. Run with testosterone base. Source quality is critical — test kits recommended. Longer cycles than most AAS are acceptable given mild profile.

Common protocols:
• Lean Mass / Recomp: Primobolan E 500mg/week, Testosterone Cypionate 200mg/week (base), BPC-157 for connective tissue support, Anastrozole per labs

Monitoring: Liver enzymes (especially oral), Lipid panel, Total T, Free T, E2, Hematocrit.

Regulatory status: Approved in some countries for wasting diseases. Schedule III controlled substance in US.

entries.title: Ostarine
entries.subtitle: MK-2866, Enobosarm, GTx-024
entries.text:
Ostarine (MK-2866, Enobosarm, GTx-024) — SARMs

Ostarine (MK-2866) is the most researched and well-tolerated SARM. Originally developed by GTx Inc for muscle-wasting and osteoporosis, it has undergone multiple Phase II clinical trials — more human data than any other SARM. Mechanism: selectively binds androgen receptors in muscle and bone with minimal androgenic effects in prostate and skin. Phase II trials demonstrated significant lean mass preservation and gains with minimal suppression at therapeutic doses. Research through 2026 continues to explore its role in cancer cachexia and sarcopenia. Despite not being FDA approved, it is the closest SARM to clinical validation.

Reported benefits:
• Most human clinical trial data of any SARM
• Significant lean mass preservation and modest gains
• Minimal androgenic side effects at therapeutic doses
• Improves bone density in studies
• Oral, once daily dosing
• Relatively mild HPTA suppression vs AAS

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not FDA approved for any indication
• HPTA suppression still occurs — PCT may be needed
• Long-term safety not established
• Liver enzyme elevations reported at higher doses
• Cholesterol impact (HDL reduction)
• Legally gray — not for human consumption label in many countries

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Therapeutic / Mild: 10-15mg/day — Daily oral (8-12 weeks)
• Performance: 20-25mg/day — Daily oral (8-12 weeks)
• Women: 5-10mg/day — Daily oral (6-8 weeks)

Progression: Start at 10mg and assess at 4 weeks. At 25mg+ mini-PCT with Nolvadex 20mg x 4 weeks is recommended. Bloodwork before and after. Liver enzymes monitored.

Common protocols:
• Recomp / Lean Mass: Ostarine 20mg/day, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin pre-bed, BPC-157 for recovery, Testosterone TRT dose if on TRT (not required)
• Injury Recovery: Ostarine 12.5mg/day, BPC-157 500mcg/day, TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week

Monitoring: Liver enzymes at 4 weeks, Lipid panel, Total T, LH, FSH baseline and post-cycle. Mini-PCT at doses above 20mg.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Legally gray — not for human consumption.

entries.title: Ligandrol
entries.subtitle: LGD-4033, VK5211
entries.text:
Ligandrol (LGD-4033, VK5211) — SARMs

Ligandrol (LGD-4033) is among the most potent SARMs — clinical trials demonstrate significant lean mass gains at very low doses (1mg/day showed 1.21kg lean mass gain vs placebo in 21 days). Developed by Ligand Pharmaceuticals and licensed to Viking Therapeutics, it has completed Phase I and II trials. More anabolic than Ostarine with correspondingly stronger suppression. Research (2013-2026) shows dose-dependent lean mass gains and strength improvements. Being investigated for hip fracture recovery. Athletes have tested positive in drug tests for LGD-4033, confirming bioactivity.

Reported benefits:
• Most potent SARM for lean mass — clinical evidence
• Significant strength gains
• Phase II trial data exists
• Once daily oral dosing
• No aromatization
• Dry gains — no water retention
• Clinical trial data in humans (Phase II)
• Effective at very low doses (1mg)
• Strong lean mass gains
• Bone density benefits
• Oral administration
• Better tolerated than many SARMs

Risks and trade-offs:
• Most suppressive common SARM — full PCT often required
• Lipid impact (HDL reduction) more pronounced than Ostarine
• Liver stress at higher doses
• Not FDA approved
• Legal gray area
• Athletes have tested positive — banned in sport
• Significant testosterone suppression even at 1mg
• HDL reduction
• PCT required
• Long half-life means slow washout
• Hepatotoxicity in rare case reports

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Conservative: 5mg/day — Daily oral (8 weeks)
• Standard: 10mg/day — Daily oral (8-10 weeks)
• Higher (experienced): 15-20mg/day — Daily oral (8 weeks)
• Clinical Dose: 1mg/day — Oral, morning (12 weeks (Phase II protocol))
• Standard: 5mg/day — Oral, morning (8–12 weeks, then PCT)
• Advanced: 10mg/day — Oral, morning (8 weeks, then PCT)

Progression: Beginners: 1mg/day following clinical trial protocol. Experienced: 5–10mg/day. Bloodwork at week 6 and end. PCT essential: begin 1 week after last dose with enclomiphene 25mg/day for 6–8 weeks.

Common protocols:
• Mass Building: LGD-4033 10mg/day, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, MK-677 (Ibutamoren) 25mg/night (if using), Full PCT on cycle completion
• Lean Mass Cycle: LGD-4033 5mg/day, MK-677 15mg at bedtime, PCT planned: Enclomiphene 25mg/day × 8 weeks
• Cutting Stack: LGD-4033 5mg/day, Cardarine 10mg/day, Caloric deficit 300–500kcal

Monitoring: Total testosterone, LH, FSH, lipid panel, liver enzymes (ALT/AST), CBC, SHBG. Baseline required. At week 6 and post-cycle.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Phase II trials completed. Banned in sport.

entries.title: RAD-140
entries.subtitle: Testolone, RAD140
entries.text:
RAD-140 (Testolone, RAD140) — SARMs

RAD-140 (Testolone) is one of the most potent SARMs developed, with an anabolic:androgenic ratio of 90:1 compared to testosterone at 100:100. Developed by Radius Health for breast cancer and muscle wasting, it has shown strong neuroprotective properties alongside anabolic effects in preclinical research. Phase I clinical trials ongoing as of 2026. Demonstrates strong lean mass and strength increases with high selectivity. Also notable for potential CNS protection. Among the most suppressive SARMs — requires robust PCT.

Reported benefits:
• Extremely high anabolic:androgenic ratio (90:1)
• Strong lean mass and strength gains
• Neuroprotective properties in preclinical studies
• No aromatization
• Oral once daily dosing
• Potential applications in Alzheimer's research (neuroprotection)
• Highest anabolic potency among SARMs
• Minimal prostate stimulation
• Neuroprotective in animal models
• Being investigated for ER+ breast cancer
• Strong lean mass gains

Risks and trade-offs:
• Highly suppressive — full PCT required
• Liver enzyme elevations reported
• Aggression and mood changes at higher doses
• Hair loss risk
• Limited long-term human safety data
• Not FDA approved
• Significant testosterone suppression
• Hepatotoxicity reports
• Altered lipid profile (HDL reduction)
• PCT required
• Aggression in some users

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Conservative: 5-10mg/day — Daily oral (8 weeks)
• Standard: 10-15mg/day — Daily oral (8-10 weeks)
• Conservative: 5mg/day — Oral, morning (8 weeks, then PCT)
• Standard: 10mg/day — Oral, morning (8–12 weeks, then PCT)
• Advanced: 15mg/day — Oral, morning (8 weeks max, then PCT)

Progression: Start at 5mg. Full PCT (Nolvadex + Clomid) required. Monitor liver enzymes at 4 weeks. Due to potency, shorter cycles preferred. Not stacked with other suppressive compounds for beginners.

Common protocols:
• Lean Mass / Strength: RAD-140 10mg/day, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin for GH support, BPC-157 for connective tissue, Full PCT on completion
• Recomposition: RAD-140 10mg/day, Cardarine 10mg/day (optional), Anastrozole 0.5mg 2x/week (if needed), PCT planned: Enclomiphene 25mg/day 6 weeks
• Lean Bulk: RAD-140 10mg/day, MK-677 15mg at bedtime, High protein diet 2.2g/kg

Monitoring: Total testosterone, LH, FSH (suppression), lipid panel (HDL), liver enzymes (ALT/AST, bilirubin), CBC. Baseline and at cycle end.

Regulatory status: Research compound — Phase I trials ongoing. No FDA approval. Banned in sport.

entries.title: Cardarine
entries.subtitle: GW-501516, GW1516
entries.text:
Cardarine (GW-501516, GW1516) — SARMs

Cardarine (GW-501516) is technically a PPARdelta agonist, not a true SARM, but is categorized alongside them in performance contexts. Originally developed by GlaxoSmithKline for metabolic syndrome and dyslipidemia. Dramatically improves endurance (marathon mice study — mice ran twice as far), oxidizes fat, and improves cholesterol profile. GSK abandoned development after it caused rapid cancer development in multiple animal tissues in 2-year rodent studies. This carcinogenicity concern is serious and ongoing — cancer risk in humans unknown. Used recreationally for endurance and fat loss despite this.

Reported benefits:
• Dramatic endurance enhancement
• Fat oxidation and body composition improvement
