• Improves HDL and overall lipid profile
• No hormonal activity — no suppression
• Oral once daily
• Anti-inflammatory properties

Risks and trade-offs:
• SERIOUS: Caused rapid cancer development in 2-year animal studies
• GSK abandoned development specifically due to carcinogenicity
• Long-term human cancer risk completely unknown
• No clinical trials completed
• Not FDA approved
• WADA banned substance

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• If used (with full awareness of risks): 10-20mg/day — Daily oral (8 weeks maximum — long-term use contraindicated)

Progression: Full informed consent on cancer risk is essential. Many researchers and physicians advise against use entirely given animal carcinogenicity data. If used, shortest cycle possible with longest possible break.

Common protocols:
• Endurance / Fat Loss (risk acknowledged): Cardarine 10-20mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose (if on TRT), BPC-157 for tissue support

Monitoring: Liver enzymes, general cancer screening awareness, lipid panel.

Regulatory status: Research compound — development abandoned by GSK due to carcinogenicity. No FDA approval. Banned in sport.

entries.title: Recombinant HGH
entries.subtitle: Somatropin, rHGH, Human Growth Hormone, Genotropin, Norditropin, Humatrope, Omnitrope, Somatropin (rhGH)
entries.text:
Recombinant HGH (Somatropin, rHGH, Human Growth Hormone, Genotropin, Norditropin, Humatrope, Omnitrope, Somatropin (rhGH)) — HGH and IGF-1

Recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin) is bioidentical to endogenous GH, produced through recombinant DNA technology. FDA-approved for adult GHD, HIV wasting, short bowel syndrome, Turner syndrome, and other conditions. In adults, GH acts primarily through IGF-1 production in the liver. Clinical research consistently demonstrates improved body composition (fat loss, lean mass increase), bone density, lipid profiles, and quality of life in GHD adults. In performance contexts it is used for body composition, recovery, and anti-aging. Effects are gradual — 3-6 months for meaningful changes. Quality and source authenticity are critical concerns.

Reported benefits:
• FDA approved for multiple adult indications
• Bioidentical — works identically to endogenous GH
• Clinically proven body composition improvements
• Improves bone density and joint health
• Lipid profile improvements
• Anti-aging effects including skin quality, sleep, and recovery
• Improves body composition over time
• Enhances recovery and sleep quality
• Supports joint, skin, and connective tissue
• Increases IGF-1 and fat metabolism
• Pharmaceutical brands highly consistent
• Synergistic with peptide GH secretagogues

Risks and trade-offs:
• Expensive — often $500-2000+/month without insurance
• Requires refrigeration
• Injection only — daily SubQ
• Carpal tunnel syndrome common at higher doses
• Water retention and joint pain at high doses
• Insulin resistance risk — glucose monitoring required
• Potential for acromegaly features at chronic supraphysiological doses
• Expensive — especially pharma grade
• Slow results — months to see effects
• Water retention, carpal tunnel, joint aches
• Can raise blood glucose / insulin resistance
• Frequently counterfeit in grey market
• Requires refrigeration and proper handling

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Anti-aging / Wellness: 1-2 IU/day — Daily SubQ before bed or fasted AM (3-6 months minimum)
• Body Composition: 2-4 IU/day — Daily SubQ — some split AM and post-workout (3-6 months)
• Medical (GHD): Physician titrated — Daily (Ongoing as prescribed)
• Performance: 4-6+ IU/day — SubQ injection, split doses (Advanced, monitor glucose)

Progression: Start at 1 IU/day for 4 weeks. Increase by 0.5 IU every 4 weeks. Monitor IGF-1 to target upper-normal range. High doses (4+ IU) provide diminishing returns with increasing side effects. Fasted morning or pre-sleep timing preferred.

Common protocols:
• Anti-aging / Recomp: HGH 2 IU/day, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, BPC-157 500mcg/day, Metformin 500-1000mg/day (insulin sensitivity)
• Recovery / Anti-Aging: Somatropin 2 IU/day, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin (synergy), Quality sleep and protein

Monitoring: IGF-1 (critical — maintain upper third of normal range), Fasting glucose, HbA1c, Lipid panel every 3 months. Wrist and joint assessment for carpal tunnel.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for adult GHD, HIV wasting, Turner syndrome, and other indications. Off-label anti-aging use.

entries.title: IGF-1 LR3
entries.subtitle: Long R3 IGF-1, Insulin-like Growth Factor 1
entries.text:
IGF-1 LR3 (Long R3 IGF-1, Insulin-like Growth Factor 1) — HGH and IGF-1

IGF-1 Long R3 is a modified form of IGF-1 with an arginine substitution and 13-amino acid extension that dramatically extends half-life from ~10 minutes (native IGF-1) to ~20-30 hours. IGF-1 mediates most of GH's anabolic effects — stimulating muscle cell proliferation, satellite cell activation, protein synthesis, and fat oxidation. Unlike HGH which requires conversion to IGF-1, LR3 acts directly. Research shows it promotes hyperplasia (new muscle fiber formation) in addition to hypertrophy, which may produce more permanent gains. Used post-workout for site enhancement and systemic anabolism.

Reported benefits:
• Direct anabolic action without GH conversion step
• Promotes muscle hyperplasia — potentially permanent new fibers
• Extended half-life allows once-daily dosing
• Fat oxidation enhancement
• Recovery and protein synthesis acceleration
• Synergistic with HGH and testosterone

Risks and trade-offs:
• Hypoglycemia risk — must be used with carbohydrates nearby
• Cancer promotion risk — IGF-1 is a mitogen (promotes cell growth)
• Organ growth concern with chronic supraphysiological use
• Expensive and difficult to source with reliable purity
• Acromegaly risk with chronic overdosing
• Not approved for human use

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Performance: 40-80mcg/day — Daily SubQ post-workout or AM (4-6 weeks — cycle off equal time)
• Site injection: 20-40mcg — IM into target muscle post-workout (4 weeks max)

Progression: Always have fast-acting carbohydrates available — hypoglycemia can occur rapidly. Start at 40mcg. Never exceed 6-week cycles. Equal time off to allow IGF-1 receptor sensitivity to normalize.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Recomp: IGF-1 LR3 50mcg/day post-workout, HGH 2-4 IU/day, Testosterone Cypionate 200-400mg/week, Metformin for insulin sensitivity

Monitoring: Fasting glucose (hypoglycemia risk critical), IGF-1 levels, tumor markers awareness, lipid panel.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label.

entries.title: NMN / NR (NAD+ Precursors)
entries.subtitle: Nicotinamide Mononucleotide, Nicotinamide Riboside
entries.text:
NMN / NR (NAD+ Precursors) (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide, Nicotinamide Riboside) — Nootropics and Longevity

NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) is a critical coenzyme involved in over 500 enzymatic reactions, DNA repair, circadian rhythm regulation, and cellular energy production. NAD+ levels decline ~50% by age 50. NMN and NR are oral precursors that effectively raise NAD+ levels. David Sinclair's research at Harvard has popularized these compounds in longevity science. Clinical trials (2021-2026) confirm NMN and NR safely increase NAD+ levels in humans. Benefits include improved mitochondrial function, DNA repair capacity, metabolic health, and potential longevity signaling via sirtuin activation.

Reported benefits:
• Clinically validated to raise NAD+ levels in humans
• Activates sirtuins — longevity-associated proteins
• Improves mitochondrial biogenesis and energy
• Enhances DNA repair mechanisms
• Metabolic benefits — improved insulin sensitivity
• Excellent safety profile in trials to date

Risks and trade-offs:
• Expensive for quality products
• Optimal dose for longevity benefits not established
• NMN vs NR debate ongoing — unclear which is superior
• Some debate whether oral NMN survives digestion without IV
• Long-term human longevity data still accumulating
• Theoretical concern: NAD+ feeds cancer cell metabolism

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• NMN: 500-1000mg/day — Daily oral AM with or without food (Ongoing)
• NR: 300-500mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing)

Progression: Take in the AM — NAD+ is involved in circadian signaling. Often combined with Resveratrol or Pterostilbene (sirtuin activators) and TMG (methyl donor) to maximize benefit. Sublingual NMN may have superior bioavailability.

Common protocols:
• Longevity / Mitochondrial: NMN 500-1000mg AM, Resveratrol 500mg with fat, TMG 500-1000mg, Testosterone TRT dose (if applicable), Epithalon pulse cycles

Monitoring: No specific labs required. Optional: cellular NAD+ testing (specialty labs), HbA1c, fasting glucose.

Regulatory status: NMN and NR are sold as dietary supplements in the US. Not FDA approved as drugs.

entries.title: Dihexa
entries.subtitle: PNB-0408, HGF Modulator
entries.text:
Dihexa (PNB-0408, HGF Modulator) — Nootropics and Longevity

Dihexa is a synthetic peptide derived from angiotensin IV, developed at Washington State University by Dr. Joseph Harding. It is a potent hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) agonist that promotes synaptogenesis — the formation of new synaptic connections. Preclinical research shows it is approximately 10 million times more potent than BDNF at promoting new synapse formation. Research demonstrates dramatic cognitive improvements in Alzheimer's disease models and traumatic brain injury. Currently in early research stages for neurodegeneration and cognitive disorders. Among the most promising and potent nootropic peptides known, though human data is very limited.

Reported benefits:
• Among the most potent synaptogenic compounds known
• Promotes new synaptic connection formation
• Dramatic cognitive improvements in animal models
• Potential for neurodegeneration treatment
• HGF agonism has systemic repair implications
• Extremely low doses required due to potency

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very limited human data — mostly animal studies
• Long-term safety completely unknown
• Difficult to dose accurately due to extreme potency
• Theoretical risk: synaptogenesis could promote certain tumor growth
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing and purity verification critical

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Research dose: 1-10mg — Oral or intranasal — once daily or less frequent (Short cycles — 2-4 weeks given limited safety data)

Progression: Extremely potent — start at the lowest end. Given the novelty and potency, many researchers use with caution and infrequent dosing. Human data will develop over the coming years. Use with full awareness of limited safety information.

Common protocols:
• Cognitive / Neuroplasticity: Dihexa (cautiously low dose), Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, BPC-157 250mcg/day (neuroprotective)

Monitoring: Cognitive and mood self-assessment. No established blood monitoring protocol.

Regulatory status: Research compound — very early stage. No FDA approval. Extremely limited human data.

entries.title: Thymosin Alpha-1
entries.subtitle: Ta1, Zadaxin, Thymalfasin
entries.text:
Thymosin Alpha-1 (Ta1, Zadaxin, Thymalfasin) — Additional Peptides

Thymosin Alpha-1 (Ta1) is a 28-amino acid peptide derived from the thymus gland, FDA-approved in over 35 countries for Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and as an immune adjuvant in cancer treatment. Not yet FDA-approved in the US but used extensively internationally. It modulates and enhances the immune system — particularly T-cell and NK cell activity — without causing overstimulation or autoimmunity. Research demonstrates antiviral, antifungal, and anti-tumor immune enhancement. Used in longevity and biohacking communities for immune system optimization, recovery from illness, and prevention. Particularly relevant for anyone immunocompromised or seeking immune optimization.

Reported benefits:
• FDA approved in 35+ countries — well validated safety
• Enhances T-cell and NK cell immune function
• Antiviral and antifungal effects
• Anti-tumor immune enhancement
• No immune overstimulation or autoimmunity
• Synergistic with BPC-157 (TB-500 is its partner)

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not FDA approved in the United States
• Expensive
• Injection only
• Limited longevity-specific human data
• Sourcing from compounding pharmacies required in US
• Effects may be subtle in healthy individuals

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Immune Optimization: 1.6mg — SubQ 2x weekly (4-6 weeks on / 4 weeks off)
• Active illness / Cancer adjuvant: 1.6mg — Daily SubQ (As directed — physician supervised)

Progression: Standard protocol is 1.6mg twice weekly. Often cycled seasonally (winter months) for immune optimization. Pairs well with BPC-157 for comprehensive immune and tissue support.

Common protocols:
• Immune / Longevity: Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week, BPC-157 250mcg/day, NMN 500mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose if applicable

Monitoring: Complete blood count (immune cell assessment), general inflammatory markers. No specific monitoring beyond standard health panel.

Regulatory status: FDA approved in 35+ countries for Hepatitis B and C. Not FDA approved in the US.

entries.title: MOTS-c
entries.subtitle: Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame Peptide, Humanin analogue
entries.text:
MOTS-c (Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame Peptide, Humanin analogue) — Additional Peptides

MOTS-c is a mitochondrially encoded peptide — one of a family of small peptides (mitochondrial-derived peptides or MDPs) encoded within mitochondrial DNA rather than nuclear DNA. Discovered in 2015 by Cohen and Lee at USC, it regulates metabolic homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and exercise capacity. Research demonstrates MOTS-c mimics the metabolic effects of exercise — improving glucose uptake in skeletal muscle independent of insulin. It activates AMPK signaling (the master metabolic switch), improves mitochondrial function, and extends lifespan in animal models. Circulating MOTS-c declines with age. One of the most exciting emerging peptides in longevity science.

Reported benefits:
• Mimics metabolic effects of exercise — AMPK activation
• Improves insulin sensitivity independently of insulin
• Enhances mitochondrial function and biogenesis
• Extends lifespan in animal models
• Declines with age — supplementation may restore youthful levels
• Novel mechanism distinct from other peptides

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very early human research stage
• Limited clinical data in humans
• Long-term effects unknown
• Expensive and difficult to source
• Optimal dosing not established
• Mechanism complex — effects may vary by individual metabolic status

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Research protocol: 5-10mg — SubQ 2-3x weekly (4-8 weeks)

Progression: Emerging compound — follow developing research. Often used in longevity stacks alongside NMN, BPC-157, and Epithalon. Best taken on training days for synergistic effect with exercise-induced AMPK activation.

Common protocols:
• Longevity / Metabolic: MOTS-c 5-10mg 3x/week, NMN 500-1000mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Epithalon pulse cycles

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, metabolic panel. Self-assessment of energy and exercise capacity.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Very early human research stage.

entries.title: P21
entries.subtitle: P21 peptide, CNTF fragment
entries.text:
P21 (P21 peptide, CNTF fragment) — Additional Peptides

P21 is a synthetic peptide derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (CNTF) that promotes neurogenesis — the formation of new neurons and neural connections. Research demonstrates it increases hippocampal neurogenesis, improves synaptic plasticity, and enhances spatial learning and memory. Unlike Dihexa which works via HGF and synaptogenesis, P21 works via CNTF receptors to promote new neuron formation. Particularly promising for cognitive decline and neurodegenerative conditions. Some researchers combine it with Dihexa for a comprehensive neuroplasticity approach.

Reported benefits:
• Promotes neurogenesis — new neuron formation
• Hippocampal neuroplasticity enhancement
• Improves learning and spatial memory
• Different mechanism than Dihexa — potentially complementary
• Promising for neurodegeneration research
• Low doses required

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very limited human data
• Theoretical cancer risk from uncontrolled neurogenesis
• Difficult to source
• Not FDA approved
• Optimal dosing not established
• Should be approached with significant caution

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Research dose: 100-200mcg — SubQ daily or every other day (2-4 weeks with breaks)

Progression: Use with caution given theoretical risks of uncontrolled neurogenesis. Short cycles with breaks. Do not combine with other strongly neurogenic compounds without careful consideration.

Common protocols:
• Neuroplasticity Stack cautious: P21 100mcg SubQ daily, Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, BPC-157 250mcg/day

Monitoring: Cognitive function assessment, mood tracking. Neurological evaluation if any concerning symptoms.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Very early research stage.

entries.title: Exemestane
entries.subtitle: Aromasin
entries.text:
Exemestane (Aromasin) — Additional Ancillaries

Exemestane is a steroidal, irreversible (Type I) aromatase inhibitor — mechanistically distinct from anastrozole and letrozole (both non-steroidal, reversible Type II). Because it irreversibly deactivates aromatase enzymes rather than competitively blocking them, estrogen suppression is sustained even after discontinuation until new aromatase is synthesized. A key advantage: exemestane itself has mild anabolic/androgenic properties (it is a steroid) and does not negatively impact cholesterol as severely as non-steroidal AIs. Some TRT specialists prefer it for these reasons. Also produces androsterone as a metabolite.

Reported benefits:
• Irreversible — sustained E2 suppression
• More favorable cholesterol profile than anastrozole
• Mild intrinsic androgenic activity
• May be preferable when anastrozole causes persistent side effects
• Well-studied — breast cancer treatment data
• Once daily dosing

Risks and trade-offs:
• Irreversible mechanism means overcorrection is harder to reverse
• Steroid-based — some androgenic sides possible
• Joint pain and hot flashes with over-suppression
• More expensive than anastrozole
• Still requires bloodwork guidance
• Bone density concerns with long-term over-suppression

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• TRT E2 Management: 12.5mg E3D or 25mg twice weekly — Oral (Lab-guided — use only while E2 elevated)
• Cycle support: 25mg EOD — Oral (During cycle as needed)

Progression: Use in same context as anastrozole — only when bloodwork confirms elevated E2 AND symptoms present. The irreversible mechanism requires more careful dose management. Some prefer it for its androgenic metabolites.

Common protocols:
• TRT E2 Alternative to Anastrozole: Exemestane 12.5-25mg E3D, Testosterone Cypionate ongoing, Recheck E2 sensitive assay in 6 weeks

Monitoring: E2 sensitive assay, Total T, Free T, Lipid panel, Bone density with long-term use.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for breast cancer. Off-label for estrogen management in TRT.

entries.title: Cabergoline
entries.subtitle: Dostinex, Caber
entries.text:
Cabergoline (Dostinex, Caber) — Additional Ancillaries

Cabergoline is a dopamine agonist (D2 receptor) primarily used to treat hyperprolactinemia (elevated prolactin) and prolactinoma tumors. In TRT and performance contexts, it is essential when using progestogenic compounds such as Nandrolone, Trenbolone, or high-dose HCG which can raise prolactin significantly. Elevated prolactin causes sexual dysfunction, gynecomastia (progesterone/prolactin mechanism), lactation, and mood disorders. Cabergoline is highly effective and long-acting (twice weekly dosing). Also studied for potential longevity benefits — dopamine system maintenance and research into its protective effects in Parkinson's disease.

Reported benefits:
• Highly effective prolactin control
• Long half-life — twice weekly dosing only
• Addresses progesterone/prolactin gynecomastia (which AIs do not fix)
• Improves libido and sexual function through dopamine
• Well-tolerated at low doses
• FDA approved for prolactinoma

Risks and trade-offs:
• Heart valve concerns at high doses (Parkinson's disease doses — much higher than TRT use)
• Nausea, especially initially
• Fatigue possible
• Orthostatic hypotension
• Not needed unless prolactin is actually elevated
• Cardiac monitoring at higher doses recommended

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Prolactin Control: 0.25-0.5mg — Twice weekly oral (During and up to 4 weeks post progestogenic compound)
• Prolactinoma (medical): Physician titrated — Physician directed (Ongoing)

Progression: Use only when prolactin confirmed elevated on bloodwork or when running progestogenic compounds (nandrolone, trenbolone). 0.25mg twice weekly is often sufficient. Do not use prophylactically without lab confirmation.

Common protocols:
• Nandrolone Cycle Support: Cabergoline 0.25mg 2x/week, Testosterone Cypionate (base), Nandrolone Decanoate, Anastrozole per E2 labs

Monitoring: Prolactin (primary target — keep in normal range), E2, Echocardiogram if using higher doses long-term.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for hyperprolactinemia and prolactinoma. Off-label for TRT prolactin management.

entries.title: Dutasteride / Finasteride
entries.subtitle: Avodart (Duta), Propecia (Fina), 5-ARIs
entries.text:
Dutasteride / Finasteride (Avodart (Duta), Propecia (Fina), 5-ARIs) — Additional Ancillaries

Dutasteride (Avodart) and Finasteride (Propecia) are 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (5-ARIs) that block conversion of testosterone to DHT — the potent androgen responsible for hair follicle miniaturization and prostate growth. Finasteride inhibits Type II 5-AR (producing ~70% DHT reduction). Dutasteride inhibits both Type I and II (producing ~90% DHT reduction). Used in TRT to prevent hair loss in genetically susceptible individuals and to manage prostate size. The trade-off: DHT is important for libido, erection quality, mood, and body composition — over-suppression can cause Post-Finasteride Syndrome in susceptible individuals.

Reported benefits:
• Effective prevention of DHT-related hair loss
• Reduces prostate size (BPH treatment)
• Finasteride FDA approved for hair loss and BPH
• Dutasteride more complete DHT suppression
• Oral once daily
• Reduces DHT-related acne and oily skin

Risks and trade-offs:
• Post-Finasteride Syndrome — persistent sexual dysfunction, depression, cognitive impairment in susceptible men (rare but serious)
• Reduces DHT — important for libido, mood, erections
• Dutasteride: very long half-life makes discontinuation slow
• May reduce muscle fullness and body composition
• Teratogenic — women of childbearing age must not handle crushed tablets
• Debate continues on long-term CNS effects

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Finasteride (hair loss): 1mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing — stop if sides develop)
• Dutasteride (more complete): 0.5mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing — long half-life)

Progression: Use only if genetically at risk for hair loss AND prioritize hair over potential DHT-related sides. Do not use prophylactically. If sexual dysfunction or mood changes develop, discontinue immediately. Some men use intermittently (3x/week) to minimize impact.

Common protocols:
• TRT Hair Loss Management: Dutasteride 0.5mg/day (if accepting trade-offs), Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, HCG 250IU 2x/week, Minoxidil topical (complementary)

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, DHT levels (if testing available), PSA, sexual function self-assessment monthly.

Regulatory status: Dutasteride FDA approved for BPH. Finasteride FDA approved for BPH and male pattern baldness.

entries.title: Liothyronine (T3)
entries.subtitle: Cytomel, T3, LT3
entries.text:
Liothyronine (T3) (Cytomel, T3, LT3) — Thyroid Hormones

Liothyronine is the active form of thyroid hormone (triiodothyronine, T3) that directly binds thyroid hormone receptors. While T4 (levothyroxine) must be converted to T3 by deiodinase enzymes, T3 acts immediately. Many individuals — particularly those on hormone optimization protocols — have suboptimal T4-to-T3 conversion due to nutrient deficiencies, chronic stress, or genetic variants in deiodinase enzymes. T3 directly controls metabolic rate, body temperature, cardiac output, cognitive function, and energy levels. Used in TRT and peptide contexts to optimize metabolism and address symptoms of subclinical hypothyroidism that persist despite normal TSH.

Reported benefits:
• Direct thyroid receptor activation — no conversion needed
• Rapidly improves metabolic rate and energy
• Enhances fat loss by increasing basal metabolic rate
• Improves cognitive function and mood
• Fast onset (hours vs weeks for T4)
• Addresses conversion issues undetectable on standard TSH testing

Risks and trade-offs:
• Short half-life — requires multiple daily doses or sustained-release
• Risk of hyperthyroidism (palpitations, anxiety, insomnia) if overdosed
• Bone density loss with long-term excess dosing
• Cardiac risk at supraphysiological doses
• Requires careful titration and monitoring
• Suppresses endogenous thyroid production

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 5-12.5mcg/day — Once or twice daily oral (4-6 weeks then assess)
• Therapeutic: 25-50mcg/day — Split twice daily (AM and noon) (Ongoing with monitoring)
• Optimization: 50-75mcg/day — Split 2-3x daily (Ongoing — physician supervised)

Progression: Start very low at 5mcg and increase by 5mcg every 2-4 weeks. Monitor heart rate, temperature, energy, and labs. Target Free T3 in upper third of normal range. Many practitioners use T3/T4 combination therapy.

Common protocols:
• Hormone Optimization: T3 25-50mcg/day (split doses), Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, Selenium 200mcg/day (supports conversion), Zinc 30mg/day
• Fat Loss / Metabolic: T3 25mcg/day, Tirzepatide (GLP-1 agent), Testosterone TRT dose (muscle preservation)

Monitoring: Free T3, Free T4, TSH, Reverse T3, heart rate (resting), blood pressure, bone density (long-term). TSH will suppress — this is expected at therapeutic T3 doses.

Regulatory status: FDA approved for hypothyroidism. Off-label for optimization when Free T3 is in low-normal range despite normal TSH.

entries.title: Levothyroxine (T4)
entries.subtitle: Synthroid, Levoxyl, LT4
entries.text:
Levothyroxine (T4) (Synthroid, Levoxyl, LT4) — Thyroid Hormones

Levothyroxine is the most prescribed hormone medication in the United States — a synthetic T4 that must be converted to active T3 by peripheral deiodinase enzymes. Standard of care for hypothyroidism. However, research (2019-2026) increasingly shows that a subset of patients feel suboptimally on T4 monotherapy due to poor T4-to-T3 conversion. In these cases, combination T4/T3 therapy or pure T3 supplementation is more effective. T4 has a long half-life of 7 days allowing once-daily dosing and stable levels.

Reported benefits:
• Most studied thyroid hormone — decades of safety data
• Once daily dosing due to long half-life
• FDA approved — widely available
• Stable blood levels
• Well understood dosing
• Lower cardiac risk than pure T3 at equivalent doses

Risks and trade-offs:
• Requires conversion to T3 — poor converters see suboptimal response
• Slower onset than T3
• TSH-based dosing may leave patients symptomatic in low-normal range
• Generic vs brand differences in absorption matter
• Absorption affected by food, coffee, calcium, iron
• Doesn't address Reverse T3 issues

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 25-50mcg/day — Once daily oral on empty stomach (6-8 weeks then recheck labs)
• Therapeutic: 75-150mcg/day — Once daily oral (Ongoing with annual monitoring)

Progression: Take 30-60 minutes before food or coffee. Titrate based on Free T4 and Free T3 — not TSH alone. If symptomatic on T4 monotherapy, consider adding small T3 dose.

Common protocols:
• Complete Thyroid Protocol: Levothyroxine T4 100mcg/day, Liothyronine T3 10mcg/day (combination), Selenium 200mcg/day, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Free T4, Free T3, TSH, Reverse T3 at 6-8 weeks after any dose change, then every 6-12 months stable.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for hypothyroidism. Standard of care worldwide.

entries.title: Natural Desiccated Thyroid
entries.subtitle: NDT, Armour Thyroid, NatureThroid, WP Thyroid
entries.text:
Natural Desiccated Thyroid (NDT, Armour Thyroid, NatureThroid, WP Thyroid) — Thyroid Hormones

Natural Desiccated Thyroid is derived from porcine (pig) thyroid glands and contains both T4 and T3 in a physiological ratio (approximately 4:1 T4:T3), along with T2, T1, and calcitonin. Used for over 100 years before synthetic alternatives. Many patients who feel suboptimal on T4 alone report feeling significantly better on NDT — a finding supported by growing research on the importance of T3 alongside T4. Contains all thyroid hormones in their natural form. Some practitioners prefer it for this reason.

Reported benefits:
• Contains both T4 and T3 in natural ratio
• Some patients report superior symptom relief vs T4 alone
• Contains additional thyroid peptides (T2, T1, calcitonin)
• Over 100 years of clinical use
• Standardized by USP for iodine content
• Often preferred by functional medicine practitioners

Risks and trade-offs:
• Variable potency between batches and brands historically
• Porcine source — not suitable for some dietary restrictions
• T3 component can cause peaks and troughs
• Requires same careful titration as synthetic hormones
• TSH suppression expected
• Some insurers don't cover it

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 15-30mg/day (1/4 to 1/2 grain) — Once daily oral (6-8 weeks then assess)
• Therapeutic: 60-120mg/day (1-2 grains) — Once or twice daily (Ongoing)

Progression: 1 grain NDT = approximately 60mcg T4 + 15mcg T3. Titrate based on symptoms AND Free T3/Free T4. Allow 6-8 weeks between dose changes. Monitor heart rate closely.

Common protocols:
• Thyroid Optimization: NDT 60-90mg/day, Selenium 200mcg/day (supports conversion), Testosterone TRT dose, Vitamin D 5000IU/day

Monitoring: Free T4, Free T3, TSH, heart rate. TSH typically suppresses — guide dose by Free T3 target.

Regulatory status: NOT FDA approved. Desiccated thyroid predates the 1938 legislation that created the modern approval pathway and has been marketed ever since under enforcement discretion rather than through an application — no manufacturer has submitted potency, purity or bioequivalence data for FDA review. Prescription required. Dispensed by most pharmacies and by compounding pharmacies.

entries.title: DHEA
entries.subtitle: Dehydroepiandrosterone, Prasterone
entries.text:
DHEA (Dehydroepiandrosterone, Prasterone) — DHEA and Adrenal

DHEA is the most abundant steroid hormone in the human body and serves as the primary precursor to both testosterone and estrogen. Produced by the adrenal glands, DHEA peaks in the mid-20s and declines ~10% per decade, reaching 10-20% of peak levels by age 70-80. Research demonstrates DHEA supplementation improves body composition, bone density, libido, immune function, cognitive performance, and mood in individuals with low levels. Recent research (2020-2026) supports its role in adrenal fatigue recovery and as an adjunct to hormone optimization. FDA-approved as Prasterone for vaginal atrophy.

Reported benefits:
• Most abundant steroid hormone — fundamental precursor
• Improves body composition and lean mass
• Enhances libido in both men and women
• Improves bone density
• Immune system support
• Mood and cognitive enhancement

Risks and trade-offs:
• Can convert to estrogen or testosterone — monitor both
• Acne and oily skin (androgenic effects)
• Hair thinning in susceptible individuals
• Can suppress DHEA-S production feedback
• Should be guided by lab testing of DHEA-S levels
• Avoid without confirmed deficiency

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Men: 25-50mg/day — Daily oral with morning meal (Ongoing — based on labs)
• Women: 5-25mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing — lower doses for women)
• Adrenal Support: 10-25mg/day — Daily AM oral (3-6 months then reassess)

Progression: Test DHEA-S before starting. Target DHEA-S in upper third of normal range for your age. Men typically need 25-50mg; women 5-25mg. Morning dosing mimics natural adrenal rhythm.

Common protocols:
• Hormone Optimization Stack: DHEA 25-50mg/day AM, Pregnenolone 50mg/day AM, Testosterone TRT dose, Vitamin D 5000IU/day
• Anti-aging / Adrenal: DHEA 25mg/day, 7-Keto DHEA 100mg/day, NMN 500mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: DHEA-S (primary marker), Total T, Free T, E2 (DHEA converts to both), PSA in men, lipid panel.

Regulatory status: Available as dietary supplement in US. FDA approved as Prasterone (Intrarosa) for vaginal atrophy. Requires monitoring for hormonal effects.

entries.title: Pregnenolone
entries.subtitle: Preg, Master Hormone, 3β-hydroxy-5-pregnen-20-one
entries.text:
Pregnenolone (Preg, Master Hormone, 3β-hydroxy-5-pregnen-20-one) — DHEA and Adrenal

Pregnenolone is the foundational steroid hormone — the first steroid synthesized from cholesterol and the precursor to all other steroid hormones including DHEA, progesterone, testosterone, estrogen, and cortisol. Called the master hormone for this reason. Research shows pregnenolone has direct neurosteroid activity — it modulates GABA and NMDA receptors in the brain, producing anxiolytic effects, improving memory, and reducing neuroinflammation independently of its role as a precursor. Levels decline with age. Clinical research supports its role in cognitive enhancement, mood stabilization, and as part of comprehensive hormone optimization.

Reported benefits:
• Precursor to all steroid hormones — comprehensive support
• Direct neurosteroid activity — memory and cognitive enhancement
• Anxiolytic effects via GABA modulation
• Anti-inflammatory in the central nervous system
• Improves sleep quality
• Well-tolerated at physiological doses
• Precursor to all steroid hormones
• Neurosteroid with direct CNS effects
• Supports memory and cognitive function
• May improve mood and energy
• Commonly used as TRT adjunct
• Low cost and widely available OTC

Risks and trade-offs:
• Can convert to any steroid — unpredictable conversion pathway
• Anxiety or irritability at high doses (stimulating)
• Monitor downstream hormone levels
• Limited large-scale human trial data
• Interacts with GABA receptors — caution with sedatives
• Best guided by hormone panel testing
• Downstream conversion unpredictable
• Can increase cortisol
• May worsen anxiety in some individuals
• Conversion to unwanted hormones possible
• Monitoring essential at higher doses

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cognitive / Mood: 50-100mg/day — Daily oral AM (Ongoing)
• Hormone Support: 100-200mg/day — Daily oral AM (3-6 months then reassess)
• Neurological Support: 10–30mg/day — Oral with fat-containing meal (Ongoing)
• Hormone Precursor: 50–100mg/day — Oral with fat-containing meal (3–6 months, then reassess)

Progression: Start at 10mg daily with meals. Assess energy, mood, and cognitive effects at 4 weeks. Increase to 50mg if well tolerated. Monitor downstream hormones — DHEA-S, testosterone, estradiol.

Common protocols:
• Comprehensive Hormone Optimization: Pregnenolone 100mg/day AM, DHEA 25-50mg/day AM, Testosterone TRT dose, Thyroid optimization if indicated
• TRT Adjunct: Pregnenolone 50mg/day, DHEA 25–50mg/day, Testosterone protocol
• Neurological: Pregnenolone 30mg/day, Semax 300mcg AM, Lion's Mane 1g/day

Monitoring: DHEA-S, testosterone, estradiol, progesterone, cortisol (AM fasted), comprehensive hormone panel at baseline and 8 weeks.

Regulatory status: Available as dietary supplement in US. Not FDA approved as a drug. Monitor hormonal effects.

entries.title: 7-Keto DHEA
entries.subtitle: 7-Keto, 3-acetyl-7-oxo-DHEA
entries.text:
7-Keto DHEA (7-Keto, 3-acetyl-7-oxo-DHEA) — DHEA and Adrenal

7-Keto DHEA is a naturally occurring metabolite of DHEA that does not convert to testosterone or estrogen — giving it DHEA's metabolic and immune benefits without androgenic or estrogenic side effects. Research demonstrates it increases resting metabolic rate by activating thermogenic enzymes, enhances immune function by restoring declining thymic hormones, and improves body composition. Clinical trials show 7-Keto DHEA supplementation leads to significantly greater fat loss than placebo when combined with exercise. Ideal for individuals who want metabolic DHEA benefits without hormonal conversion concerns.

Reported benefits:
• Does not convert to testosterone or estrogen — no hormonal sides
• Increases resting metabolic rate by 1-2%
• Thermogenic enzyme activation
• Immune enhancement — restores thymic hormones
• Improves body composition in clinical trials
• Safe for both men and women without hormonal monitoring

Risks and trade-offs:
• Less potent than DHEA for hormonal effects
• More expensive than standard DHEA
• Limited data compared to DHEA
• Not suitable as DHEA replacement for severe deficiency
• Still some adrenal effects
• Quality varies between brands

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Metabolic / Fat Loss: 100-200mg/day — Daily oral split AM and PM (12-16 weeks)
• Immune / Anti-aging: 50-100mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing)

Progression: 100mg twice daily with meals is the most studied dose. Effects are modest — best combined with exercise and diet optimization. Can be used long-term without hormonal cycling concerns.

Common protocols:
• Metabolic Optimization: 7-Keto DHEA 100mg 2x/day, DHEA 25mg/day AM, Testosterone TRT dose, Tirzepatide if GLP-1 desired

Monitoring: Metabolic markers (weight, body composition), thyroid function, DHEA-S. No testosterone or estrogen monitoring required.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement in US. Not FDA approved as drug. Considered safe with good tolerability profile.

entries.title: Metformin
entries.subtitle: Glucophage, Metformin HCl, Fortamet
entries.text:
Metformin (Glucophage, Metformin HCl, Fortamet) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Metformin is an FDA-approved biguanide for type 2 diabetes that has emerged as one of the most studied longevity compounds. Mechanism: activates AMPK (the master metabolic switch), reduces hepatic glucose production, improves insulin sensitivity, and — intriguingly — activates FOXO transcription factors associated with longevity. The TAME trial (Targeting Aging with Metformin) is the first FDA-approved trial of an aging intervention. Research through 2026 shows metformin reduces all-cause mortality, cancer incidence, cardiovascular events, and inflammatory markers in diabetics — and growing evidence suggests similar benefits in non-diabetics.

Reported benefits:
• Decades of safety data — most prescribed diabetes drug
• AMPK activation mimics caloric restriction and exercise
• Reduces all-cause mortality and cancer incidence
• Anti-inflammatory via multiple mechanisms
• Improves insulin sensitivity
• Inexpensive and widely available

Risks and trade-offs:
• GI side effects (nausea, diarrhea) — especially initially
• Reduces Vitamin B12 absorption — supplement required
• May blunt exercise adaptations (controversial — conflicting studies)
• Lactic acidosis risk (rare — primarily with renal impairment)
• Not FDA approved for longevity use
• Requires physician prescription

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Longevity / Off-label: 500-1000mg/day — Twice daily with meals (Ongoing)
• Metformin ER (preferred for GI tolerance): 500-2000mg/day — Once daily with evening meal (Ongoing)

Progression: Start at 500mg with dinner. Increase to 500mg twice daily after 2 weeks if tolerated. Extended-release (ER) formulation dramatically reduces GI side effects. Take with meals always. Supplement Vitamin B12 1000mcg/day.

Common protocols:
• Longevity / Metabolic Protocol: Metformin ER 500-1000mg/day, NMN 500-1000mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Vitamin B12 1000mcg/day (required), Vitamin D 5000IU/day

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, B12 levels annually (supplementation prevents deficiency), renal function (eGFR), lipid panel.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for type 2 diabetes. Off-label for longevity and metabolic optimization. Requires prescription.

entries.title: Berberine
entries.subtitle: Berberine HCl, BBR
entries.text:
Berberine (Berberine HCl, BBR) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Berberine is a plant alkaloid found in various herbs including Berberis. It is often called nature's Metformin for its similar AMPK-activating mechanism. Multiple meta-analyses demonstrate berberine significantly reduces fasting glucose, HbA1c, and LDL cholesterol — with head-to-head trials showing comparable efficacy to Metformin for glucose control. Additionally, berberine has antimicrobial properties, modulates gut microbiome composition favorably, and has emerging data in NASH and PCOS treatment. Available without prescription, making it accessible as a Metformin alternative or adjunct.

Reported benefits:
• Comparable glucose-lowering efficacy to Metformin in trials
• AMPK activation — same pathway as Metformin
• Improves LDL cholesterol significantly
• Gut microbiome modulation
• Antimicrobial properties
• Available without prescription

Risks and trade-offs:
• GI side effects similar to Metformin
• Lower bioavailability — take with meals
• Multiple daily doses required
• Drug interactions — inhibits CYP3A4
• Quality varies between supplements
• Less long-term safety data than Metformin

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard: 500mg 3x/day — Three times daily with meals (Ongoing)
• Metabolic / GLP-1 support: 500mg 2x/day — With main meals (Ongoing)

Progression: Take with meals — bioavailability improves significantly with food. Often cycled 8 weeks on / 4 weeks off to prevent gut microbiome adaptation. Pairs well with GLP-1 agents for enhanced metabolic effect.

Common protocols:
• Metabolic Stack: Berberine 500mg 3x/day with meals, NMN 500mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Semaglutide or Tirzepatide (complementary)

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipid panel, liver enzymes every 3-6 months.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement in US — no FDA drug approval. Well-studied with meta-analysis support for glucose and lipid management.

entries.title: Telmisartan
entries.subtitle: Micardis
entries.text:
Telmisartan (Micardis) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Telmisartan is an FDA-approved ARB (angiotensin receptor blocker) for hypertension that has gained attention in longevity and performance medicine for its unique off-target activity. Unlike other ARBs, Telmisartan is a partial PPAR-gamma agonist — the same receptor targeted by thiazolidinedione diabetes drugs — giving it insulin-sensitizing, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic effects beyond blood pressure control. Research shows it improves insulin sensitivity, reduces visceral fat, improves lipid profiles, and has cardioprotective effects. Used off-label in TRT contexts for cardiovascular protection — TRT can raise blood pressure and hematocrit, and Telmisartan addresses both concerns.

Reported benefits:
• PPAR-gamma agonism — metabolic benefits beyond blood pressure
• Insulin sensitizing — unique among ARBs
• Reduces visceral fat
• Cardioprotective — reduces major cardiovascular events
• Once daily dosing — 24-hour coverage
• Renoprotective effects

Risks and trade-offs:
• Prescription required
• Can cause hypotension — start low
• Hyperkalemia risk — monitor potassium
• Not for pregnancy
• May interact with lithium and NSAIDs
• Blood pressure monitoring required

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cardiovascular protection: 20-40mg/day — Once daily oral (Ongoing)
• Hypertension on TRT: 40-80mg/day — Once daily oral (Physician supervised)

Progression: Start at 20mg if using for metabolic benefits without hypertension. Monitor blood pressure. A good option for TRT patients with borderline-high blood pressure or elevated hematocrit.

Common protocols:
• TRT Cardiovascular Protection: Telmisartan 40mg/day, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, Omega-3 fatty acids 3-4g/day, Regular blood donation if hematocrit elevated

Monitoring: Blood pressure, potassium, renal function (eGFR, creatinine), hematocrit, fasting glucose, lipid panel.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for hypertension and cardiovascular risk reduction. Off-label for metabolic optimization and TRT support.

entries.title: Low-Dose Naltrexone
entries.subtitle: LDN
entries.text:
Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Low-dose naltrexone (LDN) is naltrexone — FDA-approved at 50mg for addiction — used at dramatically lower doses (1.5-4.5mg) to produce paradoxical immune modulation and anti-inflammatory effects. At low doses, the brief opioid receptor blockade upregulates endorphin production and modulates toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) on microglia — producing systemic anti-inflammatory effects. Research across multiple conditions (Multiple Sclerosis, Crohn's disease, fibromyalgia, chronic pain, cancers) shows LDN reduces inflammatory markers, pain, and disease activity. Growing use in functional medicine for autoimmune conditions, gut inflammation, and as part of longevity protocols.

Reported benefits:
• Potent immune modulation via TLR4 and endorphin upregulation
• Anti-inflammatory — broad applications
• Excellent safety profile at low doses
• Inexpensive — generic naltrexone compounded
• Evidence across multiple autoimmune and inflammatory conditions
• Improving sleep and mood reported

Risks and trade-offs:
• Vivid dreams initially — usually temporary
• Should not be taken within 4-6 hours of opioid pain medications
• Requires compounding pharmacy for low-dose formulations
• Limited large RCT data despite promising smaller studies
• Not FDA approved at low doses
• Takes 4-8 weeks for full effect

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting: 1.5mg at bedtime — Daily oral (2 weeks then increase)
• Therapeutic: 4.5mg at bedtime — Daily oral (Ongoing — months to years)

Progression: Start at 1.5mg and increase by 1.5mg every 2 weeks up to 4.5mg. Take at bedtime. If vivid dreams are problematic, move to morning dosing. Allow 4-8 weeks for full immune modulation effects.

Common protocols:
• Anti-inflammatory / Longevity: LDN 4.5mg at bedtime, BPC-157 250mcg/day (gut synergy), Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6), autoimmune markers if indicated, liver enzymes. Self-assessment of pain, energy, sleep quality.

Regulatory status: Naltrexone FDA approved at 50mg for addiction. Off-label compounded 1.5-4.5mg for immune modulation. Requires physician prescription.

entries.title: VIP
entries.subtitle: Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide
entries.text:
VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP) is a 28-amino acid neuropeptide with potent immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and vasodilatory effects. Originally identified for its effects on intestinal smooth muscle, research reveals VIP is one of the most powerful naturally occurring anti-inflammatory molecules known. Particularly relevant in functional medicine for MCAS (Mast Cell Activation Syndrome), mold illness (CIRS — Chronic Inflammatory Response Syndrome), POTS, and autoimmune gut conditions. The Shoemaker Protocol for CIRS uses VIP as a cornerstone treatment. Recent COVID-19 research has explored VIP for cytokine storm mitigation.

Reported benefits:
• Potent anti-inflammatory — reduces 50+ inflammatory mediators
• Mast cell stabilization — MCAS treatment
• Vasodilation and improved blood flow
• Neuroprotective effects
• Gut motility normalization
• Central to CIRS (mold illness) treatment protocol

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very short half-life — intranasal or inhaled dosing required
• Flushing and hypotension possible at higher doses
• Very expensive
• Limited availability — specialized compounding pharmacies
• Not FDA approved
• Should be used under physician guidance for CIRS

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• CIRS / MCAS (Intranasal): 50mcg 4x/day — Intranasal insufflation (Ongoing — as part of Shoemaker Protocol)
• Anti-inflammatory (Intranasal): 25-50mcg — Intranasal 2-4x daily (4-12 weeks)
• Anti-inflammatory (SubQ): 25-50mcg — Subcutaneous injection 1-2x daily (4-12 weeks — research use)

Progression: Best used under physician guidance — particularly for CIRS where it is a late-stage treatment after biotoxin and inflammatory burden has been reduced. For MCAS, start at lower doses and titrate based on tolerance.

Common protocols:
• Inflammatory / CIRS Protocol: VIP 50mcg intranasal 4x/day, BPC-157 500mcg/day (gut support), LDN 4.5mg at bedtime, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (TGF-beta1, C4a, MMP-9 for CIRS), MSH (melanocyte stimulating hormone), VIP levels if testable, blood pressure.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Compounded from specialized pharmacies. Cornerstone of Shoemaker CIRS protocol.

entries.title: Insulin
entries.subtitle: Humulin R, Novolin R, regular human insulin, insulin lispro, aspart, glargine
entries.text:
Insulin (Humulin R, Novolin R, regular human insulin, insulin lispro, aspart, glargine) — Metabolic and Cardiovascular

Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that moves glucose, amino acids and potassium out of the blood and into cells. Injected insulin is FDA-approved, life-sustaining therapy for type 1 diabetes and is widely used in type 2, and it has been in clinical use since 1922 — no hormone is better characterised. It is also used off-label in bodybuilding for nutrient partitioning and glycogen loading, usually alongside growth hormone. That use has no controlled evidence of benefit in people who are not diabetic, and it carries a failure mode nothing else in this reference shares: hypoglycaemia develops within minutes to hours, progresses through confusion to seizure and coma, and cannot be self-treated once consciousness is gone. Deaths and permanent hypoglycaemic brain injury in bodybuilders are documented in the case-report literature. This entry exists so the risk is legible. It is not a protocol and it carries no performance dose.

Reported benefits:
• Life-sustaining, FDA-approved therapy for type 1 diabetes
• In clinical use since 1922 — the best-characterised hormone in medicine
• Effect is directly measurable: glucose can be checked in seconds
• Continuous glucose monitoring has transformed the safety of prescribed use
• Modern analogues separate basal from mealtime coverage and titrate independently
• Inexpensive relative to almost every other hormone therapy

Risks and trade-offs:
• Hypoglycaemia is the failure mode and it can be fatal within an hour
• No self-rescue once consciousness is lost — someone else has to act
• No controlled evidence of performance or body-composition benefit in non-diabetics
• Deaths and permanent brain injury in bodybuilders are documented in case reports
• The margin narrows with a missed meal, alcohol, heat, cardio or a hot shower
• Drives potassium into cells — hypokalaemia is a second, quieter failure mode
• Promotes fat storage as readily as glycogen storage
• Sustained high exposure is associated with worsening insulin resistance

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Type 1 diabetes (FDA-approved use): Individualised by a prescriber — Basal plus mealtime, or pump, per the product label (Lifelong)
• Type 2 diabetes (FDA-approved use): Individualised by a prescriber — Usually basal first, added to oral agents (Ongoing)
• Performance and body-composition use: No dose is published here — Not an approved use; no controlled evidence of benefit (See the drawbacks — this is the entry where a wrong number kills)

Progression: Prescribed insulin is titrated by a clinician against measured glucose: an estimate from body weight and current control, then weeks of adjustment against readings. That is why no number appears above — the dose is an output of measurement, not something picked off a table. If insulin is in your protocol for any reason, the safety system is the boring part and it is the whole thing: glucose checked before and after each dose and again before sleep, a continuous monitor if you can get one, fast-acting carbohydrate within arm’s reach every single time, and someone nearby who knows what you have taken and what a hypo looks like. Alcohol, a missed meal, unplanned cardio and a hot shower all deepen the same drop. Anyone considering insulin without a diabetes diagnosis should have that conversation with a doctor first: the downside here is not a side effect, it is not waking up.

Monitoring: Blood glucose before and after each dose and before sleep — a continuous glucose monitor is the only monitoring that works while you are asleep. HbA1c, potassium (insulin drives it intracellularly), renal function, lipids and weight. Fasting insulin and C-peptide if the question is your own production.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for diabetes mellitus; on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines. Regular human insulin (Humulin R, Novolin R) is sold without a prescription in most US states; the rapid- and long-acting analogues require one. No approval and no controlled evidence for performance, body-composition or anti-ageing use.

entries.title: Rapamycin
entries.subtitle: Sirolimus, Rapamune, mTOR inhibitor
entries.text:
Rapamycin (Sirolimus, Rapamune, mTOR inhibitor) — Longevity Compounds

Rapamycin is an FDA-approved immunosuppressant (for organ transplant rejection) that has emerged as arguably the most promising longevity compound in current research. It inhibits mTOR (mechanistic Target of Rapamycin) — a master regulator of cellular growth, metabolism, and aging. mTOR inhibition mimics caloric restriction at the cellular level and consistently extends lifespan in every organism studied, including mice where it extended lifespan even when started in old age. The Dog Aging Project is currently testing rapamycin in dogs with compelling preliminary results. Human longevity trials (PEARL trial) are ongoing. Used intermittently (weekly dosing) in longevity medicine to minimize immunosuppressive effects while preserving anti-aging benefits.

Reported benefits:
• Strongest longevity evidence of any compound — lifespan extension in every model tested
• Extends lifespan even when started in old age (mice)
• Inhibits mTOR — mimics caloric restriction
• Reduces multiple aging hallmarks simultaneously
• Autophagy enhancement — cellular cleanup
• Weekly dosing minimizes immunosuppression
• Extends lifespan in all organisms tested
• Promotes autophagy and cellular cleanup
• Reduces senescent cell burden
• Immune system rejuvenation data in humans
• mTORC1 selective at pulsed low doses
• Most evidence-backed longevity intervention

Risks and trade-offs:
• FDA approved only as immunosuppressant — off-label longevity use
• Immunosuppression at higher doses — infection risk
• Wound healing impairment at therapeutic doses
• Mouth sores (aphthous ulcers) common
• Lipid elevation in some users
• Requires physician oversight — not OTC
• Immunosuppression at transplant doses
• Impairs wound healing
• Elevated triglycerides
• Must be physician prescribed and supervised
• Significant drug interactions
• Long-term longevity use safety data still emerging

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Longevity (intermittent): 5-10mg once weekly — Weekly oral fasted (Ongoing — reassess every 6 months)
• Conservative start: 2-5mg once weekly — Weekly oral (3 months then reassess)
• Medical (transplant): Daily dosing — Physician directed (Ongoing — different protocol)
• Longevity Protocol: 2–6mg — Oral weekly, fasted (Ongoing with physician supervision)
• Conservative Start: 1–2mg — Oral weekly (3 months, then reassess)

Progression: Longevity dosing is weekly, not daily — this is critical. Daily dosing causes immunosuppression. Weekly pulsing maintains mTOR inhibition benefits while allowing immune recovery. Start at 5mg weekly. Some practitioners cycle 3 months on / 1 month off.

Common protocols:
• Core Longevity Stack: Rapamycin 5-10mg once weekly, Metformin 500mg/day (complementary AMPK + mTOR), NMN 1000mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, Vitamin D 5000IU/day
• Advanced Anti-aging: Rapamycin 6mg weekly, Acarbose 50mg with main meals (synergistic in ITP mouse studies), Metformin 500mg/day, Epithalon pulse cycles
• Longevity Core Stack: Rapamycin 5–6mg weekly (physician supervised), Metformin 500–1000mg/day, NMN 1g/day, Urolithin A 1g/day
• mTOR Cycling: Rapamycin 5mg weekly, 16:8 intermittent fasting, Resistance training 3x/week, Adequate protein 1.6g/kg/day

Monitoring: Fasting glucose (mTOR affects insulin sensitivity), lipid panel, CBC (infection monitoring), wound healing assessment, mouth sore tracking. Physician oversight required.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED as Rapamune for transplant rejection. Off-label weekly longevity dosing. Requires physician prescription.

entries.title: Acarbose
entries.subtitle: Precose, Glucobay, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor
entries.text:
Acarbose (Precose, Glucobay, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) — Longevity Compounds

Acarbose is an FDA-approved alpha-glucosidase inhibitor for type 2 diabetes that reduces post-meal glucose spikes by slowing carbohydrate digestion. Its longevity relevance comes from the ITP (Interventions Testing Program) — the gold-standard NIA mouse longevity study — where acarbose significantly extended male mouse lifespan (by 22% in males). When combined with rapamycin in ITP studies, the combination showed greater lifespan extension than either alone. Mechanistically, reducing glucose spikes reduces glycation, oxidative stress, and chronic inflammation — all major aging drivers. Low-dose use at meals is well-tolerated.

Reported benefits:
• ITP mouse lifespan extension — 22% in males
• Synergistic with rapamycin in longevity studies
• Reduces post-meal glucose spikes significantly
• Reduces glycation and oxidative stress
• Low systemic absorption — primarily gut-level action
• Well-tolerated at low doses
• Reduces postprandial glucose spikes
• Extended lifespan in ITP mouse studies
• No hypoglycemia risk as monotherapy
• Improves gut microbiome composition
• Reduces advanced glycation end products
• Additive with metformin for longevity

Risks and trade-offs:
• GI side effects — flatulence and bloating (reduced carb fermentation)
• Must be taken with first bite of each meal
• Less effective on low-carb diets (less substrate to slow)
• Not a dramatic effect in isolation
• Requires prescription
• GI side effects limit dose escalation
• GI side effects (gas, bloating) especially initially
• Must be taken with first bite of meal — timing critical
• Reduces absorption of some medications
• Not useful without carbohydrate intake
• Uncomfortable GI effects at higher doses

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Longevity / Metabolic: 25-50mg with each main meal — 3x daily with first bite of meals (Ongoing)
• Diabetes (medical): 50-100mg 3x daily — With meals (Ongoing)
• Starting: 25mg — Oral with first bite of carb meals (2–4 weeks then titrate)
• Therapeutic: 50–100mg — Oral with first bite of each main meal (Ongoing)

Progression: Take with the very first bite of each carbohydrate-containing meal — timing is critical. Start at 25mg per meal and increase to 50mg if GI tolerance allows. Works best in context of moderate-carb diet.

Common protocols:
• Longevity / Metabolic: Acarbose 50mg with each meal, Rapamycin 6mg weekly (synergistic per ITP), Metformin 500mg/day, Berberine 500mg with meals
• Longevity Metabolic Stack: Acarbose 50–100mg with meals, Metformin 500mg 2x/day, Berberine 500mg 2x/day, NMN 1g/day
• Glucose Control: Acarbose 100mg with main meals, CGM monitoring, Low glycemic index diet

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, liver enzymes (elevated rarely). GI symptom tracking especially first 4-6 weeks.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for type 2 diabetes. Off-label longevity use based on ITP animal data. Requires prescription.

entries.title: Resveratrol / Pterostilbene
entries.subtitle: Trans-resveratrol, RSV, pterostilbene
entries.text:
Resveratrol / Pterostilbene (Trans-resveratrol, RSV, pterostilbene) — Longevity Compounds

Resveratrol is a polyphenol found in red wine and grapes that gained fame through David Sinclair's sirtuin research at Harvard. It activates SIRT1 (a longevity-associated sirtuin protein) and mimics some effects of caloric restriction. Pterostilbene is a closely related compound with superior bioavailability (~80% vs ~20% for resveratrol) and longer half-life. Both activate AMPK, have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and improve insulin sensitivity in research. While the dramatic early results in yeast and flies have proven harder to replicate in mammals, both remain popular in longevity stacks for their broad safety profile and complementary sirtuin-activating mechanism alongside NMN.

Reported benefits:
• Sirtuin activation — SIRT1 and SIRT2
• AMPK activation — metabolic benefits
• Anti-inflammatory and antioxidant
• Pterostilbene has superior bioavailability vs resveratrol
• Improves insulin sensitivity
• Synergistic with NMN (both support NAD+ pathways)

Risks and trade-offs:
• Bioavailability issues with resveratrol — take with fat
• Mammalian longevity data much weaker than yeast/fly data
• Very high doses may have pro-oxidant effects
• Estrogenic activity at high doses
• Better replaced by pterostilbene in most protocols
• Limited robust human RCT data

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Resveratrol: 250-500mg/day — Daily oral with fatty meal (Ongoing)
• Pterostilbene (preferred): 50-150mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing)

Progression: Pterostilbene is strongly preferred over resveratrol due to superior bioavailability. Take with a fatty meal (both are fat-soluble). Often stacked with NMN — they support overlapping NAD+/sirtuin pathways.

Common protocols:
• Sirtuin / NAD+ Stack: Pterostilbene 100mg/day, NMN 1000mg/day AM, TMG 500mg/day (methyl donor), Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: No specific labs required. General health panel. Liver enzymes if using high doses long-term.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Pterostilbene available OTC. Well-established safety profile.

entries.title: Argireline / Snap-8
entries.subtitle: Acetyl hexapeptide-3, Acetyl octapeptide-3
entries.text:
Argireline / Snap-8 (Acetyl hexapeptide-3, Acetyl octapeptide-3) — Collagen and Skin Peptides

Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3) and Snap-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3) are synthetic peptide analogues of the N-terminal end of SNAP-25, a protein involved in neuromuscular junction signaling. They competitively inhibit the SNARE complex formation required for acetylcholine release, reducing muscle contraction at injection/application sites — essentially a topical botox-like mechanism without injections. Research demonstrates measurable reduction in wrinkle depth with topical application, particularly around the eyes and forehead. Widely used in cosmeceuticals. SubQ injection versions explored in biohacking communities for localized effect.

Reported benefits:
• Topical botox-like mechanism without needles
• Measurable wrinkle depth reduction in clinical studies
• Snap-8 is more potent than Argireline
• No systemic effects with topical use
• Can be combined with other skin peptides
• Well-established cosmeceutical safety profile

Risks and trade-offs:
• Effects require consistent daily application
• Weaker than actual botulinum toxin
• Results take 4-8 weeks to become apparent
• SubQ injection data very limited
• Topical penetration limited without proper formulation
• Not FDA approved as a drug — cosmetic ingredient

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Topical: Apply to target areas — Once or twice daily after cleansing (Ongoing — minimum 8 weeks to assess)
• SubQ (experimental): 50-100mcg — Intradermal near target area (Research context only)

Progression: Topical application to clean dry skin. Look for formulations with 5-10% concentration for best effect. Combine with GHK-Cu and collagen peptides for comprehensive skin protocol.

Common protocols:
• Anti-aging Skin Stack: Argireline/Snap-8 topical 2x/day, GHK-Cu topical or SubQ 1-2mg/day, Collagen peptides 10-15g/day oral, Vitamin C 1000mg/day (collagen cofactor)

Monitoring: Visual assessment — photograph skin at baseline and every 4 weeks. No blood monitoring required.

Regulatory status: Cosmetic ingredient — no FDA drug approval. Widely used in skincare products.

entries.title: Collagen Peptides
entries.subtitle: Hydrolyzed collagen, collagen hydrolysate, types I/II/III
entries.text:
Collagen Peptides (Hydrolyzed collagen, collagen hydrolysate, types I/II/III) — Collagen and Skin Peptides

Collagen peptides are hydrolyzed collagen proteins broken into short amino acid chains (primarily glycine, proline, hydroxyproline) that are absorbed intact and stimulate fibroblast collagen production. Multiple randomized controlled trials demonstrate oral collagen peptides improve skin elasticity, reduce wrinkle depth, increase skin hydration, and support joint health. Research (2020-2026) confirms serum collagen peptides stimulate dermal collagen synthesis. Also relevant for tendon and joint health — type II collagen peptides specifically support cartilage matrix synthesis. One of the better-evidenced oral beauty supplements.

Reported benefits:
• Multiple RCTs showing skin elasticity and wrinkle improvements
• Joint and tendon health support
• Type II collagen specifically supports cartilage
• Stimulates fibroblast collagen synthesis
• Well-tolerated — essentially food protein
• Synergistic with Vitamin C (required for collagen synthesis)

Risks and trade-offs:
• Effects require 8-12 weeks minimum
• Quality varies — look for hydrolyzed with specific dalton weight
• Not vegan — animal-derived
• Higher doses needed for joint vs skin benefits
• Results are modest and gradual
• Best results with consistent long-term use

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Skin health: 10g/day — Daily oral — can mix in any liquid (Minimum 8 weeks)
• Joint health: 15-40g/day — Daily oral (Minimum 12 weeks)
• Type II collagen (joint): 10-40mg/day — Daily oral fasted (90 days minimum)

Progression: Take with Vitamin C for optimal collagen synthesis — Vitamin C is a required cofactor. Undenatured type II collagen (UC-II) is taken at much lower doses (10-40mg) than hydrolyzed collagen (10-40g). Mix hydrolyzed collagen into morning coffee, smoothie, or any liquid.

Common protocols:
• Joint and Skin Protocol: Collagen peptides 15g/day, Vitamin C 1000mg/day (cofactor), GHK-Cu topical, BPC-157 250mcg/day (tissue repair synergy)

Monitoring: Skin and joint symptom self-assessment. No blood monitoring needed.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Well-evidenced by clinical trial data.

entries.title: GHK-Cu
entries.subtitle: Copper Peptide, Glycyl-L-Histidyl-L-Lysine, GHK-Copper, GHK-Cu (Copper Peptide)
entries.text:
GHK-Cu (Copper Peptide, Glycyl-L-Histidyl-L-Lysine, GHK-Copper, GHK-Cu (Copper Peptide)) — Additional Peptides

GHK-Cu is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide found in human plasma, saliva, and urine. Levels decline significantly with age. Research by Loren Pickart spanning 40+ years demonstrates remarkable biological activity: wound healing, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, collagen production stimulation, hair follicle stimulation, and nerve regeneration. More recently, genome studies show GHK-Cu resets thousands of genes toward a younger expression pattern. Topical application for skin and hair is well established. Systemic SubQ use for anti-aging, injury healing, and tissue regeneration is an emerging application.

Reported benefits:
• Naturally occurring — excellent safety profile
• Stimulates collagen and elastin production
• Promotes hair follicle activation and growth
• Wound healing and tissue regeneration
• Anti-inflammatory and antioxidant
• Gene expression reset toward youthful patterns in research
• Extremely broad tissue repair effects
• Stimulates collagen and elastin
• Hair follicle regeneration
• Excellent safety profile
• Available topical and injectable

Risks and trade-offs:
• Topical vs systemic absorption debate ongoing
• SubQ injection data limited compared to topical
• Copper accumulation theoretically possible at very high doses
• Sourcing quality varies
• Mechanism fully characterized only in vitro and animal models
• Long-term systemic safety not established
• Multiple administration routes can be confusing
• Quality control varies widely by source
• Research mostly in vitro or animal models
• Not FDA approved
• Optimal dosing protocols still being established

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Topical (skin/hair): Apply to target area — 1-2x daily (Ongoing)
• SubQ systemic: 1-2mg/day — Daily SubQ (4-8 weeks on / 4 weeks off)
• Subcutaneous: 1–2mg/day — SubQ injection (1–3 months)
• Intranasal: 100–200mcg/day — Nasal spray (Ongoing)
• Topical: As directed — Topical cream/serum (Ongoing)

Progression: Topical is the most established route with the most evidence. For systemic SubQ use, 1mg/day is a starting point. Often cycled to prevent potential copper accumulation. Stack with BPC-157 for synergistic tissue healing.

Common protocols:
• Anti-aging / Tissue Repair: GHK-Cu 2mg/day SubQ or topical, BPC-157 250mcg/day, Testosterone TRT dose, NMN 500mg/day
• Longevity Stack: GHK-Cu 1mg/day SubQ, Epithalon 5mg/day (cycled), NMN 500mg/day, BPC-157 250mcg/day
• Skin and Hair: GHK-Cu topical 2x/day, GHK-Cu 1mg SubQ/day, Biotin 5mg/day

Monitoring: General health markers. Copper levels with extended high-dose use. Hair and skin photographic documentation.

Regulatory status: Topical use is cosmetic/OTC. Systemic SubQ use is research only — no FDA approval.

entries.title: Cerebrolysin
entries.subtitle: FPF-1070, CERE
entries.text:
Cerebrolysin (FPF-1070, CERE) — Neurological and Cognitive

Cerebrolysin is a porcine brain-derived peptide mixture containing neurotrophic factors including BDNF, NGF, CNTF, and GDNF in concentrated form. Approved as a drug in over 50 countries for stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), Alzheimer's disease, and vascular dementia. Extensive clinical trial data — over 130 clinical studies — demonstrate neuroprotection, neuroplasticity enhancement, synaptic density improvement, and cognitive enhancement. Used in biohacking communities for cognitive optimization. Considered one of the most potent and evidence-backed nootropic peptide preparations available, though IV or IM injection is required for systemic effect.

Reported benefits:
• Over 130 clinical studies — extensive evidence base
• Approved drug in 50+ countries for neurological conditions
• Contains multiple neurotrophic factors (BDNF, NGF, CNTF, GDNF)
• Neuroprotective and neuroplastic simultaneously
• Cognitive enhancement in healthy individuals reported
• TBI and stroke recovery — robust evidence

Risks and trade-offs:
• Injection only — IM or IV (no oral bioavailability)
• Porcine brain derived — not suitable for some
• Requires sourcing from countries where it's approved
• Not FDA approved in the United States
• Expensive per ampoule
• Rare allergic reactions possible — test dose recommended

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cognitive Enhancement: 5-10ml IM or slow IV — Daily for 10-20 days, 2-4 cycles per year (10-20 day cycles)
• TBI/Stroke Recovery: 10-30ml IV infusion — Daily — physician supervised (4-6 weeks)
• Micro-dosing: 1-2ml IM — Every other day (4-6 weeks)

Progression: Test dose of 1ml first to rule out allergy. Classic protocol is 10-20 day cycles with breaks between. IV is more effective than IM but requires clinical setting. Many biohackers use IM injection at home with smaller doses.

Common protocols:
• Cognitive Enhancement Stack: Cerebrolysin 5ml IM daily x 10 days, Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, Selank 500mcg intranasal PM, BPC-157 250mcg/day (neuroprotective support)

Monitoring: Cognitive self-assessment (memory, focus, processing speed). Mood tracking. No specific blood monitoring needed.

Regulatory status: Approved drug in 50+ countries (EU, Russia, China, etc). NOT FDA approved in the US. Must be sourced internationally or through specialty compounding.

entries.title: NAC / NALT
entries.subtitle: N-Acetyl Cysteine, N-Acetyl L-Tyrosine, NAC
entries.text:
NAC / NALT (N-Acetyl Cysteine, N-Acetyl L-Tyrosine, NAC) — Neurological and Cognitive

N-Acetyl Cysteine (NAC) is a precursor to glutathione — the body's master antioxidant — and has broad therapeutic applications including liver protection, lung health, psychiatric conditions, and addiction treatment. FDA has attempted to restrict it as a supplement due to its IND history, but it remains widely available. N-Acetyl L-Tyrosine (NALT) is a bioavailable form of L-tyrosine — precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and thyroid hormones. Together they support antioxidant defense, neurotransmitter synthesis, and cognitive performance under stress. Both are widely used as performance and recovery adjuncts in hormone optimization protocols.

Reported benefits:
• NAC: glutathione precursor — master antioxidant support
• NAC: liver protection (especially valuable on oral AAS)
• NALT: dopamine and norepinephrine precursor
• NALT: cognitive performance under stress
• Both: excellent safety profiles
• Well-studied with decades of clinical use

Risks and trade-offs:
• NAC: FDA regulatory uncertainty as supplement in US
• NALT: requires adequate cofactors (B6, iron, folate)
• NAC: can cause nausea at higher doses
• NALT: best taken away from protein-rich meals
• Individual response varies significantly
• NAC may reduce efficacy of some chemotherapy drugs

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• NAC: 600-1800mg/day — Daily oral split 2-3x (Ongoing — cycle 8 weeks on/4 off if desired)
• NALT: 300-500mg — Daily oral AM fasted (Ongoing or as needed)

Progression: NAC is best taken with food to minimize nausea. NALT best taken fasted in AM for cognitive benefit. Both are excellent adjuncts to TRT and peptide protocols — NAC particularly valuable if using any hepatotoxic compounds.

Common protocols:
• Antioxidant and Cognitive Support: NAC 600mg 2x/day, NALT 300mg AM fasted, Vitamin C 1000mg/day, Alpha-lipoic acid 300mg/day

Monitoring: Liver enzymes (especially if on oral AAS — NAC is hepatoprotective). General wellness tracking.

Regulatory status: NAC: OTC supplement (regulatory status in flux in US). NALT: dietary supplement. Both widely available.

entries.title: Selank
entries.subtitle: TP-7
entries.text:
Selank (TP-7) — Nootropics and Longevity

Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide analogue of the immune peptide tuftsin, developed by the Institute of Molecular Genetics in Russia and approved in Russia for anxiety and asthenic conditions. It modulates GABA-A receptors, increases BDNF, and affects serotonin and dopamine metabolism. Uniquely, it provides anxiolytic effects without sedation, cognitive impairment, or addiction potential — a profile distinct from benzodiazepines. Research demonstrates improvements in memory consolidation, learning, and anxiety reduction. Administered intranasally for rapid CNS penetration.

Reported benefits:
• Anxiolytic without sedation or addiction
• Increases BDNF — supports neuroplasticity
• Improves memory consolidation and recall
• Immune modulation via tuftsin analogue mechanism
• No withdrawal — non-habit forming
• Rapid onset via intranasal administration
• Anxiolytic without dependency or tolerance
• Cognitive enhancement
• Immune modulation
• BDNF upregulation
• Fast-acting intranasal administration
• No withdrawal symptoms

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited Western clinical trial data
• Intranasal route inconvenient for some
• Short half-life — multiple daily doses needed
• Some report nasal irritation
• Long-term effects not well established
• Not FDA approved
• Limited Western clinical trials
• Intranasal administration can cause nasal irritation
• Effects vary significantly by individual
• Source quality varies

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Anxiety / Cognitive (Intranasal): 250-500mcg — Intranasal 2-3x daily (2-4 weeks on / 2 weeks off)
• Anxiety / Cognitive (SubQ): 250-300mcg — Subcutaneous injection 1-2x daily (2-4 weeks on / 2 weeks off)
• Anxiolytic: 250–500mcg/dose — Intranasal, 2–3x/day (2–4 weeks as needed)
• Nootropic: 750–1500mcg/day — Intranasal, split doses (2–4 weeks on, 2 weeks off)

Progression: Use intranasally — absorbs rapidly through nasal mucosa. Works best when cycled 2 weeks on, 1-2 weeks off to prevent tolerance. Often stacked with Semax for comprehensive nootropic effect.

Common protocols:
• Cognitive / Anxiety Stack: Selank 500mcg intranasal 2x/day, Semax 300mcg intranasal AM, BPC-157 250mcg/day for gut-brain axis
• Anxiety and Focus: Selank 500mcg 2x/day, Semax 300mcg AM, Magnesium l-threonate 144mg/day
• Cognitive Stack: Selank 500mcg AM/PM, NAD+ 500mg/day, GHK-Cu intranasal 100mcg/day

Monitoring: Mood and cognitive self-assessment. No specific blood monitoring required.

Regulatory status: Approved drug in Russia for anxiety and asthenic conditions. Research compound in Western countries.

entries.title: Semax
entries.subtitle: ACTH(4-7)PGP, Heptapeptide
entries.text:
Semax (ACTH(4-7)PGP, Heptapeptide) — Nootropics and Longevity

Semax is a synthetic analogue of ACTH(4-7) developed in Russia, where it is approved for stroke, TBI, cognitive impairment, and optic nerve diseases. It dramatically increases BDNF, NGF, and BDNF mRNA expression — making it one of the most potent BDNF upregulators known. Research demonstrates neuroprotection, enhanced learning and memory, mood stabilization, and executive function improvements. Used clinically in Russia for decades with an excellent safety record. Particularly effective for cognitive enhancement and post-injury brain recovery. Administered intranasally.

Reported benefits:
• Potent BDNF and NGF upregulation
• Approved drug in Russia with decades of clinical use
• Neuroprotective — used for stroke and TBI recovery
• Improves focus, memory, and executive function
• No significant side effects reported in clinical literature
• Rapid onset intranasally
• Neuroprotective after stroke or injury
• Improves focus and working memory
• Anti-inflammatory in the CNS
• Fast-acting intranasal delivery
• No dependency reported

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited Western RCT data
• Intranasal administration only for CNS effects
• Anxiety or stimulant-like effect in some users
• Short half-life
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing quality control varies
• Stimulating — can cause anxiety at high doses
• Vivid dreams reported
• Intranasal irritation
• Source quality variable

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cognitive Enhancement (Intranasal): 300-900mcg — Intranasal once daily AM (2-4 weeks on / 1 week off)
• Cognitive Enhancement (SubQ): 250-600mcg — Subcutaneous injection once daily AM (2-4 weeks on / 1 week off)
• Neuroprotection / Recovery: 600-1800mcg — Intranasal 2x daily — or 300-750mcg SubQ 2x daily (As needed)
• Nootropic: 200–600mcg/day — Intranasal, AM (2–4 weeks on, 2 weeks off)
• Neuroprotective: 600–900mcg/day — Intranasal, 2x/day (2–4 weeks)

Progression: Start at 300mcg AM dose. Some users find it activating — avoid evening doses if sleep affected. Stack with Selank for anxiety and cognition together. Cycle to maintain sensitivity.

Common protocols:
• Cognitive / Performance: Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, Selank 500mcg intranasal (midday/PM), BPC-157 250mcg/day (gut-brain axis)
• Focus Stack: Semax 300mcg AM, Selank 500mcg PM, NAD+ 500mg/day
• Neuroprotection: Semax 600mcg 2x/day, GHK-Cu 1mg/day, NMN 1g/day
