Monitoring: Cognitive performance tracking. No bloodwork required. Monitor mood and sleep quality.

Regulatory status: Approved drug in Russia for stroke and cognitive impairment. Research compound in Western countries.

entries.title: Follistatin
entries.subtitle: FS-344, FST-344, myostatin inhibitor
entries.text:
Follistatin (FS-344, FST-344, myostatin inhibitor) — Muscle and Myostatin

Follistatin is a naturally occurring glycoprotein that binds and inhibits myostatin (GDF-8) and activin — negative regulators of muscle growth. By blocking myostatin, follistatin allows greater muscle fiber hypertrophy and satellite cell activation. Research in animals shows dramatic muscle mass increases with follistatin overexpression. Gene therapy approaches using follistatin are in clinical trials for muscular dystrophy. Recombinant follistatin peptides are used in the biohacking community for muscle growth enhancement. One of the most direct anabolic mechanisms available outside traditional androgens — works via a completely different pathway than testosterone.

Reported benefits:
• Directly inhibits myostatin — the brake on muscle growth
• Works via completely different pathway than androgens
• No androgenic side effects or HPTA suppression
• Potential for synergistic effect alongside testosterone
• Gene therapy applications in muscular dystrophy trials
• May improve insulin sensitivity

Risks and trade-offs:
• Very limited human peptide injection data
• Expensive and difficult to source with verified purity
• Long-term safety completely unknown
• Cancer risk concern — myostatin inhibition could affect tumor suppression
• Optimal dosing not established
• Mechanisms complex — systemic effects uncertain

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Research protocol: 100mcg/day — SubQ daily (2-4 week cycles with breaks)

Progression: Very early research compound for human use. Start at lowest dose. Given the theoretical cancer risk from myostatin inhibition, cycle with significant breaks. Do not use concurrently with other strongly anabolic compounds without careful consideration.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Muscle Building: Follistatin 100mcg/day (with caution), Testosterone Cypionate TRT or performance dose, BPC-157 for connective tissue support, IGF-1 LR3 (if using — monitor glucose)

Monitoring: Body composition tracking, liver enzymes, general cancer screening awareness, CBC.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Gene therapy versions in clinical trials for muscular dystrophy. Extreme caution warranted.

entries.title: Cardiogen
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp, KEDW tetrapeptide
entries.text:
Cardiogen (Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp, KEDW tetrapeptide) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Cardiogen is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp) developed by Vladimir Khavinson as a cardioprotective bioregulator targeting cardiac muscle cells. Research demonstrates it activates gene expression for cardiac proteins including alpha-myosin heavy chain, protects cardiomyocytes from apoptosis under ischemic conditions, and improves cardiac function metrics in aging. Studies show heart rate variability improvement and reduced markers of cardiac aging. Distinct from Cortagen (which targets vasculature) — Cardiogen specifically targets the myocardium. Used in longevity protocols alongside Epithalon and Thymalin.

Reported benefits:
• Directly targets cardiomyocyte gene expression
• Protects cardiac cells from ischemia-reperfusion injury
• Improves heart rate variability
• Reduces markers of cardiac aging
• Validated Khavinson research series
• Annual pulse cycling — convenient

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily from Russian literature
• Limited Western validation
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing very limited
• Best effects over 40 with cardiac aging
• Subtle effects in young healthy individuals

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Cardiac / Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use as 10-day pulse cycles alongside other Khavinson peptides. Most relevant for individuals over 45 with cardiovascular aging concerns. Often combined with Epithalon and Thymalin in the same cycle.

Common protocols:
• Cardiac Longevity: Cardiogen 10mg/day x 10 days, Epithalon 10mg/day x 10 days (concurrent), Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: HRV monitoring, lipid panel, blood pressure, BNP if cardiac function concern.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical research and longevity medicine.

entries.title: Ventfort
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu-Asp, KED tripeptide, vascular bioregulator
entries.text:
Ventfort (Lys-Glu-Asp, KED tripeptide, vascular bioregulator) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Ventfort is a synthetic tripeptide (Lys-Glu-Asp) developed by Khavinson as a vascular bioregulator targeting vascular endothelium. Research demonstrates it normalizes vascular tone, improves endothelial function, reduces lipid peroxidation in vessel walls, and supports smooth muscle cell health. Studies show improvements in blood flow parameters and microcirculation in aging individuals. Particularly relevant as a complement to cardiovascular TRT management — testosterone therapy can affect vascular tone, and Ventfort supports endothelial health directly.

Reported benefits:
• Targets vascular endothelium specifically
• Normalizes vascular tone and blood flow
• Reduces lipid peroxidation in vessel walls
• Improves microcirculation
• Synergistic with Cardiogen for comprehensive cardiovascular support
• Annual pulse cycling

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily Russian literature
• Limited Western validation
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing limited
• Subtle effects requiring long-term use
• Best effects in those with vascular aging

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Vascular / Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use alongside Cardiogen for comprehensive cardiovascular longevity. 10-day pulse cycles twice yearly. Can be administered concurrently with other Khavinson peptides.

Common protocols:
• Cardiovascular Longevity: Ventfort 10mg/day x 10 days, Cardiogen 10mg/day x 10 days, Cortagen 10mg/day x 10 days, Telmisartan 40mg/day (ongoing)

Monitoring: Blood pressure, HRV, lipid panel, inflammatory markers (CRP).

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical and longevity research.

entries.title: Sigumir
entries.subtitle: Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, AEDG tetrapeptide, cartilage bioregulator
entries.text:
Sigumir (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, AEDG tetrapeptide, cartilage bioregulator) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Sigumir is a synthetic tetrapeptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) developed by Khavinson targeting cartilage and bone. Research demonstrates it stimulates proteoglycan and collagen synthesis in cartilage, supports chondrocyte activity, improves joint function metrics in aging, and may slow cartilage degradation. Relevant for athletes, TRT patients experiencing joint issues (common with high-dose testosterone), and aging individuals with osteoarthritis. Complements BPC-157 and TB-500 for comprehensive joint health — where those peptides heal acute injury, Sigumir supports ongoing cartilage maintenance.

Reported benefits:
• Directly targets cartilage chondrocytes
• Stimulates proteoglycan and collagen synthesis
• Supports long-term joint health maintenance
• Complements BPC-157 for comprehensive joint support
• Annual pulse cycling
• Part of validated Khavinson series

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily Russian
• Limited Western validation
• Not FDA approved
• Long-term benefits require consistent cycling
• Sourcing limited
• Acute injury treatment better served by BPC-157

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Joint / Cartilage Maintenance: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2-4x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: For ongoing joint maintenance use 2 cycles per year. For active joint issues increase to 3-4 cycles per year. Combine with BPC-157 for acute injury and Sigumir for long-term cartilage maintenance.

Common protocols:
• Joint Health Stack: Sigumir 10mg/day x 10 days, BPC-157 500mcg/day (ongoing), Collagen peptides 15g/day, AOD-9604 500mcg/day (cartilage support)

Monitoring: Joint pain VAS scale, functional movement assessment, Vitamin D levels (critical for cartilage health).

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian sports medicine and longevity research.

entries.title: Chonluten
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu-Asp, bronchial/lung bioregulator
entries.text:
Chonluten (Lys-Glu-Asp, bronchial/lung bioregulator) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Chonluten is a synthetic tripeptide developed by Khavinson targeting bronchial epithelial cells and lung tissue. Research demonstrates it normalizes bronchial mucosa cell function, supports respiratory epithelium regeneration, reduces bronchial inflammation, and improves lung function parameters in aging. Particularly relevant for smokers, ex-smokers, individuals with chronic respiratory conditions, and those in occupational or environmental exposure situations. Also relevant in post-COVID lung recovery contexts where peptide therapy is being actively explored.

Reported benefits:
• Targets bronchial epithelium specifically
• Supports respiratory mucosa regeneration
• Reduces bronchial inflammation
• Improves lung function metrics in research
• Part of validated Khavinson series
• Relevant for post-COVID recovery

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily Russian
• Limited Western data
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing limited
• Best effects in those with respiratory aging or damage
• Subtle effects in healthy lungs

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Respiratory / Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use in spring and fall cycles alongside other Khavinson peptides. Most relevant for individuals with respiratory history or post-COVID lung involvement.

Common protocols:
• Respiratory Longevity: Chonluten 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Epithalon 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week (ongoing)

Monitoring: Spirometry if available, respiratory symptom tracking, inflammatory markers.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical and longevity research.

entries.title: Bonomarlot
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro, KEDP tetrapeptide, bone marrow bioregulator
entries.text:
Bonomarlot (Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro, KEDP tetrapeptide, bone marrow bioregulator) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Bonomarlot is a synthetic tetrapeptide developed by Khavinson targeting bone marrow hematopoietic cells. Research demonstrates it stimulates hematopoiesis (blood cell production), normalizes erythropoiesis, supports immune cell precursor production, and may help maintain bone marrow function in aging. Relevant for anyone experiencing hematocrit issues on TRT (both too high and too low), those with anemia, or individuals seeking comprehensive immune system optimization. Complements Thymalin (which targets mature T-cells) by supporting immune cell production at the source.

Reported benefits:
• Targets bone marrow hematopoietic cells directly
• Stimulates blood cell production
• Supports immune cell precursor production
• Relevant for TRT-related hematocrit management
• Complements Thymalin for comprehensive immune support
• Part of validated Khavinson series

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily Russian
• Limited Western validation
• Not FDA approved
• Complex interactions with hematopoiesis
• Sourcing very limited
• Blood count monitoring important

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Hematopoietic / Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use in annual cycles. Monitor CBC before and after to track hematopoietic response. Most relevant for individuals with sub-optimal blood counts or those managing high hematocrit on TRT.

Common protocols:
• Immune and Blood Support: Bonomarlot 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: CBC with differential (critical — tracks hematopoietic response), hematocrit, hemoglobin, platelet count.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical research.

entries.title: Crystagen
entries.subtitle: Lys-Glu-Asp-Gly, lymphocyte bioregulator
entries.text:
Crystagen (Lys-Glu-Asp-Gly, lymphocyte bioregulator) — Khavinson Bioregulators

Crystagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide developed by Khavinson targeting lymphocytes and the immune system. Research demonstrates it stimulates lymphocyte activation and proliferation, enhances T-helper cell function, improves cytokine production balance, and supports adaptive immunity restoration in aging. While Thymalin targets thymus function and T-cell maturation, Crystagen acts on mature lymphocytes directly — making them complementary for comprehensive immune optimization.

Reported benefits:
• Directly activates mature lymphocytes
• Enhances T-helper cell function
• Improves cytokine balance
• Complements Thymalin at different stage of immune cascade
• Part of Khavinson validated series
• Annual pulse cycling

Risks and trade-offs:
• Research primarily Russian
• Limited Western data
• Not FDA approved
• Sourcing very limited
• Theoretical autoimmune caution with existing autoimmune conditions
• Effects subtle in healthy individuals

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Immune / Longevity: 10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles)

Progression: Use as part of comprehensive Khavinson immune protocol. Can be cycled alongside Thymalin and Epithalon. Most significant effects in immunocompromised or aging individuals.

Common protocols:
• Complete Immune Longevity: Crystagen 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymalin 10mg/day x 10 days, Epithalon 10mg/day x 10 days, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week (ongoing)

Monitoring: CBC with differential, CD4/CD8 ratio if available, inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6).

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian clinical and longevity research.

entries.title: Epithalon
entries.subtitle: Epithalamin, Epitalon, Epithalone
entries.text:
Epithalon (Epithalamin, Epitalon, Epithalone) — Peptides

Synthetic tetrapeptide from pineal gland extract. Research by Khavinson (2003-2020) shows telomerase activation, extending telomere length and potentially cellular lifespan. Additional research: antioxidant properties, melatonin regulation, anti-cancer effects in animal studies. Used in longevity protocols as 10-day pulse cycles twice yearly.

Reported benefits:
• Activates telomerase — cellular longevity potential
• Antioxidant properties
• May regulate circadian rhythm and melatonin
• Anti-cancer effects in animal models
• Very low toxicity profile
• Unique mechanism among peptides
• Telomerase activation and telomere support
• Decades of clinical research
• Improves sleep via melatonin regulation
• Immune modulation
• Antioxidant and anti-tumor effects in studies
• Excellent safety profile

Risks and trade-offs:
• Most research from one research group (Khavinson)
• Needs independent replication
• Very limited long-term human data
• Mechanism translation to humans uncertain
• Not FDA approved
• Limited Western peer-reviewed data
• Primarily Russian research base
• Long-term effects in healthy subjects not fully established
• Requires injection or intranasal administration

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard Cycle: 5-10mg/day — SubQ daily for 10 days, 2x per year (10-day pulse cycles spring and fall)
• Extended: 5mg/day — 20-day cycle once or twice annually (As tolerated)
• Intranasal: 2–3mg/day — Nasal spray (10–20 days)

Progression: Standard protocol: 5–10mg subcutaneous daily for 10–20 days, repeated 1–2 times per year. Spring and fall cycles most common.

Common protocols:
• Longevity Protocol: Epithalon 5mg/day x 10 days 2x/year, Testosterone TRT dose, BPC-157 continuous low dose, Sermorelin + Ipamorelin pre-bed
• Sleep Optimization: Epithalon 5mg/night SubQ, DSIP 100mcg at bedtime, Magnesium glycinate 400mg

Monitoring: Telomere length testing (optional, expensive). General longevity panel. No mandatory monitoring.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Approved for clinical use in Russia.

entries.title: Retatrutide
entries.subtitle: LY3437943, triple G agonist
entries.text:
Retatrutide (LY3437943, triple G agonist) — Metabolic Peptides

Retatrutide is a triple agonist targeting GIP, GLP-1, AND glucagon receptors — the next generation beyond tirzepatide's dual mechanism. Phase II clinical trials (2023) demonstrated extraordinary weight loss outcomes: up to 24.2% body weight reduction at 48 weeks — exceeding even tirzepatide. The addition of glucagon receptor agonism increases energy expenditure and fat oxidation beyond what GLP-1/GIP alone can achieve. Currently in Phase III trials. Considered the most potent weight loss compound in development and likely to become best-in-class when approved.

Reported benefits:
• Up to 24.2% body weight loss in Phase II trials — best ever recorded
• Triple mechanism: GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon
• Glucagon agonism adds energy expenditure beyond GLP-1 alone
• Phase III trials ongoing — strong pipeline
• Once weekly dosing
• Strong cardiovascular outcome data expected

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not yet FDA approved — Phase III as of 2024
• All GLP-1 class side effects apply plus glucagon effects
• Muscle loss without testosterone and resistance training
• Nausea and GI effects potentially more pronounced than tirzepatide
• Long-term safety data still accumulating
• Not yet commercially available — research/clinical trial access only

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Phase II trial doses: 1-12mg/week — Weekly SubQ — titrated over months (Ongoing)
• Estimated clinical: Start 1-2mg/week, titrate — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing when approved)

Progression: Follow same titration approach as tirzepatide — slow titration minimizes GI side effects. Testosterone support for muscle preservation is even more critical given the superior fat loss potential. Protein intake minimum 1g/lb body weight.

Common protocols:
• Maximum Fat Loss: Retatrutide (per clinical protocol when available), Testosterone Cypionate 200mg/week (muscle preservation essential), CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin (GH support), Collagen peptides + resistance training

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, body composition monthly, weight weekly.

Regulatory status: Phase III clinical trials ongoing as of 2026. Not FDA approved. Expect approval 2025-2026.

entries.title: Cagrilintide
entries.subtitle: AM833, amylin analogue
entries.text:
Cagrilintide (AM833, amylin analogue) — Metabolic Peptides

Cagrilintide is a long-acting amylin analogue (amylin is a pancreatic hormone co-secreted with insulin). Amylin reduces food intake through central satiety signaling, slows gastric emptying, and suppresses post-meal glucagon. Cagrilintide has a 7-day half-life allowing weekly dosing. In clinical trials combined with semaglutide (CagriSema), the combination achieved up to 22.7% weight loss — superior to either alone. The combination is under investigation as a fixed-dose combination. Amylin works through different receptors than GLP-1, making this a complementary mechanism that could stack with any GLP-1 agent.

Reported benefits:
• Complementary mechanism to GLP-1 — different receptor pathway
• Long half-life — weekly dosing
• CagriSema combination shows superior weight loss to semaglutide alone
• Reduces post-meal glucagon
• Central satiety signaling — reduces appetite via different CNS pathway
• Good tolerability profile in trials

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not FDA approved
• Nausea and GI effects similar to GLP-1 class
• Phase III trials ongoing
• Not yet commercially available
• Muscle preservation still requires testosterone support
• Long-term safety data accumulating

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Clinical trial doses: 0.5-2.4mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing)
• Expected clinical: Start 0.5mg/week, titrate to 2.4mg — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing when approved)

Progression: Will likely be used in combination with semaglutide or as part of fixed-dose CagriSema combination. Same muscle preservation principles apply as all weight loss agents — testosterone and protein essential.

Common protocols:
• Advanced Metabolic: Cagrilintide (per trial protocol), Semaglutide or Tirzepatide (complementary), Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, body composition, weight, GI tolerance.

Regulatory status: Phase III clinical trials. Not FDA approved. Expected approval 2025-2026.

entries.title: Melanotan II
entries.subtitle: MT-2, bremelanotide precursor
entries.text:
Melanotan II (MT-2, bremelanotide precursor) — Metabolic Peptides

Melanotan II (MT-2) is a synthetic analogue of alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH) that activates multiple melanocortin receptors (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R, MC5R). Effects include: skin tanning without UV exposure (MC1R), appetite suppression and fat mobilization (MC3R), potent sexual desire and erectile function enhancement (MC4R — same as PT-141's mechanism), and potential anti-inflammatory effects. Unlike PT-141 (bremelanotide) which is a fragment of MT-2 targeting primarily MC4R, MT-2 has the full melanocortin spectrum. Popular in TRT clinics as an adjunct for libido, sexual function, and body composition. Requires careful dosing to avoid side effects.

Reported benefits:
• Tanning without UV — melanogenesis via MC1R
• Appetite suppression and fat mobilization
• Potent sexual function enhancement via MC4R
• Erection quality improvement
• Combines tanning + libido + fat loss effects simultaneously
• Popular and widely studied in clinical research

Risks and trade-offs:
• Nausea — most common side effect, dose-dependent
• Facial flushing
• Spontaneous erections can be problematic
• Moles and nevi can darken — skin check important
• Yawning and drowsiness at higher doses
• Not FDA approved — PT-141 (bremelanotide) is the FDA-approved version for women

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Starting (tanning): 0.25mg — SubQ before tanning/bedtime (Build up slowly)
• Standard: 0.5-1mg — SubQ as needed — not daily use (Cycle on/off)
• Sexual function: 0.5-1mg — SubQ 30-60 min before activity (As needed)

Progression: Start at 0.25mg to assess nausea — most users develop tolerance to nausea within 5-10 uses. Take at bedtime to sleep through nausea. Avoid high-fat meals around dosing. Sun exposure after dosing accelerates tanning effect. Have skin checked by dermatologist before use — existing moles should be monitored.

Common protocols:
• Sexual Health and Body Composition: MT-2 0.5-1mg as needed, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, PT-141 1mg (can alternate with MT-2), BPC-157 for overall wellness

Monitoring: Skin monitoring — photograph moles at baseline and every 3 months. Blood pressure (transient elevation). Dermatologist consultation before long-term use.

Regulatory status: Research compound — not FDA approved. PT-141 (bremelanotide) is FDA approved for women's HSDD. MT-2 is a precursor compound.

entries.title: Kisspeptin-54
entries.subtitle: KP-54, metastin full length
entries.text:
Kisspeptin-54 (KP-54, metastin full length) — Sexual Health Peptides

Kisspeptin-54 is the full-length 54-amino acid form of kisspeptin (versus Kisspeptin-10 which is the C-terminal fragment). Both activate the same kisspeptin receptors (Kiss1R) on GnRH neurons, triggering LH and FSH release. KP-54 has a longer half-life than KP-10, allowing less frequent dosing. Clinical trials have used KP-54 IV and SubQ for reproductive hormone stimulation in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and fertility treatment. Also demonstrates pro-sexual effects and may have anti-cancer properties (anti-metastatic, hence the original name metastin). Both forms require pulsatile dosing to prevent receptor desensitization.

Reported benefits:
• Longer half-life than KP-10 — less frequent dosing
• Activates HPG axis at the upstream GnRH level
• Clinical trial use in reproductive medicine
• Pro-sexual and libido-enhancing effects
• Anti-metastatic properties researched
• Fertility applications well-documented

Risks and trade-offs:
• Continuous dosing causes desensitization — pulsatile protocol essential
• Limited availability compared to KP-10
• Not FDA approved for testosterone restoration
• Complex administration protocol
• Injection only
• Expensive and difficult to source

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• HPG Axis stimulation: 1-3nmol/kg — SubQ pulsatile 1-2x daily with 12-hour gaps (4-8 weeks)
• Fertility protocol: Per clinical protocol — Physician supervised (Per fertility treatment plan)

Progression: Pulsatile dosing is absolutely essential — same principle as KP-10. Continuous administration desensitizes kisspeptin receptors and paradoxically suppresses the HPG axis. Maximum 2 doses per day with minimum 10-12 hour separation.

Common protocols:
• Fertility and HPG Restoration: Kisspeptin-54 1-2mg pulsatile 2x/day, HCG 250IU 3x/week (direct testicular support), Enclomiphene 25mg/day (complementary)

Monitoring: LH, FSH, Total T, E2 every 4 weeks. LH surge 45-60 min post-injection confirms receptor response.

Regulatory status: Research compound — clinical trial use in reproductive medicine. Not FDA approved for testosterone restoration.

entries.title: Gonadorelin
entries.subtitle: GnRH, LHRH, Factrel, Lutrepulse
entries.text:
Gonadorelin (GnRH, LHRH, Factrel, Lutrepulse) — Sexual Health Peptides

Gonadorelin is synthetic GnRH (Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone) — the master upstream signal that triggers LH and FSH release from the pituitary. FDA-approved in pulsatile pump form for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and cryptorchidism. In TRT clinics it is increasingly used as an alternative to HCG for maintaining testicular function and fertility during testosterone therapy. Unlike HCG (which mimics LH directly at the testes), gonadorelin stimulates the pituitary naturally, potentially providing a more physiological approach. Pulsatile delivery is critical — continuous GnRH paradoxically suppresses LH/FSH (the mechanism behind GnRH agonist cancer treatments like Lupron).

Reported benefits:
• Most upstream HPG axis intervention — physiological
• FDA approved in pulsatile form for hypogonadism
• Alternative to HCG for testicular maintenance on TRT
• Maintains pituitary LH/FSH production
• Supports fertility during TRT
• Growing clinical use in men's health clinics

Risks and trade-offs:
• Pulsatile dosing CRITICAL — continuous use suppresses the axis (pharmaceutical castration)
• Very short half-life — requires frequent pulsatile dosing
• Pulsatile pump ideal but impractical outside clinical setting
• SubQ pulsatile injection required multiple times daily
• More complex protocol than HCG
• Limited SubQ injection data vs pump delivery

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• TRT Testicular Maintenance: 100mcg — SubQ twice daily (minimum 8-hour gap) — pulsatile (Ongoing with TRT)
• Fertility Protocol: Pulsatile pump 5-20mcg every 90 min — Continuous pump delivery (Physician supervised)

Progression: PULSATILE PROTOCOL IS NON-NEGOTIABLE. SubQ twice daily with 8+ hour gaps. Some practitioners use 3x daily with 6-8 hour gaps. Must never be used continuously. Growing alternative to HCG in clinical TRT practice.

Common protocols:
• TRT Testicular Function: Gonadorelin 100mcg SubQ 2x/day (pulsatile), Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose, Anastrozole only if E2 elevated on labs

Monitoring: LH, FSH (will show some activity unlike HCG protocols), Total T, E2, testicular volume assessment. LH response 30-60 min post-injection confirms pituitary response.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED as Factrel for diagnostic use and Lutrepulse pump for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Off-label SubQ pulsatile use for TRT testicular maintenance.

entries.title: PT-141
entries.subtitle: Bremelanotide, Vyleesi
entries.text:
PT-141 (Bremelanotide, Vyleesi) — Additional Peptides

PT-141 (Bremelanotide) is FDA-approved for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women (Vyleesi) and studied extensively for male sexual dysfunction. Unlike PDE5 inhibitors (Viagra, Cialis) that work peripherally on blood vessels, PT-141 acts centrally on melanocortin receptors (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R) in the brain to increase sexual desire and arousal. Research demonstrates effectiveness in both male and female sexual dysfunction including cases where PDE5 inhibitors have failed. It addresses the desire/libido component rather than purely mechanical erection, making it uniquely effective for psychological components of sexual dysfunction.

Reported benefits:
• FDA approved (for women) — validated mechanism
• Central action addresses libido/desire not just mechanics
• Effective when PDE5 inhibitors fail
• Works in both men and women
• Addresses psychological components of sexual dysfunction
• On-demand dosing
• FDA-approved for women (Vyleesi)
• CNS mechanism works when Viagra fails
• Rapid onset 30–60 minutes
• Effective for both libido and erectile function
• No cardiovascular contraindications of PDE5 inhibitors

Risks and trade-offs:
• Nausea is the primary side effect — can be significant
• Transient blood pressure increase
• Flushing and facial warmth
• Not FDA approved for men (though extensively studied)
• Cost — not typically covered by insurance for men
• Injection only (SubQ)
• Nausea is common especially first use
• Cannot use with nitrates
• Expensive
• Facial flushing and hyperpigmentation with repeated use

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Male Sexual Dysfunction: 1-2mg — SubQ 30-60 min before activity (As needed — not daily use)
• Female (FDA approved): 1.75mg — SubQ 45 min before activity (As needed)
• Starting Dose: 0.5mg — SubQ injection 45 min before (As needed)
• Standard: 1.75mg — SubQ injection 45 min before (Max 1x per 24 hours)
• High Response: 1mg — SubQ injection 45 min before (Titrate based on response)

Progression: Start at 1mg. Eat a light meal 1-2 hours before to reduce nausea. Nausea typically peaks at 30-60 min and subsides. Anti-nausea medication (ondansetron) can be taken prophylactically. Do not use more than once per 24 hours.

Common protocols:
• Sexual Health Stack: PT-141 1-2mg on demand, Testosterone Cypionate TRT dose (addresses testosterone component), Zinc and Vitamin D optimization
• Male Libido: PT-141 1mg 45 min before, Testosterone optimized (600+ ng/dL), Zinc 30mg daily
• Female HSDD: PT-141 1.75mg 45 min before (FDA approved protocol), DHEA 25mg daily, Estradiol (if appropriate)

Monitoring: Blood pressure before and after first dose, nausea severity tracking, skin hyperpigmentation assessment with long-term use.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for female HSDD (Vyleesi). Off-label for male sexual dysfunction.

entries.title: CJC-1295 with DAC
entries.subtitle: CJC-1295 DAC, Drug Affinity Complex
entries.text:
CJC-1295 with DAC (CJC-1295 DAC, Drug Affinity Complex) — Anti-Inflammatory Peptides

CJC-1295 with DAC (Drug Affinity Complex) is a modified version of CJC-1295 where a lysine residue is coupled to a maleimido-propionic acid group that binds albumin, dramatically extending half-life from 30 minutes to 6-8 days. This allows once-weekly dosing compared to daily or twice-daily dosing for CJC-1295 without DAC. The tradeoff is that rather than producing natural pulsatile GH release, CJC-1295 DAC produces a prolonged GH bleed — a sustained elevation rather than sharp pulses. This blunts the natural pulsatile pattern that many practitioners prefer. GHRP pairing is still beneficial. Some prefer the convenience; others prefer the more physiological pulsatile approach of Mod GRF 1-29.

Reported benefits:
• Once or twice weekly dosing — maximum convenience
• Very long half-life — stable blood levels
• Same GH-stimulating mechanism as CJC-1295 without DAC
• Good synergy with Ipamorelin still applicable
• Less frequent injections — better adherence
• Cost-effective per week of coverage

Risks and trade-offs:
• Non-pulsatile GH elevation — blunts natural rhythm
• May cause more water retention than pulsatile version
• Tachyphylaxis (desensitization) may develop faster
• Some practitioners prefer pulsatile pattern
• Higher individual dose per injection
• IGF-1 monitoring especially important

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard: 1-2mg — Once or twice weekly SubQ (3 months on / 1 month off)
• With Ipamorelin: CJC DAC 1mg + Ipamorelin 200mcg — Once weekly (CJC DAC) + daily (Ipamorelin) (3 months on / 1 month off)

Progression: Once weekly injection of CJC-1295 DAC combined with daily Ipamorelin is a popular clinic protocol — the DAC provides sustained GH elevation while daily Ipamorelin provides additional pulsatile amplification. Monitor IGF-1 carefully.

Common protocols:
• Convenient GH Protocol: CJC-1295 DAC 1mg once weekly, Ipamorelin 200mcg daily before bed, Testosterone TRT dose, BPC-157 if recovery is concurrent goal

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 6-8 weeks, fasting glucose, water retention assessment.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Not for human use label. Widely used in anti-aging and TRT clinics.

entries.title: BPC-157 Systemic Protocol
entries.subtitle: BPC-157 oral systemic, extended protocol
entries.text:
BPC-157 Systemic Protocol (BPC-157 oral systemic, extended protocol) — Anti-Inflammatory Peptides

Beyond acute injury use, BPC-157 has an emerging systemic protocol for broader anti-inflammatory, gut-brain axis support, and neuroprotective applications. Research through 2026 increasingly shows BPC-157 acts systemically via multiple pathways: nitric oxide modulation, dopaminergic system support, and VEGF-mediated angiogenesis throughout the body. For systemic use, oral administration provides gut-specific benefits while SubQ provides broader distribution. New research explores BPC-157 in neuroinflammation, neurotransmitter dysregulation (useful alongside TRT where mood issues are common), and cardiovascular protection.

Reported benefits:
• Systemic anti-inflammatory across multiple pathways
• Gut-brain axis support via oral route
• Dopaminergic system modulation — mood and motivation
• Nitric oxide pathway — cardiovascular benefits
• Neuroprotective emerging data
• Excellent long-term safety profile in research

Risks and trade-offs:
• Long-term systemic use data still limited
• Quality sourcing remains critical
• Mechanism is highly pleiotropic — complex to predict individual response
• Not FDA approved
• Cost for long-term systemic use can be significant
• Optimal dosing for systemic vs local effects not fully established

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Systemic anti-inflammatory: 250mcg/day — SubQ daily — or 500mcg orally for gut-brain (Cycle 8-12 weeks / 4 weeks off)
• Maintenance: 200mcg — SubQ 3-5x weekly (Long-term maintenance cycling)

Progression: For systemic protocols cycle 8-12 weeks on with a 4-week break. Oral route for gut-brain axis effects; SubQ for systemic distribution. Can be used year-round at lower maintenance doses with periodic full breaks.

Common protocols:
• Systemic Wellness Stack: BPC-157 250mcg/day SubQ, LDN 4.5mg at bedtime (complementary anti-inflammatory), Testosterone TRT dose, NAC 600mg 2x/day (antioxidant support)

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (CRP) before and after cycles. Gut symptom tracking. Mood and energy self-assessment.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Growing use in functional medicine and TRT clinics for systemic protocols.

entries.title: TB-500 Systemic Protocol
entries.subtitle: Thymosin Beta-4 systemic, TB-500 extended
entries.text:
TB-500 Systemic Protocol (Thymosin Beta-4 systemic, TB-500 extended) — Anti-Inflammatory Peptides

TB-500 systemic protocols extend beyond acute injury treatment to address chronic inflammatory conditions, fibrosis prevention, and whole-body tissue maintenance. Research through 2026 increasingly documents TB-500 effects on cardiac muscle (protection from fibrosis), neural tissue (neuroprotection in spinal cord research), and systemic actin regulation. In TRT and peptide clinics, TB-500 is increasingly used at lower maintenance doses year-round rather than only during acute injury — functioning as a systemic anti-fibrotic and tissue maintenance agent.

Reported benefits:
• Systemic anti-fibrotic effects
• Cardiac muscle protection from fibrosis
• Neural tissue protection
• Reduces systemic inflammation
• Year-round maintenance dosing possible
• Synergistic with BPC-157 systemically

Risks and trade-offs:
• Cancer concern from some animal models — important consideration for long-term use
• Limited long-term human safety data
• Expensive for year-round use
• Quality sourcing critical
• Mechanism systemic — effects hard to attribute precisely
• Not FDA approved

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Acute injury: 2.5mg 2x/week (loading) — SubQ — 4-6 week loading (Loading then maintenance)
• Systemic maintenance: 2.5mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Ongoing with periodic breaks)
• Conservative maintenance: 2.5mg every 2 weeks — Biweekly SubQ (Long-term)

Progression: For systemic maintenance after injury recovery, transition to 2.5mg weekly then biweekly. Given theoretical cancer concern from animal studies, many practitioners cycle 3 months on / 1 month off for long-term protocols rather than continuous year-round use.

Common protocols:
• Systemic Repair Maintenance: TB-500 2.5mg weekly, BPC-157 250mcg/day (synergistic), Testosterone TRT dose, Collagen peptides 15g/day

Monitoring: General health panel. Given theoretical cancer concern, periodic comprehensive health screening appropriate for long-term use.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Growing clinical use for injury recovery and systemic protocols.

entries.title: KPV
entries.subtitle: Lys-Pro-Val, Alpha-MSH C-terminal tripeptide, α-MSH(11-13)
entries.text:
KPV (Lys-Pro-Val, Alpha-MSH C-terminal tripeptide, α-MSH(11-13)) — Peptides

KPV is a tripeptide representing the C-terminal fragment of alpha-melanocyte stimulating hormone. It possesses potent anti-inflammatory properties via inhibition of NF-kB signaling — particularly effective for inflammatory bowel disease, skin inflammation, and systemic inflammatory conditions. Uniquely, it can penetrate cell nuclei and act directly on intracellular inflammatory pathways. FDA Orphan Drug designation for IBD applications is in progress. Can be taken orally for gut-specific effects.

Reported benefits:
• Potent NF-kB inhibition — broad anti-inflammatory
• Effective for IBD — Crohn's and ulcerative colitis
• Skin inflammation treatment (eczema, psoriasis)
• Can be taken orally for gut-specific effects
• Nuclear penetration — intracellular mechanism
• No significant side effects in research
• Powerful gut anti-inflammatory
• Systemic NF-κB suppression
• Oral bioavailability for gut-specific use
• Excellent safety profile
• Synergistic with BPC-157
• Immune modulation

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited human clinical trial data
• Not FDA approved
• Oral bioavailability variable
• Quality sourcing critical
• Long-term effects not established
• May need higher oral doses vs SubQ
• Limited human clinical data
• Optimal dosing not yet established
• Multiple administration routes can be confusing
• Short half-life

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Gut and IBD: 500mcg-1mg orally — Twice daily fasted (4-8 weeks)
• Systemic anti-inflammatory: 250-500mcg — SubQ once daily (4-6 weeks)
• Gut Protocol (Oral): 500mcg–2mg — Oral capsule, twice daily fasted (4–12 weeks)
• Systemic: 500mcg–1mg — SubQ injection daily (4–8 weeks)

Progression: For gut-specific use, oral capsules preferred. 500mcg twice daily fasted. For systemic inflammation, 500mcg–1mg subcutaneous daily. Combine with BPC-157 for synergistic gut healing.

Common protocols:
• Gut Healing Stack: KPV 500mcg orally 2x/day, BPC-157 250mcg orally 2x/day, Thymosin Alpha-1 1.6mg 2x/week
• Systemic Anti-Inflammatory: KPV 500mcg SubQ daily, TB-500 2.5mg 2x/week, Omega-3 EPA/DHA 3g/day

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) if available. Symptom tracking for GI conditions. No specific blood monitoring required.

Regulatory status: Research compound — Orphan Drug Designation in progress for IBD. Not FDA approved.

entries.title: Fisetin
entries.subtitle: 7,3',4'-flavon-3-ol, senolytic flavonoid
entries.text:
Fisetin (7,3',4'-flavon-3-ol, senolytic flavonoid) — Senolytics and Autophagy

Fisetin is a naturally occurring flavonoid found in strawberries, apples, and onions that has emerged as one of the most potent senolytic compounds identified in aging research. Senolytics selectively eliminate senescent cells — the 'zombie cells' that accumulate with age, secrete pro-inflammatory compounds (SASP), and drive tissue dysfunction. Mayo Clinic and the Buck Institute studies demonstrate fisetin clears senescent cells across multiple tissues, extends healthspan in aged mice, and reduces inflammatory markers. The intermittent 'pulse' dosing protocol is critical — senolytics are taken in high-dose bursts (2-5 days) every 1-3 months rather than daily, to allow clearance of senescent cells followed by tissue recovery.

Reported benefits:
• One of most potent natural senolytics identified
• Mayo Clinic and Buck Institute research validated
• Clears senescent cells across multiple tissues
• Anti-inflammatory via SASP reduction
• Crosses blood-brain barrier — neuroprotective
• Intermittent pulse dosing — no daily pill burden

Risks and trade-offs:
• High doses needed for senolytic effect (20mg/kg in studies)
• Pulse dosing protocol requires planning
• Human optimal dose not firmly established
• Quality varies significantly between supplements
• May cause temporary fatigue during senolytic pulse
• Long-term pulse protocol effects still being studied

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Senolytic pulse: 1000-1500mg/day — For 2-3 consecutive days, every 1-3 months (Pulse cycles)
• Anti-inflammatory daily: 100-200mg/day — Daily oral with fatty meal (Ongoing between pulses)

Progression: For senolytic effect: take 1000-1500mg/day for 2-3 days, then stop. Repeat every 1-3 months. Between pulses, 100-200mg/day provides anti-inflammatory maintenance. Take with fat-containing meal — fisetin is fat-soluble. Often combined with quercetin and dasatinib for a comprehensive senolytic protocol.

Common protocols:
• Senolytic Pulse Stack: Fisetin 1500mg/day x 3 days (pulse), Quercetin 1000mg/day x 3 days (concurrent pulse), Rapamycin 6mg weekly (ongoing mTOR inhibition), Metformin 500mg/day (ongoing AMPK activation)

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6) before and after pulse cycles — expect temporary elevation then reduction. Self-assessment of energy, joint pain, cognitive clarity.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Research compound for senolytic indications. Well-established safety profile.

entries.title: Quercetin
entries.subtitle: Quercetin dihydrate, senolytic flavonoid
entries.text:
Quercetin (Quercetin dihydrate, senolytic flavonoid) — Senolytics and Autophagy

Quercetin is a plant flavonoid with broad biological activity including senolytic, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antiviral properties. It was identified as a senolytic compound in the landmark Mayo Clinic study alongside dasatinib — the combination (D+Q) is the most studied senolytic protocol in human clinical trials. Quercetin inhibits anti-apoptotic pathways that senescent cells rely on for survival, selectively eliminating them while leaving healthy cells intact. Additionally quercetin inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation, reduces histamine release (antihistamine properties), modulates gut microbiome, and has antiviral activity demonstrated in COVID-19 research.

Reported benefits:
• Validated senolytic — human clinical trial data with dasatinib
• Broad anti-inflammatory via NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition
• Antiviral activity — broad spectrum
• Antihistamine properties — useful in MCAS
• Gut microbiome modulation
• Better bioavailability with bromelain or quercetin phytosome

Risks and trade-offs:
• Poor bioavailability without bioavailability enhancers
• High doses needed for senolytic effect
• May interact with antibiotics (quinolones) and blood thinners
• Quality varies between supplements
• Quercetin phytosome more expensive but better absorbed
• Full senolytic effects require dasatinib combination per trials

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Senolytic pulse (D+Q protocol): 1000mg/day — For 2-3 days concurrently with fisetin pulse (Every 1-3 months)
• Daily anti-inflammatory: 500-1000mg/day — Daily oral with bromelain or zinc for absorption (Ongoing)

Progression: For maximum senolytic effect pair with dasatinib (D+Q protocol per Mayo Clinic trials). For solo use pair with fisetin in pulse cycles. Take with bromelain 500mg or quercetin phytosome formulation for better absorption. Zinc 10mg enhances quercetin cellular uptake.

Common protocols:
• D+Q Senolytic Protocol: Dasatinib 100mg/day x 2-3 days (pulse — Rx required), Quercetin 1000mg/day x 2-3 days (concurrent), Fisetin 1500mg/day x 2-3 days (concurrent), Repeat every 2-3 months

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers pre and post pulse. CBC (dasatinib affects blood counts). Self-assessment of energy, cognition, joint health.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Senolytic research ongoing in human clinical trials.

entries.title: Dasatinib
entries.subtitle: Sprycel, senolytic Rx, BCR-ABL inhibitor
entries.text:
Dasatinib (Sprycel, senolytic Rx, BCR-ABL inhibitor) — Senolytics and Autophagy

Dasatinib is an FDA-approved tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) for leukemia that was identified by the Mayo Clinic as the most potent senolytic compound discovered in a drug screen. The D+Q (Dasatinib + Quercetin) protocol is the most clinically studied senolytic combination, with human trials demonstrating reduced senescent cell burden, improved physical function, reduced frailty markers, and improved lung function in IPF patients. Unlike natural senolytics, dasatinib is a prescription drug with real side effects — it must be used under physician supervision and only in the same intermittent low-dose pulse protocol (not as continuous cancer treatment doses).

Reported benefits:
• Most potent senolytic compound identified — FDA approved drug
• Human clinical trial data (Mayo Clinic multiple trials)
• D+Q combination synergistic — more potent than either alone
• Demonstrated reduction in actual senescent cell biomarkers in humans
• Improved physical function and frailty measures in trials
• Low intermittent doses (not cancer doses) used for longevity

Risks and trade-offs:
• Prescription drug — physician oversight absolutely required
• Side effects at cancer doses are significant — longevity doses are much lower
• Not FDA approved for longevity or anti-aging
• Drug interactions — check all current medications
• Bone marrow suppression monitoring required
• Cost — brand name expensive, generic available

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• D+Q Longevity protocol: 100mg/day for 2-3 days — Oral — pulse every 2-3 months with Quercetin (Intermittent pulse only — never daily)
• Clinical trial dose: 100mg/day x 2-3 days — Per Mayo Clinic protocols with Quercetin 1000mg (Quarterly or biannual cycles)

Progression: MUST be prescribed and supervised by a physician. The longevity dose (100mg x 2-3 days) is dramatically lower than cancer treatment doses. Never use continuously — only in the intermittent pulse protocol. Always combine with quercetin per the validated D+Q protocol.

Common protocols:
• D+Q Senolytic Protocol: Dasatinib 100mg/day x 2-3 days (Rx — physician supervised), Quercetin 1000mg/day x 2-3 days, Fisetin 1500mg/day x 2-3 days, Rapamycin 6mg weekly ongoing (complementary longevity)

Monitoring: CBC with differential before and 2 weeks after each pulse (dasatinib affects blood counts). Liver enzymes. Physician monitoring required for each cycle. Senescent cell biomarkers (p16, p21) if available via specialty labs.

Regulatory status: FDA APPROVED for leukemia (Sprycel). Off-label longevity use at much lower intermittent doses. Physician prescription and supervision required.

entries.title: Spermidine
entries.subtitle: Spermidine trihydrochloride, polyamine, N-(3-Aminopropyl)putrescine
entries.text:
Spermidine (Spermidine trihydrochloride, polyamine, N-(3-Aminopropyl)putrescine) — Senolytics and Autophagy

Spermidine is a naturally occurring polyamine found in high concentrations in wheat germ, soybeans, mushrooms, and aged cheese. It is one of the most potent inducers of autophagy — the cellular self-cleaning process that degrades damaged proteins and organelles. Research demonstrates spermidine extends lifespan in multiple model organisms, reduces cardiovascular mortality in epidemiological studies, improves cognitive function in aging, and reduces hair loss. Unlike senolytics which eliminate senescent cells, spermidine enhances the cellular maintenance process that prevents cells from becoming senescent. Growing human evidence — a randomized trial showed cognitive improvement in older adults.

Reported benefits:
• Potent autophagy inducer — cellular cleanup mechanism
• Epidemiological data linking intake to reduced cardiovascular mortality
• Randomized trial showing cognitive improvement in older adults
• Lifespan extension in multiple model organisms
• Reduces hair loss via follicle autophagy activation
• Well-tolerated with food-sourced safety history
• Potent autophagy inducer
• Reduced cardiovascular mortality in studies
• Cognitive preservation data
• Natural compound found in foods
• Well-tolerated supplement
• Synergistic with fasting and rapamycin

Risks and trade-offs:
• Human doses for longevity effect higher than dietary sources
• Quality varies significantly between supplement brands
• Expensive for pharmaceutical-grade spermidine trihydrochloride
• Optimal dose and timing not firmly established
• Fasting potentiates effects but hard to maintain daily
• Long-term supplement safety data still accumulating
• Effective food doses require large quantities of wheat germ
• Supplement standardization varies
• Long-term human intervention data limited
• Mechanism complex and not fully understood
• Relatively expensive for quality supplements

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard longevity: 1-5mg/day — Daily oral — fasted state preferred (Ongoing)
• Higher therapeutic: 5-10mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing)
• Dietary: 1–2mg/day — High spermidine foods (Ongoing)
• Supplement: 1–5mg/day — Oral supplement (Ongoing)

Progression: Take fasted for maximum autophagy induction — spermidine and fasting synergize. Even 1mg/day from supplements alongside dietary sources (wheat germ) may provide meaningful autophagy support. Works synergistically with rapamycin (both induce autophagy via different mechanisms).

Common protocols:
• Autophagy and Longevity: Spermidine 5mg/day fasted, Rapamycin 6mg weekly (synergistic autophagy), NMN 1000mg/day, Fisetin quarterly pulse
• Autophagy Stack: Spermidine 5mg/day, Urolithin A 1g/day, Fasting 16:8 protocol, Rapamycin 5mg/week (physician supervised)
• Cardiovascular Longevity: Spermidine 5mg/day, Omega-3 EPA/DHA 3g/day, Coenzyme Q10 300mg/day

Monitoring: No specific blood monitoring. Cognitive self-assessment, hair health, energy tracking. Inflammatory markers optionally.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Well-tolerated with strong mechanistic and growing human evidence.

entries.title: Taurine
entries.subtitle: 2-aminoethanesulfonic acid
entries.text:
Taurine (2-aminoethanesulfonic acid) — Supplements and Nutraceuticals

Taurine is a sulfur-containing amino acid that declines dramatically with age — a landmark 2023 Science paper (Singh et al.) demonstrated taurine deficiency is a driver of aging, and taurine supplementation extended healthspan and lifespan in multiple animal models. In humans, serum taurine levels inversely correlate with multiple aging markers. Taurine has broad biological roles: regulates calcium signaling in muscle (improves contraction and endurance), protects mitochondria, acts as an antioxidant, supports cardiovascular function, modulates GABA receptors (anxiolytic), and improves insulin sensitivity. One of the best-evidenced and safest longevity supplements available.

Reported benefits:
• 2023 Science paper linking taurine to aging — major evidence
• Levels decline significantly with age
• Improves exercise endurance and muscle function
• Cardiovascular protective — reduces blood pressure
• Mitochondrial protection and antioxidant
• Anxiolytic via GABA modulation — improves sleep quality

Risks and trade-offs:
• High doses needed for robust longevity effects (3-6g/day)
• Most research still animal-based for longevity claims
• May cause digestive upset at very high doses
• Relatively tasteless in powder form but requires large amounts
• Interaction with lithium — space apart
• Largely safe but optimal longevity dose in humans unknown

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard health: 1-3g/day — Daily oral — any time (Ongoing)
• Performance and longevity: 3-6g/day — Daily oral split AM and PM (Ongoing)

Progression: Well-tolerated at doses up to 6g/day. Powder form cost-effective for higher doses. Can be taken any time — some prefer pre-workout for performance benefits. No cycling required.

Common protocols:
• Longevity Foundation Stack: Taurine 3-6g/day, NMN 1000mg/day, Spermidine 5mg/day, Metformin 500mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Blood pressure (taurine lowers it — monitor if on antihypertensives). Exercise performance and endurance self-assessment. Fasting glucose (insulin sensitivity improvement).

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. GRAS (Generally Recognized as Safe). Decades of safety data as food additive.

entries.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA)
entries.subtitle: ALA, R-ALA, thioctic acid
entries.text:
Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) (ALA, R-ALA, thioctic acid) — Supplements and Nutraceuticals

Alpha-lipoic acid is a naturally occurring compound that functions as a cofactor in mitochondrial energy metabolism and as a potent antioxidant that works in both water-soluble and fat-soluble environments — unlike most antioxidants which are limited to one. ALA regenerates other antioxidants (Vitamin C, Vitamin E, glutathione) and chelates heavy metals. R-ALA (the natural isomer) is significantly more bioactive than racemic ALA. Clinical research demonstrates improvements in insulin sensitivity, peripheral neuropathy (FDA-approved in Germany), heavy metal chelation, cognitive protection, and cardiovascular health. Widely used alongside NAC in hormone optimization protocols for antioxidant support.

Reported benefits:
• Dual-phase antioxidant — works in water and fat-soluble environments
• Regenerates Vitamin C, E, and glutathione
• Improves insulin sensitivity — comparable to some pharmaceuticals
• FDA approved in Germany for diabetic neuropathy
• Heavy metal chelation — removes mercury, lead, arsenic
• Neuroprotective — crosses blood-brain barrier

Risks and trade-offs:
• R-ALA degrades quickly — refrigeration and fresh product important
• Can cause hypoglycemia in diabetics — monitor glucose
• High doses (1000mg+) may cause thiamine depletion
• Should be separated from thyroid medication by 4 hours
• Racemic ALA (cheaper) less bioactive than R-ALA
• May cause nausea if taken without food

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Antioxidant support: 300-600mg/day R-ALA — Daily oral with food (Ongoing)
• Insulin sensitivity: 600-1200mg/day — Split 2-3x daily with meals (Ongoing)
• Neuropathy: 600mg/day — Once daily or split (3-6 months minimum)

Progression: R-ALA preferred over racemic ALA for better absorption and activity. Take with food to minimize nausea. Supplement thiamine (B1) 100mg/day if using high doses long-term. Take 4 hours away from thyroid medications.

Common protocols:
• Antioxidant and Metabolic: R-ALA 600mg/day with meals, NAC 600mg 2x/day, Vitamin C 1000mg/day, Berberine 500mg 3x/day

Monitoring: Fasting glucose (ALA improves insulin sensitivity — watch for hypoglycemia if diabetic). Thyroid function if on thyroid medication.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement in US. FDA approved as drug for diabetic neuropathy in Germany. Well-established safety profile.

entries.title: Oxytocin
entries.subtitle: OT, bonding hormone, Pitocin (Rx)
entries.text:
Oxytocin (OT, bonding hormone, Pitocin (Rx)) — Supplements and Nutraceuticals

Oxytocin is a neuropeptide and hormone produced in the hypothalamus with roles far beyond its well-known bonding and labor functions. Research through 2026 demonstrates oxytocin has potent anti-inflammatory effects, improves muscle regeneration (activates satellite cells), counteracts age-related muscle atrophy, reduces stress and cortisol, improves social cognition, and enhances recovery. Intranasal oxytocin (the route used in research) bypasses the blood-brain barrier and reaches central oxytocin receptors. Growing use in TRT clinics for libido enhancement, relationship and social wellness, workout recovery, and as a complement to testosterone therapy where mood and social connection are concerns.

Reported benefits:
• Muscle regeneration via satellite cell activation — anti-aging
• Potent anti-inflammatory and cortisol reduction
• Libido and intimacy enhancement
• Social bonding and mood improvement
• Recovery enhancement — post-workout and post-injury
• Well-studied safety profile in clinical research

Risks and trade-offs:
• Intranasal route required for CNS effects — not effective orally
• Very short half-life — effects last 30-60 minutes
• Tolerance develops with frequent use — limit to a few times weekly
• Can cause headache at higher doses
• Not FDA approved for performance or recovery use
• Emotionally sensitizing — can intensify negative as well as positive emotions

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Intranasal: 8-24 IU (2-6 sprays) — Intranasal — 1 spray per nostril, 2-3x weekly (As needed — avoid daily use)
• Subcutaneous: 5-10 IU — Subcutaneous injection — as needed (As needed — avoid frequent daily use)
• Performance and recovery: 16 IU intranasal / 5-10 IU SubQ — 30 min before activity or social event (As needed)

Progression: Intranasal only for CNS effects. Use 2-3x weekly maximum to prevent tolerance. Effects onset in 15-45 minutes. Most effective when combined with social interaction or physical contact — exogenous oxytocin primes natural oxytocin pathways.

Common protocols:
• Recovery and Social Wellness: Oxytocin 16 IU intranasal 2-3x weekly, Testosterone TRT dose, BPC-157 (recovery synergy), Magnesium glycinate 400mg PM (sleep and stress)

Monitoring: Mood self-assessment, cortisol (if stress is a concern), libido and social wellness tracking. No specific blood monitoring required.

Regulatory status: FDA approved as Pitocin for labor induction. Off-label intranasal use for wellness. Compounding pharmacies produce intranasal formulations.

entries.title: NAD+ IV Protocol
entries.subtitle: NAD+ infusion, intravenous NAD, NMN IV equivalent
entries.text:
NAD+ IV Protocol (NAD+ infusion, intravenous NAD, NMN IV equivalent) — Supplements and Nutraceuticals

Intravenous NAD+ delivers nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide directly into the bloodstream, bypassing gut and liver metabolism for immediate cellular availability. IV NAD+ dramatically increases blood NAD+ levels — achieving 5-10x higher peak concentrations than oral NMN or NR supplementation. Research demonstrates benefits for addiction recovery (FDA-approved study context), neurodegenerative conditions, chronic fatigue, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cognitive enhancement. Many TRT and functional medicine clinics now offer NAD+ IV as a premium service. Typical infusions run 250-1000mg over 2-4 hours. The experience can include flushing, nausea, and chest tightness during infusion — these resolve with slower infusion rate.

Reported benefits:
• Highest achievable blood NAD+ levels — 5-10x oral supplements
• Immediate cellular availability
• Dramatic energy and cognitive enhancement reported
• Addiction and substance recovery research base
• Combined with glutathione push for comprehensive antioxidant protocol
• Popular clinic revenue service — high patient satisfaction

Risks and trade-offs:
• Requires clinical setting and IV access
• Expensive per infusion ($300-1000 per session)
• Side effects during infusion: flushing, nausea, chest tightness (rate-dependent)
• Oral NMN/NR provides sustained levels vs spike
• Frequency for optimal benefit not established
• Insurance does not cover wellness NAD+ infusions

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Maintenance: 250-500mg IV — Monthly or quarterly infusion (Ongoing maintenance schedule)
• Loading / Intensive: 500-1000mg IV — 3-5 consecutive days then monthly (Loading protocol then maintenance)

Progression: Infuse slowly — 250mg over 2 hours minimum. Most side effects are rate-dependent and resolve by slowing the drip. Often combined with a glutathione push (1000-2000mg) at the end of the infusion. Between sessions, maintain with oral NMN 1000mg/day.

Common protocols:
• IV Longevity Protocol: NAD+ IV 500mg monthly, Glutathione IV push 1500mg (same session), NMN 1000mg/day oral between infusions, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: General wellness and energy self-assessment. No specific blood monitoring required for wellness use. Liver enzymes if frequent high-dose infusions.

Regulatory status: NAD+ is not FDA approved as a drug for wellness indications. Used in research contexts for addiction. Clinical infusions are off-label wellness services.

entries.title: DSIP
entries.subtitle: Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide, DSIP nonapeptide
entries.text:
DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide, DSIP nonapeptide) — Sleep and Neurological

DSIP (Delta Sleep-Inducing Peptide) is a naturally occurring nonapeptide discovered in 1974 that modulates sleep architecture, stress response, and neuroendocrine function. Research demonstrates DSIP increases delta (slow-wave) sleep — the most restorative sleep stage — reduces sleep onset latency, and normalizes disrupted sleep patterns. Beyond sleep, DSIP has anti-stress properties, modulates cortisol and ACTH release, has antioxidant effects, and may have anti-cancer properties. Growing use in TRT and peptide clinics for patients with sleep dysfunction, high cortisol patterns, or those whose deep sleep is disrupted by peptide protocols (GHRPs taken too late can disrupt sleep architecture).

Reported benefits:
• Increases delta wave slow-wave sleep — most restorative stage
• Reduces sleep onset latency
• Anti-stress — modulates cortisol and ACTH
• Antioxidant properties
• Normalizes disrupted sleep patterns
• Short half-life — flexible timing

Risks and trade-offs:
• Limited large-scale human trial data
• Not FDA approved
• Quality sourcing critical
• May cause vivid dreams initially
• Tolerance may develop with daily use — cycle recommended
• Intranasal or SubQ required — no oral bioavailability

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Sleep optimization: 200-500mcg — SubQ or intranasal 30 min before bed (5 days on / 2 days off cycling)
• Stress and cortisol: 200mcg — SubQ once daily (4-6 weeks)

Progression: Best used 30-60 minutes before intended sleep. Cycle 5 days on / 2 days off to prevent tolerance. Particularly useful for those on GHRP protocols to restore natural sleep architecture. Can be combined with Selank for comprehensive sleep-stress support.

Common protocols:
• Sleep Optimization Stack: DSIP 300mcg SubQ pre-bed, Selank 500mcg intranasal PM, Magnesium glycinate 400mg, Testosterone TRT dose (morning only)

Monitoring: Sleep quality self-assessment (consider sleep tracking with wearable). Cortisol AM if stress is concurrent concern. Mood and energy next-day tracking.

Regulatory status: Research compound — no FDA approval. Used in Russian sleep medicine research. Growing use in functional medicine clinics.

entries.title: Glycine
entries.subtitle: Aminoacetic acid, glycine powder
entries.text:
Glycine (Aminoacetic acid, glycine powder) — Sleep and Neurological

Glycine is the simplest amino acid with diverse physiological roles: collagen synthesis cofactor (33% of collagen is glycine), inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord and brainstem, gluconeogenesis substrate, and increasingly recognized longevity compound. Research demonstrates glycine supplementation improves sleep quality (reduces sleep onset, improves sleep architecture), is required for glutathione synthesis (alongside NAC and cysteine), extends lifespan in animal models, and has anti-inflammatory properties. A landmark ITP study showed glycine extended mouse lifespan. Dietary glycine intake is typically insufficient — the glycine deficit hypothesis suggests most people are chronically deficient given collagen is the most abundant protein in the body.

Reported benefits:
• Improves sleep quality — reduces sleep onset and improves deep sleep
• Essential for collagen synthesis — 1/3 of all collagen
• Required for glutathione production alongside NAC
• ITP lifespan extension data
• Anti-inflammatory — reduces inflammatory markers
• Inexpensive — widely available as powder

Risks and trade-offs:
• High doses needed for sleep benefit (3-5g)
• Slightly sweet taste — noticeable in water
• Very large doses (>30g) can cause GI upset
• Not a dramatic standalone sleep agent
• Effects on longevity in humans speculative from animal data
• May cause excessive sedation at very high doses

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Sleep quality: 3-5g — Oral before bed in water (Ongoing)
• Collagen and longevity: 5-10g/day — Split AM and PM oral (Ongoing)

Progression: Take 30-60 minutes before bed for sleep benefit. Dissolves easily in warm water. Combines powerfully with NAC for glutathione support — together they provide two of the three glutathione precursors. Stack with collagen peptides for comprehensive connective tissue support.

Common protocols:
• Sleep and Longevity: Glycine 5g before bed, NAC 600mg 2x/day (glutathione cofactor), Collagen peptides 15g/day, Magnesium glycinate 400mg PM

Monitoring: Sleep quality tracking. No specific blood monitoring needed. Glutathione levels if available via specialty labs.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. GRAS status. Decades of safety data as food additive.

entries.title: Lithium Orotate
entries.subtitle: Micro-dose lithium, lithium orotate supplement
entries.text:
Lithium Orotate (Micro-dose lithium, lithium orotate supplement) — Sleep and Neurological

Lithium orotate is lithium bound to orotic acid — a form that reportedly achieves brain levels at much lower doses than pharmaceutical lithium carbonate (used at 300-1200mg/day for bipolar disorder). At micro-doses (1-20mg elemental lithium), research suggests neuroprotective effects: promotes BDNF, inhibits GSK-3β (a key Alzheimer's-related enzyme), reduces neuroinflammation, and may protect against neurodegeneration. Epidemiological studies show inverse correlation between drinking water lithium levels and rates of suicide, violent crime, and dementia — suggesting background lithium exposure is neuroprotective. Used by longevity practitioners and neurologists as a brain health supplement at doses far below psychiatric levels.

Reported benefits:
• Neuroprotective via GSK-3β inhibition
• Promotes BDNF — neuroplasticity support
• Epidemiological data linking water lithium to reduced dementia
• Anti-inflammatory in neural tissue
• Mood stabilizing effects at micro-doses
• May slow Alzheimer's progression (emerging research)

Risks and trade-offs:
• Not well-studied at micro-doses — most data extrapolated from high-dose psychiatric use
• Thyroid suppression possible — monitor TSH
• Kidney function monitoring recommended
• Not FDA approved at supplement doses
• Quality and elemental lithium content varies between brands
• Dehydration concentrates lithium — stay well hydrated

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Neuroprotective micro-dose: 5-10mg elemental lithium — Daily oral with food (Ongoing — long-term)
• Mood support: 10-20mg elemental lithium — Daily oral (Ongoing)

Progression: Ensure adequate hydration — dehydration raises lithium levels. Take with food. Monitor thyroid and kidney function annually. At these doses side effects are rare but thyroid suppression is the main concern.

Common protocols:
• Brain Longevity Stack: Lithium orotate 5-10mg/day, Cerebrolysin periodic cycles, NMN 1000mg/day, Semax 600mcg intranasal AM, Omega-3 DHA 2g/day

Monitoring: TSH (thyroid) every 6 months, kidney function (creatinine, eGFR) annually. Mood and cognitive self-assessment.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA approval at these doses. Lithium carbonate is FDA approved for bipolar disorder at much higher doses. Consult physician before use.

entries.title: Creatine Monohydrate
entries.subtitle: Creatine, Cr, creatine monohydrate
entries.text:
Creatine Monohydrate (Creatine, Cr, creatine monohydrate) — Performance and Recovery

Creatine monohydrate is the most studied performance supplement in history with over 500 peer-reviewed studies. It increases phosphocreatine stores in muscle, allowing faster ATP regeneration during high-intensity exercise — directly improving strength, power output, and high-intensity exercise capacity. Beyond performance, emerging research (2020-2026) demonstrates creatine improves cognitive function, reduces cognitive fatigue, is neuroprotective, reduces muscle loss during caloric restriction, and improves glucose metabolism. Particularly synergistic with testosterone therapy — TRT increases creatine uptake and utilization. One of the safest and most cost-effective supplements available. The 'loading phase' is optional — consistent daily dosing achieves the same saturation in 3-4 weeks.

Reported benefits:
• Most studied performance supplement — 500+ studies
• Increases strength and power output 5-15% in research
• Cognitive enhancement — improves working memory
• Neuroprotective emerging data
• Reduces muscle loss during caloric restriction
• Synergistic with testosterone therapy
• Safe — no kidney damage in healthy individuals

Risks and trade-offs:
• Water retention initially (intramuscular, not subcutaneous)
• GI discomfort with loading phase — skip and dose daily instead
• Creatine non-responders exist (10-30% of population)
• Caffeine may blunt effects slightly
• Weight increase from water retention can be misleading on scale
• Quality varies — stick to pure creatine monohydrate

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Standard daily: 3-5g/day — Daily oral — any time, consistent timing preferred (Ongoing — no cycling needed)
• Loading protocol (optional): 20g/day (5g x4) — Four split doses for 5-7 days, then 3-5g/day maintenance (Loading 5-7 days then maintenance indefinitely)

Progression: No loading required — 3-5g daily reaches saturation in 3-4 weeks without GI discomfort. Take consistently. Timing doesn't matter significantly — post-workout may have slight advantage. Monohydrate is the gold standard — no need for expensive variants (HCl, ethyl ester, etc.).

Common protocols:
• Strength and Muscle Stack: Creatine monohydrate 5g/day, Testosterone TRT dose, BPC-157 500mcg/day (recovery), Collagen peptides 15g/day (connective tissue)

Monitoring: No specific monitoring needed in healthy individuals. Creatinine on blood panels will be elevated — inform your lab that you supplement creatine (it affects interpretation). Kidney function fine in healthy individuals.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. GRAS status. One of the most safety-validated supplements available.

entries.title: Urolithin A
entries.subtitle: UA, Mitopure, ellagitannin metabolite
entries.text:
Urolithin A (UA, Mitopure, ellagitannin metabolite) — Performance and Recovery

Urolithin A is a metabolite produced by gut bacteria from ellagitannins (found in pomegranates, walnuts, raspberries). It is the most potent known inducer of mitophagy — the selective removal of damaged mitochondria — via the PINK1/Parkin pathway. Clinical trials (2022 human RCT published in Nature Aging) demonstrate Urolithin A supplementation increases muscle strength, endurance, and mitochondrial gene expression in older adults. Only 30-40% of people produce meaningful Urolithin A from diet — the rest produce little regardless of pomegranate consumption due to gut microbiome differences. Mitopure (Timeline Nutrition) is the pharmaceutical-grade version used in trials.

Reported benefits:
• Most potent mitophagy inducer identified — selective damaged mitochondria removal
• Human RCT in Nature Aging showing muscle and mitochondrial benefits
• Addresses root cause of mitochondrial aging
• Only 30-40% of people produce it from diet
• PINK1/Parkin pathway activation — well-characterized mechanism
• Synergistic with SS-31 and MOTS-c for comprehensive mitochondrial support
• Human clinical trial data (Phase I/II)
• Improves mitochondrial function
• Increases muscle endurance
• Reduces inflammatory markers
• Safe and well-tolerated
• Available as commercial supplement

Risks and trade-offs:
• Expensive — Mitopure (clinical grade) is $100-150/month
• Generic urolithin A supplements variable quality and bioavailability
• Mitophagy effects take weeks to become apparent
• Not a dramatic acute effect — cumulative cellular benefit
• Long-term human data still accumulating beyond trial periods
• Should be taken consistently — not suited to intermittent use
• Expensive as commercial supplement (Timeline)
• Can produce via diet (pomegranate) with variable absorption
• Not all humans are urolithin A producers
• Long-term data still emerging
• Optimal dosing not fully established

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Clinical (Mitopure): 500-1000mg/day — Daily oral with fatty meal (Ongoing)
• Supplement grade: 500mg/day — Daily oral (Ongoing)
• Clinical Dose: 500mg/day — Oral with or without food (Ongoing)
• Therapeutic: 1000mg/day — Oral with or without food (Ongoing)

Progression: Mitopure (Timeline Nutrition) is the only form with clinical trial validation. Generic alternatives may work but bioavailability is less established. Take with a fat-containing meal. Effects accumulate over weeks — allow 8-12 weeks before assessing.

Common protocols:
• Mitochondrial Longevity: Urolithin A 500mg/day (Mitopure), SS-31 5mg 4x/week SubQ, MOTS-c 5mg 3x/week SubQ, NMN 1000mg/day, Spermidine 5mg/day fasted
• Mitochondrial Health: Urolithin A 1g/day, CoQ10 300mg/day, PQQ 20mg/day, SS-31 1mg/day SubQ
• Longevity Core: Urolithin A 1g/day, Spermidine 1mg/day, NMN 1g/day, Rapamycin 5mg/week (physician supervised)

Monitoring: Exercise capacity and endurance self-assessment. Grip strength testing. Energy levels. No specific blood monitoring — consider VO2 max testing if serious longevity tracking.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. Mitopure has GRAS notification. Human clinical trial validated.

entries.title: Alpha-Ketoglutarate (AKG)
entries.subtitle: alpha-ketoglutaric acid, calcium AKG, AAKG
entries.text:
Alpha-Ketoglutarate (AKG) (alpha-ketoglutaric acid, calcium AKG, AAKG) — Performance and Recovery

Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG) is a key intermediate in the Krebs cycle (TCA cycle) — the cellular energy production pathway — and a cofactor for hundreds of enzymatic reactions. Research demonstrates AKG levels decline dramatically with age. A landmark 2020 Cell Metabolism study showed calcium AKG supplementation extended healthy lifespan in mice by 12% and compressed morbidity. AKG inhibits mTOR (like rapamycin but via different mechanism), activates AMPK, supports collagen synthesis (cofactor for prolyl hydroxylase), and reduces epigenetic age in a small human trial. Growing use in longevity protocols as an accessible, safe mTOR-modulating compound.

Reported benefits:
• Key Krebs cycle intermediate — fundamental energy metabolism
• 2020 Cell Metabolism lifespan extension study
• Inhibits mTOR — longevity mechanism similar to rapamycin
• AMPK activation — metabolic health
• Cofactor for collagen synthesis (prolyl hydroxylase)
• Reduced epigenetic age in human trial
• Safe and well-tolerated

Risks and trade-offs:
• Human longevity data very preliminary — mostly animal
• GI discomfort at higher doses for some
• AAKG (arginine AKG) vs calcium AKG are different compounds
• Calcium AKG is the longevity-studied form — verify formulation
• Best form for longevity is calcium AKG, not the bodybuilding AAKG form
• Not FDA approved as longevity compound

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Longevity: 1000-2000mg calcium AKG/day — Daily oral with food (Ongoing)
• Exercise performance: 3-6g AAKG — Pre-workout oral (As needed)

Progression: Calcium AKG is the longevity-relevant form (used in Cell Metabolism study). AAKG (arginine-AKG) is the bodybuilding form with different effects. Specify calcium AKG when purchasing for longevity use. Can be taken with other longevity compounds.

Common protocols:
• Longevity Stack: Calcium AKG 1000mg/day, Rapamycin 6mg weekly, Metformin 500mg/day, NMN 1000mg/day, Testosterone TRT dose

Monitoring: Exercise capacity, energy, inflammatory markers. No specific blood monitoring. Epigenetic age testing (TruAge, Elysium Index) if tracking biological age.

Regulatory status: Dietary supplement — no FDA drug approval. GRAS status. Growing longevity research base.

entries.title: Testosterone Pellets
entries.subtitle: Testopel, subcutaneous pellet implant, BHRT pellets
entries.text:
Testosterone Pellets (Testopel, subcutaneous pellet implant, BHRT pellets) — Performance and Recovery

Testosterone pellets are small crystalline cylinders (typically 75mg each) implanted subcutaneously in the buttock or hip area every 3-6 months by a physician. They provide steady, consistent testosterone delivery without the peaks and troughs of injections or the daily application of gels. Testopel is FDA-approved. Pellets dissolve slowly over 3-6 months releasing testosterone directly into surrounding tissue and vasculature. Growing in popularity particularly among TRT clinics serving women with HSDD and men who prefer fewer interventions. Hormone levels are more consistent than injections — no weekly injection peaks — but dosing adjustments require waiting for the pellet to dissolve.

Reported benefits:
• Consistent steady-state testosterone — no injection peaks and troughs
• Every 3-6 months — minimal intervention burden
• FDA approved (Testopel)
• No daily application — superior to gels for compliance
• Growing clinic revenue stream — high margin procedure
• Well-suited for women's BHRT testosterone therapy

Risks and trade-offs:
• Dosing cannot be adjusted once implanted — must wait for dissolution
• Minor surgical procedure — trocar insertion under local anesthesia
• Risk of extrusion (pellet works out) — 1-5%
• Infection risk at insertion site (low but real)
• More expensive than injectable TRT per dose
• No ability to stop therapy immediately if side effects emerge

Dosing discussed in the literature:
• Men — TRT: 600-1200mg total (8-16 x 75mg pellets) — Implanted every 3-5 months (Ongoing — physician managed)
• Women — BHRT: 75-225mg total (1-3 pellets) — Implanted every 3-4 months (Ongoing — physician managed)

Progression: Procedure performed under local anesthesia — 5-10 minutes. Avoid vigorous exercise and hot tubs for 5-7 days post-insertion. Levels checked at 4 weeks to confirm absorption. Next insertion typically at 80% dissolution.
