entries.title: High prolactin
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
High prolactin — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Most often from 19-nor compounds (nandrolone, trenbolone).

Signs: Nipple sensitivity or discharge, killed libido, erectile trouble, flat mood.

Labs: Serum prolactin. Confirm it is actually elevated before treating — these symptoms overlap with high and low E2.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Cabergoline is the commonly used dopamine agonist; literature dosing is typically 0.25 mg twice weekly, titrated on labs.
• Reduce or drop the 19-nor — the response treats the number, not the cause.
• P5P (active B6) is a mild adjunct discussed in the community; evidence is thin.

entries.title: High estradiol
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
High estradiol — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Aromatization of testosterone — scales with dose and body fat.

Signs: Water retention, puffy or sensitive nipples, moodiness, elevated blood pressure.

Labs: Sensitive (LC/MS) estradiol assay — the standard assay reads high on cycle and misleads.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Lowering the testosterone dose is the cleanest fix and often enough.
• Anastrozole: commonly cited on-cycle use is 0.25–0.5 mg two to three times weekly — it accumulates (t½ ~46 h), so start low.
• Exemestane 12.5 mg every other day is the commonly cited steroidal alternative; harder to crash E2 with and kinder to lipids.

entries.title: Crashed estradiol
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Crashed estradiol — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Overshooting an AI — usually stacked anastrozole doses taken off symptoms.

Signs: Dry, cracking joints, dead libido, fatigue, anxiety or doom feeling, poor sleep.

Labs: Sensitive estradiol — single digits confirms it.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Stop the AI entirely. Do not taper — just stop.
• E2 rebuilds as testosterone aromatizes; expect several days to two weeks to feel normal.
• Resume the AI, if at all, at a fraction of the prior dose once labs justify it.

entries.title: High hematocrit
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
High hematocrit — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Testosterone drives red cell production; worse with higher doses and sleep apnea.

Signs: Often silent. Flushed face, headaches, high BP at the extreme.

Labs: CBC — hematocrit and hemoglobin. Hydrate normally before the draw; dehydration fakes a high reading. Track ferritin alongside.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Above roughly 52–54%, clinicians typically act: dose reduction, injection frequency increase (smaller, more frequent doses flatten peaks), or supervised therapeutic phlebotomy.
• Regular cardio measurably helps plasma volume.
• Screen for sleep apnea — it compounds erythrocytosis.

entries.title: Rising blood pressure
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Rising blood pressure — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Water retention from E2, hematocrit, stimulants, or the compounds themselves (especially orals and tren).

Signs: Headaches, visual changes at the extreme — usually silent. Buy a cuff.

Labs: Home BP log, morning and evening. CMP for kidney markers on long cycles.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Fix the drivers first: E2 control, hematocrit, sodium, bodyweight.
• Telmisartan is the commonly discussed agent in the community for on-cycle BP (ARB with favorable metabolic profile) — prescription territory.
• Cardio again. It is the cheapest BP drug there is.

entries.title: Lipid strain
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Lipid strain — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Orals and DHT-derivatives crush HDL; injectables strain lipids less.

Signs: None — labs only.

Labs: Lipid panel (fasted): HDL, LDL, ApoB if available.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Time-box oral compounds; HDL typically recovers weeks after stopping.
• Omega-3 (2–4 g EPA/DHA) and citrus bergamot are the commonly cited adjuncts.
• Keep cardio in the program; diet quality matters more on cycle, not less.

entries.title: Early gyno signs
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Early gyno signs — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Estrogen or prolactin activity at breast tissue — puffy, itchy, or tender nipple, or a small firm lump under the areola.

Signs: Itch and puffiness first, palpable lump second. Early action matters — established tissue rarely regresses without surgery.

Labs: Sensitive E2 and prolactin, to identify which pathway is driving it.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Address the cause immediately (AI for E2-driven, cabergoline for prolactin-driven, or drop the offending compound).
• Raloxifene 60 mg daily is the commonly cited SERM for reversal attempts at the tissue level; tamoxifen 20 mg daily is the older alternative.
• Give a reversal attempt weeks, not days, and get real medical involvement.

entries.title: HPTA suppression & recovery
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
HPTA suppression & recovery — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Any suppressive compound. The question is never if, only how deep and how long.

Signs: Post-cycle: fatigue, low mood, no libido — the low-T package.

Labs: LH, FSH, total and free testosterone. Recovery is confirmed on paper, not by feel.

Commonly discussed responses:
• On TRT for life: recovery protocols don’t apply — this section is for cycling without a TRT base.
• Wait out the ester before starting a restart protocol (long esters keep you suppressed for weeks after the last pin).
• SERM-based restarts (clomiphene, enclomiphene, or tamoxifen at commonly cited doses) are the standard framework; HCG during the cycle preserves testicular volume and shortens the road back.

entries.title: Hair shedding
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Hair shedding — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: DHT and DHT-derived compounds in the androgen-sensitive.

Signs: Increased shed at the crown and temples, visible in the drain.

Labs: None useful — genetics decide this one.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Compound selection is the real lever: nandrolone and less androgenic choices shed less than masteron, winstrol, or high-dose test.
• Topical ketoconazole and minoxidil are the low-risk adjuncts.
• Finasteride/dutasteride block T→DHT conversion and can help on testosterone.

entries.title: Injection-site reactions
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
Injection-site reactions — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Technique, oil concentration and volume, unsanitary practice, or immune response to the carrier.

Signs: Post-injection pain (PIP), lumps, redness. Normal PIP fades over days and stays local.

Labs: None — but know the red flags below.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Rotate sites religiously (the app tracks this), warm the oil to body temperature, inject slowly, use a fresh needle to inject (not the draw needle).
• High-concentration blends (e.g. anything 300+ mg/ml) hurt — diluting with a second compound or carrier is why people combine syringes.
• Massage and warmth after help dispersal.

entries.title: GLP-1 side effects
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
GLP-1 side effects — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: Semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide — delayed gastric emptying does the work and causes the trouble.

Signs: Nausea, reflux, constipation, early satiety. Worst in the days after a dose increase.

Labs: None routinely; lipase if significant abdominal pain.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Titrate slower — the schedule printed on the pen is the fastest allowed, not the required pace.
• Smaller meals, less fat per sitting, stop eating at first fullness, hydrate hard.
• Time the weekly dose so the roughest 48 hours land on easy days.

entries.title: GH secretagogue effects
entries.subtitle: side-effect playbook
entries.text:
GH secretagogue effects — what it is and what to do

Usual causes: MK-677, GHRP-2/6, ipamorelin, CJC — water retention and blood-sugar drift come with the territory.

Signs: Tingling hands or carpal-tunnel feeling, puffiness, vivid dreams, raging hunger (GHRP-6 and MK-677 especially).

Labs: Fasting glucose and HbA1c on anything run for months — GH antagonizes insulin.

Commonly discussed responses:
• Water symptoms usually settle in 2–3 weeks; if not, the dose is too high.
• Take MK-677 at night to sleep through the hunger wave.
• Ipamorelin is the selective choice — GHRP-6 and hexarelin also bump cortisol and prolactin at higher doses.

entries.title: Never Combine GLP-1 Agonists
entries.subtitle: Semaglutide + Tirzepatide
entries.text:
Never Combine GLP-1 Agonists — Do not combine

Compounds: Semaglutide + Tirzepatide

Combining two GLP-1 or dual GLP-1/GIP agonists dramatically increases risk of severe GI side effects, pancreatitis, and offers no additive benefit. Choose one.

Monitoring: Do not combine. If switching agents, wash out first GLP-1 before starting the second.

entries.title: Do Not Double-Stack Aromatase Inhibitors
entries.subtitle: Anastrozole + Exemestane
terms: do not double stack aromatase inhibitors
entries.text:
Do Not Double-Stack Aromatase Inhibitors — Do not combine

Compounds: Anastrozole + Exemestane

Using two AIs simultaneously causes severe estrogen crash leading to joint pain, depression, osteoporosis risk, and cardiovascular damage. Use one AI only, guided by bloodwork.

Monitoring: E2 sensitive assay, Total T, bone density if long-term.

entries.title: Nandrolone Requires Testosterone Base
entries.subtitle: Nandrolone Decanoate + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
Nandrolone Requires Testosterone Base — Worth knowing

Compounds: Nandrolone Decanoate + Testosterone Cypionate

Nandrolone strongly suppresses natural testosterone. Running it without an adequate testosterone base causes 'Deca Dick' — severe sexual dysfunction and low mood. Always run Test:Deca at minimum 1:1 ratio.

Monitoring: Total T, E2, Prolactin (nandrolone raises prolactin), Hematocrit, Libido self-assessment.

entries.title: Cardarine Cancer Risk — Use With Caution
entries.subtitle: Cardarine + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: cardarine cancer risk — use with caution
cardarine cancer risk use with caution
entries.text:
Cardarine Cancer Risk — Use With Caution — Use caution

Compounds: Cardarine + Testosterone Cypionate

Cardarine (GW-501516) was abandoned by GSK due to rapid multi-tissue cancer development in animal studies. Combining with androgens (which promote cellular growth) may compound this risk. Many physicians advise against Cardarine use entirely.

Monitoring: If used, shortest cycle possible. Regular cancer screening awareness. Liver enzymes.

entries.title: HCG Must Stop Before PCT SERMs Begin
entries.subtitle: HCG + Tamoxifen
terms: hcg must stop before pct serms begin
entries.text:
HCG Must Stop Before PCT SERMs Begin — Use caution

Compounds: HCG + Tamoxifen

HCG should be used during the last 2 weeks of a cycle to prime the testes, then stopped completely before starting Nolvadex or Clomid. Running HCG concurrently with SERMs blunts the PCT response by continuing LH suppression via HCG's action.

Monitoring: Timing critical: Stop HCG, wait 2 weeks after last long-ester injection, then start SERMs.

entries.title: HCG Must Stop Before PCT SERMs Begin
entries.subtitle: HCG + Clomiphene
terms: hcg must stop before pct serms begin
entries.text:
HCG Must Stop Before PCT SERMs Begin — Use caution

Compounds: HCG + Clomiphene

Same as above — HCG and SERMs work at cross purposes during PCT. HCG ends the cycle phase; SERMs begin the PCT phase. They should not overlap.

Monitoring: Sequential use only: HCG during cycle, SERMs after.

entries.title: IGF-1 Hypoglycemia Risk Amplified
entries.subtitle: IGF-1 LR3 + Recombinant HGH
entries.text:
IGF-1 Hypoglycemia Risk Amplified — Use caution

Compounds: IGF-1 LR3 + Recombinant HGH

Both HGH and IGF-1 LR3 lower blood sugar. Combining them significantly amplifies hypoglycemia risk, especially post-workout when glucose is already depleted. Fast-acting carbohydrates must be on hand.

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, post-injection glucose monitoring, always have fast carbohydrates available.

entries.title: GHRP Stacking Increases Cortisol and Prolactin
entries.subtitle: Hexarelin + GHRP-2
terms: ghrp stacking increases cortisol and prolactin
entries.text:
GHRP Stacking Increases Cortisol and Prolactin — Use caution

Compounds: Hexarelin + GHRP-2

Stacking two GHRPs amplifies cortisol and prolactin elevation beyond what either compound causes alone. If dual-GHRP use is desired, use lowest effective doses and monitor prolactin.

Monitoring: Prolactin, Cortisol, IGF-1. Consider Cabergoline if prolactin elevates.

entries.title: GHRP Stacking Increases Cortisol and Prolactin
entries.subtitle: Hexarelin + GHRP-6
terms: ghrp stacking increases cortisol and prolactin
entries.text:
GHRP Stacking Increases Cortisol and Prolactin — Use caution

Compounds: Hexarelin + GHRP-6

Stacking two GHRPs amplifies cortisol and prolactin elevation. Use lowest effective doses and monitor prolactin.

Monitoring: Prolactin, Cortisol, IGF-1. Consider Cabergoline if prolactin elevates.

entries.title: Comprehensive Hormone Management Stack
entries.subtitle: Cabergoline + Anastrozole
entries.text:
Comprehensive Hormone Management Stack — Worth knowing

Compounds: Cabergoline + Anastrozole

Using both an AI and a dopamine agonist together is appropriate when running progestogenic compounds like nandrolone that raise both estrogen and prolactin. Ensure each is dosed based on its respective lab value — E2 guides AI dose, prolactin guides Cabergoline dose.

Monitoring: E2 (sensitive), Prolactin, Total T every 6-8 weeks.

entries.title: DHT Suppression Trade-offs With TRT
entries.subtitle: Dutasteride + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: dht suppression trade offs with trt
entries.text:
DHT Suppression Trade-offs With TRT — Worth knowing

Compounds: Dutasteride + Testosterone Cypionate

Dutasteride suppresses ~90% of DHT conversion from testosterone. This prevents hair loss but reduces libido, erection quality, mood, and muscle fullness in some men. The trade-off is significant — weigh hair preservation vs androgenic benefits of DHT.

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, DHT if testable, libido and sexual function self-assessment monthly.

entries.title: DHT Suppression Trade-offs With TRT
entries.subtitle: Finasteride + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: dht suppression trade offs with trt
entries.text:
DHT Suppression Trade-offs With TRT — Worth knowing

Compounds: Finasteride + Testosterone Cypionate

Finasteride suppresses ~70% of DHT. Risk of Post-Finasteride Syndrome (persistent sexual dysfunction) exists in a subset of users. If symptoms develop, discontinue immediately.

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, libido and sexual function. Discontinue if persistent sexual or mood side effects occur.

entries.title: Synergistic HPG Axis Restoration
entries.subtitle: Kisspeptin-10 + Clomiphene
entries.text:
Synergistic HPG Axis Restoration — Worth knowing

Compounds: Kisspeptin-10 + Clomiphene

Kisspeptin-10 acts upstream of GnRH while Clomid acts at the hypothalamic estrogen receptor — together they stimulate the HPG axis at multiple points. This combination may be more effective than either alone for secondary hypogonadism recovery.

Monitoring: Total T, LH, FSH, E2 every 4 weeks. LH surge post-Kisspeptin confirms receptor function.

entries.title: Excellent GHRH + GHRP Synergistic Pairing
entries.subtitle: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin
entries.text:
Excellent GHRH + GHRP Synergistic Pairing — Worth knowing

Compounds: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin

Tesamorelin (GHRH analogue) and Ipamorelin (GHRP) work synergistically to produce larger GH pulses than either alone — the GHRH primes the somatotrophs and the GHRP amplifies the pulse. This is the FDA-validated compound type pairing with the most evidence.

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months, fasting glucose, HbA1c.

entries.title: Gold Standard Injury Recovery Combination
entries.subtitle: BPC-157 + TB-500
entries.text:
Gold Standard Injury Recovery Combination — Worth knowing

Compounds: BPC-157 + TB-500

BPC-157 and TB-500 are synergistic — BPC-157 acts locally on tissue repair mechanisms while TB-500 promotes systemic cell migration and actin upregulation. Together they represent the most comprehensive peptide approach to injury recovery.

Monitoring: No specific labs. Monitor healing progress and injection sites.

entries.title: GLP-1 + Testosterone — Essential Muscle Preservation
entries.subtitle: Semaglutide + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
GLP-1 + Testosterone — Essential Muscle Preservation — Worth knowing

Compounds: Semaglutide + Testosterone Cypionate

GLP-1 agents cause significant muscle loss without adequate testosterone support. Running TRT-dose testosterone alongside semaglutide is strongly recommended to preserve lean mass during weight loss. Resistance training is also essential.

Monitoring: Body composition (DEXA preferred), Total T, HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids.

entries.title: GLP-1 + Testosterone — Essential Muscle Preservation
entries.subtitle: Tirzepatide + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
GLP-1 + Testosterone — Essential Muscle Preservation — Worth knowing

Compounds: Tirzepatide + Testosterone Cypionate

Same as semaglutide — tirzepatide's superior fat loss effect also means superior muscle loss risk without testosterone support. TRT-dose testosterone is strongly recommended alongside any GLP-1 agent.

Monitoring: Body composition (DEXA preferred), Total T, HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids.

entries.title: SARM + Testosterone — Amplified Suppression
entries.subtitle: RAD-140 + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
SARM + Testosterone — Amplified Suppression — Use caution

Compounds: RAD-140 + Testosterone Cypionate

Adding a SARM to a testosterone cycle significantly amplifies HPTA suppression. Post-cycle recovery will be more challenging and require a comprehensive PCT. Not recommended for beginners.

Monitoring: Full bloodwork before, mid-cycle, end-cycle and post-PCT. Liver enzymes critical with RAD-140.

entries.title: SARM + Testosterone — Amplified Suppression
entries.subtitle: Ligandrol + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
SARM + Testosterone — Amplified Suppression — Use caution

Compounds: Ligandrol + Testosterone Cypionate

LGD-4033 is the most suppressive SARM. Adding it to a testosterone cycle amplifies suppression significantly and will require a full PCT. Liver enzymes should be monitored throughout.

Monitoring: Full bloodwork including liver enzymes every 4 weeks. Full PCT required.

entries.title: Gold Standard GH Secretagogue Pairing
entries.subtitle: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin
entries.text:
Gold Standard GH Secretagogue Pairing — Worth knowing

Compounds: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin

CJC-1295 (GHRH analogue) and Ipamorelin (selective GHRP) are the gold standard GH secretagogue combination. CJC-1295 primes pituitary somatotrophs while Ipamorelin triggers GH release with minimal cortisol or prolactin elevation. Always pair these — neither is as effective alone.

Monitoring: IGF-1 every 3 months. Fasting glucose. No prolactin monitoring needed with Ipamorelin.

entries.title: T3 + Testosterone — Metabolic Synergy
entries.subtitle: Liothyronine (T3) + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
T3 + Testosterone — Metabolic Synergy — Worth knowing

Compounds: Liothyronine (T3) + Testosterone Cypionate

T3 and testosterone work synergistically for body composition. T3 increases metabolic rate and fat oxidation while testosterone preserves and builds lean mass. A common optimization combination. Monitor carefully as T3 can increase protein catabolism at high doses.

Monitoring: Free T3, Free T4, TSH, Total T, heart rate (resting), body composition.

entries.title: T3 + GLP-1 — Powerful Fat Loss Combination
entries.subtitle: Liothyronine (T3) + Tirzepatide
terms: t3 + glp-1 — powerful fat loss combination
t3 glp 1 powerful fat loss combination
entries.text:
T3 + GLP-1 — Powerful Fat Loss Combination — Worth knowing

Compounds: Liothyronine (T3) + Tirzepatide

T3 and GLP-1 agents both reduce body fat via complementary mechanisms. T3 increases basal metabolic rate; GLP-1 reduces appetite. Combined, they can produce significant fat loss. Add testosterone to prevent muscle loss in this combination.

Monitoring: Heart rate, body weight weekly, Free T3 to avoid hyperthyroidism, fasting glucose.

entries.title: Never Double-Dose T3
entries.subtitle: Liothyronine (T3) + Liothyronine (T3)
entries.text:
Never Double-Dose T3 — Do not combine

Compounds: Liothyronine (T3) + Liothyronine (T3)

T3 has a narrow therapeutic window. Taking more than prescribed can cause cardiac arrhythmias, bone density loss, and hyperthyroid crisis. Use exactly as directed.

Monitoring: Heart rate (keep under 80 resting), Free T3, symptoms of hyperthyroidism.

entries.title: DHEA + Testosterone — Verify No Excess Estrogen
entries.subtitle: DHEA + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: dhea + testosterone — verify no excess estrogen
dhea testosterone verify no excess estrogen
entries.text:
DHEA + Testosterone — Verify No Excess Estrogen — Worth knowing

Compounds: DHEA + Testosterone Cypionate

DHEA can convert to both testosterone and estrogen. Adding DHEA to a TRT protocol may raise estrogen further. Monitor E2 closely and do not add DHEA without baseline DHEA-S testing.

Monitoring: DHEA-S, Total T, Free T, E2 (sensitive assay), PSA. Recheck 6 weeks after adding DHEA.

entries.title: DHEA May Partially Offset AI Effect
entries.subtitle: DHEA + Anastrozole
terms: dhea may partially offset ai effect
entries.text:
DHEA May Partially Offset AI Effect — Use caution

Compounds: DHEA + Anastrozole

DHEA aromatizes to estrogen, potentially undermining the estrogen-lowering effect of anastrozole. If using both, E2 monitoring is especially important to confirm AI is achieving target levels.

Monitoring: E2 sensitive assay every 6-8 weeks. Adjust anastrozole dose based on labs only.

entries.title: Pregnenolone + DHEA — Comprehensive Adrenal Stack
entries.subtitle: Pregnenolone + DHEA
entries.text:
Pregnenolone + DHEA — Comprehensive Adrenal Stack — Worth knowing

Compounds: Pregnenolone + DHEA

Pregnenolone is the upstream precursor to DHEA. Using both ensures the adrenal hormone cascade is supported at multiple levels. Start with lower doses of each to assess conversion patterns before increasing.

Monitoring: Pregnenolone, DHEA-S, Total T, E2, Cortisol AM. Downstream hormones shift with both compounds.

entries.title: Metformin + TRT — Insulin Sensitivity Benefits
entries.subtitle: Metformin + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
Metformin + TRT — Insulin Sensitivity Benefits — Worth knowing

Compounds: Metformin + Testosterone Cypionate

Metformin improves insulin sensitivity and activates AMPK — complementary to testosterone's anabolic effects. Some research suggests metformin may slightly reduce testosterone levels; ensure adequate TRT dose and monitor labs.

Monitoring: Total T, Free T, HbA1c, fasting glucose, Vitamin B12 (metformin depletes B12 — supplement). Recheck labs at 8 weeks.

entries.title: Metformin + GLP-1 — Additive Metabolic Benefits
entries.subtitle: Metformin + Semaglutide
entries.text:
Metformin + GLP-1 — Additive Metabolic Benefits — Worth knowing

Compounds: Metformin + Semaglutide

Metformin and GLP-1 agents work via complementary mechanisms (AMPK activation vs GLP-1 receptor) and are commonly combined in diabetes management. Both reduce HbA1c and fasting glucose. Monitor for additive GI side effects.

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, weight, GI tolerance. B12 levels with long-term metformin.

entries.title: Metformin + Tirzepatide — Additive Metabolic Benefits
entries.subtitle: Metformin + Tirzepatide
entries.text:
Metformin + Tirzepatide — Additive Metabolic Benefits — Worth knowing

Compounds: Metformin + Tirzepatide

Same as metformin + semaglutide — complementary mechanisms with additive glucose-lowering and weight loss benefits. Combination used in clinical practice for T2 diabetes management.

Monitoring: HbA1c, fasting glucose, weight, GI tolerance, B12 levels.

entries.title: Berberine + Metformin — Avoid Combining Without Monitoring
entries.subtitle: Berberine + Metformin
terms: berberine + metformin — avoid combining without monitoring
berberine metformin avoid combining without monitoring
entries.text:
Berberine + Metformin — Avoid Combining Without Monitoring — Use caution

Compounds: Berberine + Metformin

Both activate AMPK and lower blood glucose via similar pathways. Combining can cause additive blood sugar lowering and increased GI side effects. If using both, start at lower doses and monitor glucose carefully.

Monitoring: Fasting glucose (hypoglycemia risk), GI symptoms, HbA1c. Consider using one or the other rather than both.

entries.title: LDN + BPC-157 — Synergistic Anti-inflammatory
entries.subtitle: Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN) + BPC-157
entries.text:
LDN + BPC-157 — Synergistic Anti-inflammatory — Worth knowing

Compounds: Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN) + BPC-157

LDN modulates immune function via TLR4 and endorphin upregulation while BPC-157 acts on gut healing and systemic inflammation. Together they address gut-brain-immune inflammation via complementary mechanisms. A popular combination in functional medicine.

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (CRP), gut symptom tracking, mood and energy self-assessment.

entries.title: Telmisartan + TRT — Recommended Cardiovascular Protection
entries.subtitle: Telmisartan + Testosterone Cypionate
entries.text:
Telmisartan + TRT — Recommended Cardiovascular Protection — Worth knowing

Compounds: Telmisartan + Testosterone Cypionate

TRT can raise blood pressure and hematocrit. Telmisartan addresses both concerns via angiotensin blockade and its PPAR-gamma activity improves insulin sensitivity. A thoughtful pairing for TRT patients with BP concerns.

Monitoring: Blood pressure, hematocrit, potassium, eGFR. Target BP under 130/80.

entries.title: VIP + BPC-157 — Comprehensive Gut and Immune Stack
entries.subtitle: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) + BPC-157
terms: vip + bpc-157 — comprehensive gut and immune stack
vip bpc 157 comprehensive gut and immune stack
entries.text:
VIP + BPC-157 — Comprehensive Gut and Immune Stack — Worth knowing

Compounds: VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide) + BPC-157

VIP and BPC-157 address gut inflammation via completely different mechanisms — VIP via mast cell stabilization and vasodilation, BPC-157 via tissue repair and GH receptor upregulation. Together they form a comprehensive gut and immune repair protocol.

Monitoring: Inflammatory markers (TGF-beta1, C4a for CIRS), gut symptom tracking, blood pressure (VIP can cause hypotension).

entries.title: Thymosin Alpha-1 + LDN — Immune Modulation Stack
entries.subtitle: Thymosin Alpha-1 + Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN)
terms: thymosin alpha-1 + ldn — immune modulation stack
thymosin alpha 1 ldn immune modulation stack
thymosin alpha 1 low dose naltrexone ldn
entries.text:
Thymosin Alpha-1 + LDN — Immune Modulation Stack — Worth knowing

Compounds: Thymosin Alpha-1 + Low-Dose Naltrexone (LDN)

Ta1 enhances T-cell and NK cell function while LDN modulates innate immunity via TLR4. Together they address both adaptive and innate immune pathways — a comprehensive immune optimization combination.

Monitoring: CBC with differential (immune cells), inflammatory markers, infection frequency tracking.

entries.title: 7-Keto DHEA + DHEA — Complementary Adrenal Support
entries.subtitle: 7-Keto DHEA + DHEA
terms: 7 keto dhea dhea complementary adrenal support
entries.text:
7-Keto DHEA + DHEA — Complementary Adrenal Support — Worth knowing

Compounds: 7-Keto DHEA + DHEA

7-Keto DHEA provides metabolic benefits without hormonal conversion while DHEA provides precursor hormone support. Together they offer broader adrenal optimization. Monitor downstream hormones from DHEA conversion.

Monitoring: DHEA-S, Total T, E2. 7-Keto DHEA itself requires no hormonal monitoring.

entries.title: T4 + T3 Combination Therapy
entries.subtitle: Levothyroxine (T4) + Liothyronine (T3)
entries.text:
T4 + T3 Combination Therapy — Worth knowing

Compounds: Levothyroxine (T4) + Liothyronine (T3)

Combination T4/T3 therapy is used when T4 monotherapy leaves patients symptomatic due to poor conversion. The typical ratio is 4:1 T4:T3 (mirroring NDT). Start with low T3 addition (5-10mcg) and titrate based on Free T3 target.

Monitoring: Free T4, Free T3, TSH, heart rate, symptoms of both hypo and hyperthyroidism.

entries.title: NDT Already Contains T3 — Avoid Adding More Without Monitoring
entries.subtitle: Natural Desiccated Thyroid (NDT) + Liothyronine (T3)
terms: ndt already contains t3 — avoid adding more without monitoring
ndt already contains t3 avoid adding more without monitoring
natural desiccated thyroid ndt liothyronine t3
entries.text:
NDT Already Contains T3 — Avoid Adding More Without Monitoring — Use caution

Compounds: Natural Desiccated Thyroid (NDT) + Liothyronine (T3)

NDT contains both T4 and T3 (approximately 4:1 ratio). Adding additional T3 can cause hyperthyroidism symptoms. If symptoms suggest inadequate T3, adjust NDT dose before adding separate T3.

Monitoring: Free T3, Free T4, TSH, heart rate (target 60-80 resting). Symptoms of hyperthyroidism.

entries.title: Metformin + GH Secretagogues — Monitor Glucose
entries.subtitle: Metformin + CJC-1295
entries.text:
Metformin + GH Secretagogues — Monitor Glucose — Worth knowing

Compounds: Metformin + CJC-1295

GH secretagogues can reduce insulin sensitivity while metformin improves it. The two may partially offset each other's metabolic effects. Metformin can act as a useful safety net for glucose management when using GH peptides long-term.

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, IGF-1. The combination is reasonable — just monitor metabolic markers.

entries.title: DHEA + Cardarine — Compounding Cancer Risk
entries.subtitle: DHEA + Cardarine (GW-501516)
entries.text:
DHEA + Cardarine — Compounding Cancer Risk — Do not combine

Compounds: DHEA + Cardarine (GW-501516)

Cardarine was abandoned by GSK due to multi-tissue cancer development in animals. DHEA promotes cell growth via its conversion to sex hormones. Combining a potential carcinogen with a growth-promoting hormone warrants serious caution.

Monitoring: If using Cardarine at all, avoid adding growth-promoting hormones. Many practitioners advise against Cardarine entirely.

entries.title: SS-31 + MOTS-c — Comprehensive Mitochondrial Stack
entries.subtitle: SS-31 + MOTS-c
terms: ss 31 mots c comprehensive mitochondrial stack
entries.text:
SS-31 + MOTS-c — Comprehensive Mitochondrial Stack — Worth knowing

Compounds: SS-31 + MOTS-c

SS-31 targets the inner mitochondrial membrane (cardiolipin) while MOTS-c activates AMPK and nuclear gene expression. Together they address mitochondrial function at two distinct levels — membrane integrity and metabolic signaling.

Monitoring: Energy and exercise capacity self-assessment, VO2 max if available, fasting glucose.

entries.title: Insulin + GLP-1 agonist — Additive Hypoglycemia
entries.subtitle: Insulin + Semaglutide
entries.text:
Insulin + GLP-1 agonist — Additive Hypoglycemia — Do not combine

Compounds: Insulin + Semaglutide

A recognised clinical interaction, not a theoretical one. GLP-1 agonists lower glucose and suppress appetite, so a person on both eats less and clears glucose faster while the insulin dose stays where it was. Diabetes guidelines call for the insulin dose to be reduced when a GLP-1 is started or escalated. The same applies to tirzepatide. Severe hypoglycemia in this combination is well documented and is why it belongs to a prescriber, not to a spreadsheet.

Monitoring: Glucose before and after every dose and before sleep, and a continuous monitor if one is available. Reduce insulin under medical supervision when starting or increasing a GLP-1 — never in the other order.

entries.title: Insulin + Growth Hormone — The Combination Behind the Case Reports
entries.subtitle: Insulin + Recombinant HGH
terms: insulin + growth hormone — the combination behind the case reports
insulin growth hormone the combination behind the case reports
entries.text:
Insulin + Growth Hormone — The Combination Behind the Case Reports — Do not combine

Compounds: Insulin + Recombinant HGH

Growth hormone raises blood glucose and induces insulin resistance over hours to days; insulin lowers glucose over minutes. The two effects run on completely different clocks, which is exactly why the pairing is dangerous: an insulin amount that was tolerable alongside GH one week can be far too much on a day the GH is skipped, the dose changes, or food does not arrive on schedule. This is the combination that appears in the published bodybuilding fatality and hypoglycemic brain injury reports.

Monitoring: Fasting glucose, HbA1c and IGF-1. Glucose checked before and after each insulin dose and again before sleep. Anyone using both should have fast-acting carbohydrate to hand and a person nearby who knows what has been taken.

entries.title: Insulin + T3 — Wider Swings, Usually While Under-Eating
entries.subtitle: Insulin + Liothyronine (T3)
terms: insulin + t3 — wider swings, usually while under-eating
insulin t3 wider swings usually while under eating
entries.text:
Insulin + T3 — Wider Swings, Usually While Under-Eating — Use caution

Compounds: Insulin + Liothyronine (T3)

T3 raises glucose turnover and speeds insulin clearance, and it is most often used during a deficit, when carbohydrate intake is already low and unpredictable. The combination does not create a new mechanism; it widens the swing in both directions and removes the dietary buffer that makes an insulin dose forgiving. Missed or delayed meals are the usual trigger.

Monitoring: Glucose before and after doses, TSH, free T3 and free T4, potassium, and resting heart rate. Treat any day with a missed or delayed meal as a day the numbers no longer apply.

entries.title: Gonadorelin and HCG — Choose One for Testicular Maintenance
entries.subtitle: Gonadorelin + HCG
terms: gonadorelin and hcg — choose one for testicular maintenance
gonadorelin and hcg choose one for testicular maintenance
entries.text:
Gonadorelin and HCG — Choose One for Testicular Maintenance — Use caution

Compounds: Gonadorelin + HCG

Both gonadorelin and HCG serve the same purpose on TRT — preserving testicular function. Gonadorelin stimulates LH/FSH from the pituitary; HCG mimics LH directly at the testes. Using both simultaneously is redundant and may cause over-stimulation. Choose one approach.

Monitoring: Total T, LH, FSH, E2, testicular volume. Monitor prolactin — over-stimulation can elevate it.

entries.title: MT-2 and PT-141 — Overlap in Mechanism
entries.subtitle: Melanotan II (MT-2) + PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
terms: mt-2 and pt-141 — overlap in mechanism
mt 2 and pt 141 overlap in mechanism
entries.text:
MT-2 and PT-141 — Overlap in Mechanism — Use caution

Compounds: Melanotan II (MT-2) + PT-141 (Bremelanotide)

MT-2 and PT-141 (bremelanotide) both activate MC4R for sexual function enhancement. They overlap significantly in mechanism. Using both simultaneously provides little additional benefit and increases side effect risk (nausea, flushing, blood pressure elevation). Use one at a time.

Monitoring: Blood pressure (both cause transient elevation), nausea assessment.

entries.title: Never Combine CJC-1295 and CJC-1295 DAC
entries.subtitle: CJC-1295 + CJC-1295 with DAC
terms: never combine cjc-1295 and cjc-1295 dac
never combine cjc 1295 and cjc 1295 dac
entries.text:
Never Combine CJC-1295 and CJC-1295 DAC — Do not combine

Compounds: CJC-1295 + CJC-1295 with DAC

These are two forms of the same compound. Combining them dramatically elevates IGF-1 and GH beyond safe physiological ranges. Use one or the other — not both.

Monitoring: IGF-1, fasting glucose. If accidentally combined, stop both and recheck IGF-1 in 2 weeks.

entries.title: Never Combine GLP-1 Class Agents
entries.subtitle: Retatrutide + Tirzepatide
entries.text:
Never Combine GLP-1 Class Agents — Do not combine

Compounds: Retatrutide + Tirzepatide

Retatrutide and tirzepatide both target GLP-1 receptors. Combining any two GLP-1/GIP/glucagon receptor agonists dramatically increases pancreatitis risk, severe GI events, and provides no additive weight loss benefit beyond one agent at maximum dose.

Monitoring: Amylase, lipase if any abdominal pain. Do not combine.

entries.title: Never Combine GLP-1 Class Agents
entries.subtitle: Retatrutide + Semaglutide
entries.text:
Never Combine GLP-1 Class Agents — Do not combine

Compounds: Retatrutide + Semaglutide

Same as above — retatrutide and semaglutide both target GLP-1 receptors. Never combine two agents from this class.

Monitoring: Do not combine. If switching agents, appropriate washout period required.

entries.title: MT-2 + TRT — Monitor Skin and E2
entries.subtitle: Melanotan II (MT-2) + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: mt-2 + trt — monitor skin and e2
mt 2 trt monitor skin and e2
entries.text:
MT-2 + TRT — Monitor Skin and E2 — Worth knowing

Compounds: Melanotan II (MT-2) + Testosterone Cypionate

MT-2 can darken existing moles and nevi. On TRT, where estrogen can also affect skin, monitoring skin changes is important. E2 optimization is also important as both estrogen and melanocortin pathways affect libido — don't over-suppress E2 if also using MT-2 for sexual function.

Monitoring: Dermatology skin check baseline and every 6 months. E2 (sensitive assay) — maintain 20-35 pg/mL for optimal libido synergy.

entries.title: Rapamycin + TRT — Monitor for mTOR Effects on Muscle
entries.subtitle: Rapamycin + Testosterone Cypionate
terms: rapamycin + trt — monitor for mtor effects on muscle
rapamycin trt monitor for mtor effects on muscle
entries.text:
Rapamycin + TRT — Monitor for mTOR Effects on Muscle — Worth knowing

Compounds: Rapamycin + Testosterone Cypionate

mTOR is required for muscle protein synthesis. Rapamycin's mTOR inhibition could theoretically blunt anabolic effects of testosterone. At weekly longevity doses (5-10mg), this effect is minimal due to intermittent dosing. Ensure adequate protein intake and resistance training.

Monitoring: Body composition, lean mass tracking, strength metrics. Dose rapamycin weekly (not daily) to minimize muscle synthesis blunting.

entries.title: Cagrilintide + Semaglutide — Intended Combination (CagriSema)
entries.subtitle: Cagrilintide + Semaglutide
entries.text:
Cagrilintide + Semaglutide — Intended Combination (CagriSema) — Worth knowing

Compounds: Cagrilintide + Semaglutide

Cagrilintide is specifically being developed in combination with semaglutide as CagriSema — a fixed-dose combination. Clinical trials show superior weight loss compared to either alone. This is an intended therapeutic combination, not a dangerous one. Monitor GI tolerance carefully.

Monitoring: GI tolerance, weight, HbA1c, fasting glucose. This combination requires gradual titration of both agents.

entries.title: Gonadorelin + Clomid — Synergistic HPG Restoration
entries.subtitle: Gonadorelin + Clomiphene
entries.text:
Gonadorelin + Clomid — Synergistic HPG Restoration — Worth knowing

Compounds: Gonadorelin + Clomiphene

Gonadorelin stimulates LH/FSH at the pituitary level while Clomid blocks hypothalamic estrogen receptors to increase GnRH pulsatility. Together they address HPG restoration at two distinct points. A potentially more comprehensive HPTA restart than either alone.

Monitoring: LH, FSH, Total T, E2 every 4 weeks. LH response to gonadorelin confirms pituitary function.

entries.title: Kisspeptin-54 + Gonadorelin — Upstream and Downstream HPG
entries.subtitle: Kisspeptin-54 + Gonadorelin
terms: kisspeptin-54 + gonadorelin — upstream and downstream hpg
kisspeptin 54 gonadorelin upstream and downstream hpg
entries.text:
Kisspeptin-54 + Gonadorelin — Upstream and Downstream HPG — Worth knowing

Compounds: Kisspeptin-54 + Gonadorelin

Kisspeptin acts upstream of GnRH neurons to trigger GnRH release, while gonadorelin IS GnRH acting directly on the pituitary. Using both covers the HPG axis at two levels but requires careful pulsatile timing for both. Both must be pulsatile — never continuous.

Monitoring: LH, FSH, Total T, E2. Both compounds require pulsatile dosing — coordinate timing to avoid receptor conflicts.

entries.title: TRT Starter Protocol
entries.subtitle: Beginner · Ongoing
entries.text:
TRT Starter Protocol — Beginner, Ongoing

Conservative first TRT protocol for those new to testosterone therapy. Focus on dialing in the foundation before adding anything else.

Compounds:
• Testosterone Cypionate: 100mg/week — Split: 50mg twice weekly (Mon/Thu) (Start conservative. Bloodwork at 6-8 weeks determines if adjustment needed.)
• HCG: 250IU twice weekly — Mon/Thu alongside Test injection (Preserves testicular volume and fertility. Optional but recommended under 45.)

PCT: N/A — TRT is ongoing. If discontinuing, consult physician.

Bloodwork: Baseline before starting. Recheck Total T, Free T, E2, SHBG, Hematocrit, PSA at 6-8 weeks. Titrate based on results.

Notes: Do NOT add anastrozole until you have bloodwork showing elevated E2 AND symptoms. Most men starting TRT do not need an AI immediately.

entries.title: Injury Recovery Protocol
entries.subtitle: Beginner · 8-12 weeks
entries.text:
Injury Recovery Protocol — Beginner, 8-12 weeks

The most validated peptide protocol for accelerating healing from tendon, ligament, muscle, or gut injury. No hormones required.

Compounds:
• BPC-157: 500mcg/day — 250mcg AM + 250mcg PM SubQ near injury (For gut issues use oral route. For musculoskeletal inject near the injury site.)
• TB-500: 2.5mg loading — Twice weekly for 4-6 weeks, then once weekly (Systemic complement to BPC-157. Promotes cell migration throughout the body.)

PCT: No PCT needed — no hormonal suppression.

Bloodwork: No specific labs required. Optional: inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) to track progress.

Notes: This stack is the most studied peptide combination for injury healing. Allow 2-4 weeks for initial response. Can run longer than most protocols given low risk profile.

entries.title: Anti-Aging GH Protocol
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 3 months on / 1 off
entries.text:
Anti-Aging GH Protocol — Intermediate, 3 months on / 1 off

Conservative GH axis optimization for anti-aging and body composition. Works within the natural feedback system.

Compounds:
• CJC-1295: 200mcg — Once before bed SubQ — fasted (Always combine with Ipamorelin. Fasted state is critical for GH release.)
• Ipamorelin: 200mcg — Once before bed with CJC-1295 (Gold standard GHRP pairing — most selective, fewest side effects.)

PCT: No PCT needed.

Bloodwork: IGF-1 at baseline and every 3 months. Fasting glucose. Target IGF-1 in upper third of normal range.

Notes: Advance to twice-daily dosing (fasted AM + pre-bed) after 4-6 weeks if well tolerated. Most users notice improved sleep quality within 2-3 weeks.

entries.title: Body Recomposition Stack
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 12-16 weeks
entries.text:
Body Recomposition Stack — Intermediate, 12-16 weeks

Comprehensive fat loss and muscle building protocol combining hormonal optimization, GH axis support, and metabolic enhancement.

Compounds:
• Testosterone Cypionate: 200mg/week — 100mg twice weekly (Mon/Thu) (Supraphysiological dose to support muscle during caloric deficit.)
• CJC-1295: 200mcg — Twice daily fasted (AM + pre-bed) (GH optimization for fat oxidation and recovery.)
• Ipamorelin: 200mcg — Twice daily fasted with CJC-1295 (Pair with CJC-1295 always.)
• Tirzepatide: Start 2.5mg/week — Weekly SubQ — titrate by 2.5mg every 4 weeks (Appetite control and insulin sensitization. Titrate slowly.)
• BPC-157: 250mcg twice daily — SubQ — helps gut during GLP-1 initiation (Reduces GI side effects during Tirzepatide titration.)

PCT: HCG 500IU 3x/week final 2 weeks of cycle, then Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg + Clomid 50/50/25/25mg.

Bloodwork: Baseline, 6-8 weeks, end of cycle. Add IGF-1, HbA1c, fasting glucose for GLP-1 monitoring.

Notes: Minimum 1g protein per lb body weight. Resistance training essential — GLP-1 without training causes significant muscle loss.

entries.title: Comprehensive Longevity Protocol
entries.subtitle: Advanced · Ongoing with pulse cycles
entries.text:
Comprehensive Longevity Protocol — Advanced, Ongoing with pulse cycles

A comprehensive longevity protocol combining TRT, GH axis optimization, cellular repair peptides, and Khavinson bioregulators.

Compounds:
• Testosterone Cypionate: 100-150mg/week — Twice weekly (Physiological TRT — cornerstone of male longevity.)
• Sermorelin: 300mcg — Before bed SubQ fasted (Conservative GH axis within natural feedback.)
• Ipamorelin: 300mcg — Before bed with Sermorelin (Amplifies GH pulse with Sermorelin.)
• BPC-157: 250mcg/day — SubQ daily (Systemic cellular repair and anti-inflammatory.)
• Epithalon: 10mg/day — 10-day pulse cycles spring and fall (Telomerase activation. Pulse twice yearly.)
• Thymalin: 10mg/day — 10-day pulse cycles annually (Thymic immune restoration. Most meaningful over 40.)
• NMN: 1000mg/day — Daily oral AM (NAD+ precursor for mitochondrial health.)

PCT: N/A — TRT is ongoing.

Bloodwork: Comprehensive annual panel: hormones, IGF-1, inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6), DHEA-S, thyroid, metabolic, DEXA scan.

Notes: Lifestyle fundamentals are non-negotiable: 7-9 hours sleep, resistance training, Mediterranean-style diet, stress management. Compounds amplify a healthy foundation — they cannot replace it.

entries.title: Aggressive Fat Loss
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 6-12 months
entries.text:
Aggressive Fat Loss — Intermediate, 6-12 months

Maximum fat loss protocol with muscle preservation. GLP-1 agent as primary driver with hormonal and GH support.

Compounds:
• Tirzepatide: Start 2.5mg/week — Weekly SubQ — titrate to 10-15mg over 3 months (Best-in-class fat loss. Slow titration minimizes nausea.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: 150-200mg/week — Twice weekly (Critical for muscle preservation during aggressive deficit.)
• CJC-1295: 200mcg — Twice daily fasted (GH directly stimulates lipolysis — amplifies fat loss.)
• Ipamorelin: 200mcg — Twice daily fasted with CJC-1295 (Pair with CJC-1295.)

PCT: Nolvadex 40/40/20/20/20/20mg + Clomid 50/50/25/25mg if running performance-level testosterone.

Bloodwork: HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, body composition monthly for first 3 months.

Notes: GLP-1 results compound over 6-12 months. Minimum 1g protein per lb body weight. Resistance training 3-4x per week non-negotiable.

entries.title: Standard PCT Protocol
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 6 weeks
entries.text:
Standard PCT Protocol — Intermediate, 6 weeks

Evidence-based post-cycle therapy for restoring the HPTA after a testosterone cycle.

Compounds:
• HCG: 500IU 3x/week — Final 2 weeks of cycle (then stop completely) (Primes testes before SERM PCT begins. Do NOT use during actual PCT.)
• Tamoxifen (Nolvadex): 40mg/day weeks 1-2, 20mg/day weeks 3-6 — Daily oral — start 2 weeks after last long-ester injection (Primary HPTA restart agent.)
• Clomiphene (Clomid): 50mg/day weeks 1-2, 25mg/day weeks 3-4 — Daily oral concurrent with Nolvadex (Stimulates LH/FSH production. Run alongside Nolvadex.)

PCT: This IS the PCT.

Bloodwork: Total T, LH, FSH, E2 at end of PCT and 4 weeks post-PCT. Goal: T returning toward baseline, LH/FSH rising.

Notes: Timing critical: HCG in last 2 weeks of cycle, stop HCG, wait 2 weeks, start SERMs. Support with Zinc 30mg/day, Vitamin D 5000IU, Ashwagandha 600mg for natural testosterone support.

entries.title: Thyroid Optimization Protocol
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 8-12 weeks
entries.text:
Thyroid Optimization Protocol — Intermediate, 8-12 weeks

A systematic approach to optimizing thyroid function — from initial T4 monotherapy to combination T3/T4 and natural desiccated thyroid options.

Compounds:
• Levothyroxine (T4): Start 50mcg/day, titrate to 100-125mcg — Daily oral on empty stomach 30-60 min before food (Start low and titrate every 6-8 weeks based on Free T4 and Free T3.)
• Liothyronine (T3): 5-12.5mcg/day (add if Free T3 remains low-normal) — Split dose — AM and noon (Only add T3 if symptomatic despite adequate Free T4. Start very low.)
• DHEA: 25mg/day AM — Daily oral with morning meal (Adrenal support — often needed alongside thyroid optimization.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing thyroid hormone replacement.

Bloodwork: Baseline: Free T4, Free T3, TSH, Reverse T3, TPO antibodies, DHEA-S, cortisol AM. Recheck every 6-8 weeks when adjusting.

Notes: Never dose thyroid by TSH alone. Target Free T3 in upper third of normal range for symptom relief. Take T4 consistently — absorption affected by coffee, calcium, iron, and food.

entries.title: Adrenal Hormone Restoration
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 3-6 months
entries.text:
Adrenal Hormone Restoration — Intermediate, 3-6 months

Systematic restoration of the adrenal hormone cascade — DHEA, pregnenolone, and downstream sex hormones for aging individuals with confirmed deficiency.

Compounds:
• Pregnenolone: 50-100mg/day — Daily oral AM with meal (The master precursor — start here. Assess downstream hormone response at 6-8 weeks.)
• DHEA: 25mg/day (men) or 10mg/day (women) — Daily oral AM (Add after establishing pregnenolone. Test DHEA-S before starting.)
• 7-Keto DHEA: 100mg 2x/day — Daily oral with meals (Metabolic complement — no hormonal conversion.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: TRT dose if indicated — Twice weekly (Often needed in men with confirmed low T alongside adrenal restoration.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing hormone optimization.

Bloodwork: DHEA-S, Total T, Free T, E2, Cortisol AM, Pregnenolone levels, Lipid panel. Baseline and every 6-8 weeks when adjusting.

Notes: Build the adrenal pyramid from the bottom up — cholesterol to pregnenolone to DHEA to sex hormones. Morning dosing for all adrenal compounds mimics the natural cortisol/adrenal rhythm.

entries.title: Advanced Longevity Protocol
entries.subtitle: Advanced · Ongoing
entries.text:
Advanced Longevity Protocol — Advanced, Ongoing

A comprehensive multi-pathway longevity protocol targeting mTOR, AMPK, NAD+, sirtuins, telomeres, mitochondria, and cellular cleanup simultaneously.

Compounds:
• Rapamycin: 5-6mg once weekly — Weekly oral fasted (mTOR inhibition — the most evidence-backed longevity intervention. Weekly not daily.)
• Metformin: 500mg/day — Daily oral with evening meal (AMPK activation — complementary to rapamycin. Take B12 supplement always.)
• NMN: 1000mg/day — Daily oral AM (NAD+ precursor — mitochondrial and DNA repair support.)
• Pterostilbene: 100mg/day — Daily oral with fat (Sirtuin activation — synergistic with NMN.)
• Epithalon: 10mg/day x 10 days — SubQ pulse cycles twice yearly (Telomerase activation — spring and fall pulse cycles.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: TRT dose — Twice weekly (Physiological testosterone — cornerstone of male longevity.)
• BPC-157: 250mcg/day — Daily SubQ (Systemic cellular repair and anti-inflammatory.)

PCT: N/A — TRT is ongoing.

Bloodwork: Comprehensive annual panel: hormones, IGF-1, HbA1c, lipids, CRP, IL-6, DHEA-S, complete metabolic, CBC. DEXA annually. B12 every 6 months (metformin depletes).

Notes: This protocol targets 6 hallmarks of aging simultaneously. Lifestyle fundamentals are the non-negotiable foundation — quality sleep, resistance training, Mediterranean diet, stress management, and social connection. Compounds amplify a healthy baseline; they cannot replace it.

entries.title: Post-Injury Return to Training
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 12-16 weeks
entries.text:
Post-Injury Return to Training — Intermediate, 12-16 weeks

Accelerated healing and return-to-performance protocol combining tissue repair peptides, anabolic support, and gradual loading progression.

Compounds:
• BPC-157: 500mcg/day — 250mcg AM + 250mcg PM SubQ near injury (Primary tissue healing compound. For gut injuries use oral route.)
• TB-500: 2.5mg twice weekly — SubQ loading phase 4-6 weeks, then once weekly (Systemic repair complement to BPC-157.)
• AOD-9604: 500mcg/day — SubQ daily AM fasted — near joint if applicable (Cartilage regeneration support — particularly relevant for joint injuries.)
• CJC-1295: 200mcg before bed — Daily SubQ fasted (GH critical for collagen synthesis and tissue repair.)
• Ipamorelin: 200mcg before bed — Daily SubQ with CJC-1295 (Pair with CJC-1295 always.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: 150-200mg/week — Twice weekly (Anabolic environment for tissue repair and maintenance of lean mass during restricted training.)

PCT: Nolvadex 40/40/20/20mg + Clomid 50/50/25/25mg if running above TRT dose.

Bloodwork: Baseline, 6 weeks, end of protocol. Focus on inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR), liver enzymes, hormone panel. Vitamin D levels (critical for tendon healing).

Notes: Follow a graduated loading protocol under physiotherapy guidance. Return to training too quickly is the most common mistake — peptides accelerate healing but do not eliminate the need for progressive rehabilitation. Ensure Vitamin D is optimal (60-80 ng/mL).

entries.title: Female Testosterone Optimization
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · Ongoing
entries.text:
Female Testosterone Optimization — Intermediate, Ongoing

Evidence-based testosterone therapy for women experiencing low libido, fatigue, and suboptimal body composition. Female TRT uses dramatically lower doses than male TRT.

Compounds:
• Testosterone Cypionate: 10-20mg/week (female dose) — Weekly SubQ injection OR twice weekly for steadier levels (Female dose is 10-20x lower than male TRT. Start at 10mg/week and titrate slowly based on Free T labs.)
• DHEA: 10-25mg/day — Daily oral AM (Adrenal androgen precursor — often helps libido and energy in women.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing therapy.

Bloodwork: Free T (critical — target 1.0-2.0 pg/mL for women), Total T, E2, SHBG, CBC, lipid panel every 6-8 weeks initially. Female testosterone reference ranges are much lower than male.

Notes: Female TRT requires more careful monitoring than male TRT. Virilization signs (voice changes, clitoral enlargement, acne, hair loss) signal excessive dosing — reduce dose immediately if any appear.

entries.title: Female BHRT Protocol
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · Ongoing
entries.text:
Female BHRT Protocol — Intermediate, Ongoing

Bioidentical hormone replacement therapy for perimenopause, menopause, or hormone optimization. Addresses estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone simultaneously.

Compounds:
• Estradiol (bioidentical): 0.5-2mg/day — Topical cream or patch daily (Bioidentical E2 — dosing guided by E2 labs and symptom relief. Transdermal preferred for cardiovascular safety.)
• Progesterone (bioidentical): 100-200mg — Oral capsule at bedtime (luteal phase or continuously) (Micronized progesterone (Prometrium) preferred. Take at bedtime — has sedating effect. Protects uterus if intact.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: 10-20mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Female TRT dose — improves libido, energy, and body composition.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing BHRT.

Bloodwork: E2, Progesterone, Free T, Total T, SHBG, FSH, LH every 6-8 weeks when adjusting. Target E2 50-150 pg/mL (follicular-like levels). Annual mammogram and pelvic exam.

Notes: All BHRT should be physician-supervised. Progestins (synthetic) are different from bioidentical progesterone — the latter has a more favorable safety profile. Annual breast and gynecological screening essential.

entries.title: Female GLP-1 + Hormone Protocol
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · 6-12 months
entries.text:
Female GLP-1 + Hormone Protocol — Intermediate, 6-12 months

GLP-1 agent combined with female hormone support for sustainable fat loss while preserving lean mass and hormonal balance.

Compounds:
• Semaglutide: Start 0.25mg/week — Weekly SubQ — titrate by 0.25mg every 4 weeks to max 2.4mg (Slow titration essential. Female patients often achieve good results at lower doses than male patients.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: 10-15mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Critical for muscle preservation during GLP-1 weight loss. Low female dose.)
• BPC-157: 250mcg/day — SubQ daily (Reduces GI side effects during GLP-1 titration and supports gut healing.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing protocols.

Bloodwork: HbA1c, fasting glucose, lipids, liver enzymes, Free T, E2 every 6-8 weeks. Body composition monthly.

Notes: Minimum 1g protein per lb body weight. Resistance training essential — GLP-1 without training causes significant muscle loss in women. Monitor hair loss — GLP-1 agents can cause telogen effluvium in women.

entries.title: Female Thyroid Optimization
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · Ongoing
entries.text:
Female Thyroid Optimization — Intermediate, Ongoing

Women are 5-8x more likely than men to develop thyroid dysfunction. This protocol addresses the most common female thyroid presentation.

Compounds:
• Levothyroxine (T4): Start 25-50mcg/day — Daily oral — 30-60 min before food or coffee (Start very low in women — they are more sensitive to thyroid hormones. Titrate by 12.5-25mcg every 6-8 weeks.)
• Liothyronine (T3): Add 5mcg/day if Free T3 remains low — Split dose AM and noon (Only add T3 if symptomatic despite adequate Free T4 and normal TSH. Many women are poor T4-to-T3 converters.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing thyroid replacement.

Bloodwork: Free T4, Free T3, TSH, Reverse T3, TPO antibodies baseline. Recheck every 6-8 weeks when adjusting. Many women have Hashimoto's (autoimmune thyroiditis) — TPO antibodies confirm this.

Notes: Hashimoto's thyroiditis is the most common thyroid condition in women — autoimmune, requires long-term management. Gluten and dairy elimination reduces TPO antibodies in some patients. Selenium 200mcg/day supports thyroid conversion. Never dose by TSH alone — target Free T3 in upper third of range for symptom relief.

entries.title: Perimenopause Management
entries.subtitle: Intermediate · Ongoing
entries.text:
Perimenopause Management — Intermediate, Ongoing

Perimenopause (typically 40-55) involves erratic hormone fluctuations before menopause. This protocol stabilizes hormones, reduces symptoms, and protects long-term health.

Compounds:
• Progesterone (bioidentical): 100-200mg — Oral at bedtime — continuously or days 14-28 of cycle (First-line intervention for perimenopause. Reduces hot flashes, improves sleep, stabilizes mood.)
• Estradiol (bioidentical): 0.5-1mg/day — Topical daily (Add if hot flashes and vasomotor symptoms persist despite progesterone. Start low.)
• Testosterone Cypionate: 5-15mg/week — Weekly SubQ (Libido, energy, and brain fog — commonly affected in perimenopause.)
• DHEA: 10-25mg/day — Daily oral AM (Adrenal support — DHEA declines significantly in perimenopause.)

PCT: N/A — ongoing hormone support.

Bloodwork: E2, Progesterone, Free T, SHBG, FSH, LH, DHEA-S every 6-8 weeks initially. Annual lipid panel, bone density (DEXA) every 2 years.

Notes: The window of opportunity for hormone therapy is the first 10 years of menopause for cardiovascular protection. Earlier intervention produces better long-term outcomes. Lifestyle fundamentals are essential: weight-bearing exercise (bone density), adequate protein, sleep optimization.

entries.title: Female Peptide Protocol
entries.subtitle: Beginner · 8-12 weeks
entries.text:
Female Peptide Protocol — Beginner, 8-12 weeks

Peptide protocol designed specifically for women's primary concerns: skin, hair, body composition, recovery, and hormonal balance.

Compounds:
• BPC-157: 250mcg/day — SubQ daily or orally for gut health (Tissue repair, gut healing, anti-inflammatory. Excellent for women with GI issues common alongside hormone imbalances.)
• GHK-Cu: Apply topically 2x/day — Face, neck, and hands — morning and evening (Collagen stimulation, skin tightening, wound healing. One of the best skin peptides available.)
• Collagen Peptides: 15g/day — Daily oral — mix in coffee or smoothie (Skin elasticity, joint health, hair strength. Take with Vitamin C for optimal synthesis.)
• CJC-1295: 200mcg — Before bed SubQ fasted (GH optimization for body composition, skin quality, and recovery. Female dose same as male.)
• Ipamorelin: 200mcg — Before bed with CJC-1295 (Selective GHRP — minimal cortisol or prolactin effects. Safe for women.)

PCT: No PCT needed — no hormonal suppression.

Bloodwork: No specific labs required. Optional: IGF-1 at baseline and 3 months if using GH secretagogues. General health panel.

Notes: Women often respond very well to GH secretagogues for skin quality and body composition. GHK-Cu is particularly valuable for female skin health. Collagen synthesis declines rapidly after menopause — supplementation becomes even more important.
